eugeniosegala/mako.name: MAKO Decky v5.0.0
eugeniosegala/mako.body:
> Looking for the standalone Vulkan layer? See [MAKO Renderer v5.0.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/render-v5.0.0). ## What's new in MAKO Decky v5.0.0

### Release codename: Phoenix > _“Where the phoenix lit the drowned stones, the mako found a way through.”_ > > **Mira Valen, _Charts of the Ember Tide_** --- Phoenix brings bundled MAKO FG to MAKO Decky through the matching Renderer: open-weight Frame Generation for SteamOS and Linux. At 3×, shared motion work can turn 30 FPS into 90 FPS when the game and GPU sustain it; 2×, 4× and other output schedules are also supported. Free for non-commercial use, with no Lossless Scaling required. See the [model card](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/engine/docs/mako-fg/MODEL_CARD.md) for design, benchmarks and limitations, or download the model and runtime from [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/eugeniosegala/MAKO-FG). - **MAKO FG:** V1.24 supports Fixed and Adaptive Frame Generation, SDR, HDR and Flow Scale, including self-contained AppImages. It is the default for profiles without a saved model, including profiles from earlier releases. Developed by Eugenio Segala. See the [setup guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/engine/docs/MAKO-FG.md). - **Pick a Frame Generation model:** Choose **MAKO FG**, **LSFG Quality** or **LSFG Performance** per profile and power mode. Switching between MAKO FG and LSFG needs a restart; LSFG Quality and Performance switch live. LSFG and LS1 still require your own Lossless Scaling installation. - **Clearer model availability:** Unavailable Lossless Scaling choices are grayed out; MAKO FG and MAKO Scaler stay usable. Failed LSFG starts fall back to MAKO FG without changing the saved choice. A missing DLL keeps that choice with a warning; the editor changes it only when a present DLL fails validation. Live Status shows the running model. - **MAKO FG performance controls:** Flow Scale trades motion detail for GPU cost. Ultra Performance uses 60% Flow Scale and MAKO Scaler when Scaling is on. Supports frames up to 8,294,400 pixels (the area of 3840×2160) and 8192 pixels per side; the analysis grid may be capped at higher resolutions. - **MAKO FG Mode:** Quality, Balanced, Performance and Extra Performance switch live and control how often motion is fully estimated at 2× and 3×. Balanced and Performance correct motion between full estimates; Extra Performance uses cheaper reuse when frames arrive evenly and correction otherwise. Start with Balanced; try Quality for artifacts in fast motion. At 4× and above, every pair gets a full estimate. Ultra Performance uses at least Performance. - **MAKO Scaler by default:** Profiles without a saved scaling method use MAKO Scaler; existing choices stay. The Renderer improves eligible scaling and HDR bridge paths. - **Capture frames for comparison:** Arm burst or rolling capture, then press L3 + R3 to save real frames locally. Rolling mode buffers recent frames until saved; burst pauses Frame Generation. The game also receives the button press. See [recording setup and limits](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/engine/docs/MAKO-FG.md#record-test-frames). - **Mailbox Presentation:** Optional compatibility setting for FIFO hangs or failures, off by default. Requires a restart. Where supported, newer frames replace queued ones, which may reduce smoothness. - **MangoHud real FPS:** **Count Real Frames Only** excludes generated frames from MangoHud's FPS counter. Requires a restart and host-installed MangoHud; cannot run alongside MAKO Shaders. - **Adaptive and bridge pacing:** Skips recovery probes that cannot succeed, handles Gamescope timing drift, and restores normal Adaptive pacing within seconds when a game's clock outpaces the display at the chosen multiplier. - **OpenGL games through Zink:** Fixes swapchain failures and uneven pacing after loading screens. With Base FPS Cap off and a known Gamescope refresh, Fixed mode paces eligible Zink games at refresh divided by the multiplier; Dynamic Cadence Recovery keeps that cap off. Workarounds also address colour speckles and tearing. See [compatibility settings and limits](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md#compatibility-and-external-tools). - **Even pacing on the desktop:** Outside Gamescope, generated frames are spaced evenly when total output is below display refresh, helping capped games and low-FPS video at some added latency. Game Mode is unchanged. - **Non-Steam games and AppImages:** Fixes Frame Generation under Steam's older Vulkan loader and shader pre-caching layer, plus related X11 window crashes. - **Proton 8 and 9 offscreen windows:** Applies Wine's workaround on the first enabled launch, fixing offscreen Frame Generation in games such as Half-Life 2. If video or UI displays incorrectly, add `WINE_DISABLE_VK_CHILD_WINDOW_RENDERING_HACK=0` before `mako-run`. Other Proton versions may use different paths; see [setup and limits](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md#proton-offscreen-windows). - **MAKO FG in games with large per-thread data:** Fixes MAKO FG startup in games with large thread-local allocations, including some native ports. ## 🎮 In-game considerations > [!TIP] > **Try V-Sync on and off.** The smoother choice depends on the game, FPS cap, VRR, and compositor. Compare Fixed, Adaptive, and scaling-only modes one at a time. If a feature does not work, try Fullscreen, Borderless Fullscreen, and Windowed. For Scaling, test in-game resolutions and check that Live Status shows Input smaller than Display. - **Adaptive target:** Adaptive aims for an average frame rate; it cannot lower a game’s native rate or exceed available GPU and compositor capacity. - **Quality and latency:** Higher multipliers and lower real-frame rates can increase ghosting and latency. Smooth Cadence may trade responsiveness for steadier motion. See the [Configuration guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/CONFIGURATION.md) and [Troubleshooting guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for complete behaviour and per-game controls. > [!IMPORTANT] > MAKO does not contain or distribute Lossless Scaling, `Lossless.dll`, or extracted proprietary model payloads. Only the optional Lossless Scaling frame generation model and LS1 scaling read selected resources at runtime from a lawful, user-supplied Lossless Scaling installation. MAKO FG, the open MAKO Scaler, and bundled shaders do not require it. MAKO does not alter the user’s DLL file, and translated resources remain process-local. Users are responsible for complying with the terms applicable to their copy. > ⚠️ **Required MAKO Renderer update:** Installing the ZIP updates MAKO Decky, but does **not** replace the shared native Renderer. Open the plugin and select **Install MAKO Renderer** afterwards. ## Installation New to Decky or installing MAKO Decky for the first time? See the [full install and use guide](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO#install-and-use) for Decky Loader setup and prerequisites. 1. Download `MAKO-Decky-v5.0.0.zip` below. 2. On SteamOS, open Decky Loader's settings and enable **Developer Mode**. 3. Choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the downloaded ZIP. 4. In MAKO Decky, select **Install MAKO Renderer**. For native Steam/Proton games, add `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run %command%` to the game’s Steam launch options. **Third-party launcher setup:** Follow the [quick guides for Heroic, Lutris, EmuDeck, and other Flatpak apps](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/blob/main/plugin/docs/LAUNCHERS.md). ## Updating an existing MAKO Decky installation 1. Quit any game currently using `/home/deck/.local/bin/mako-run`. 2. Uninstall **MAKO Decky**, then download the newer ZIP from [version 5.0.0](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/releases/tag/plugin-v5.0.0). 3. In Game Mode, open Decky Loader’s settings, choose **Developer** > **Install Plugin from Zip**, then select the newer ZIP. 4. Restart your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. 5. ⚠️ **Required:** Open MAKO Decky and select **Install MAKO Renderer** to install the version bundled in the new ZIP. 6. In **Flatpak Setup**, select **Update** for every prepared application’s matching runtime extension. This replaces its Flatpak layer with the engine bundled in the new ZIP while preserving its preparation and per-game Wrapper commands. Existing profiles and Steam launch options are retained. The shared native Renderer and launcher are re-created in step 5; shared Flatpak extensions are retained, then refreshed in step 6. ## Before you play - Test MAKO per game. Start with Frame Generation and Scaling disabled, then enable one path at a time before combining them. - If you use a Lossless Scaling frame generation model or LS1 scaling, confirm the detected `Lossless.dll` path before launching. Leaving it blank permits normal discovery. The open MAKO Scaler does not need it. - Do not combine `mako-run` with another frame-generation or scaling Vulkan wrapper for the same game. ## Bundled MAKO Renderer `5.0.0` - Includes checksum-verified `MAKO-Renderer-v5.0.0-linux.tar.xz`. - Corresponding MAKO Decky source: [`plugin-v5.0.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/plugin-v5.0.0). - Corresponding MAKO Renderer source: [`render-v5.0.0`](https://github.com/eugeniosegala/MAKO/tree/render-v5.0.0), pinned by commit and checksum in the ZIP metadata.

xxjsonderuloxx/decky-lsfg-vk.name: v0.14.1 The LSFG-VK 2.0.0 Update
xxjsonderuloxx/decky-lsfg-vk.body:
This release is a ground-up rewrite of Decky LSFG-VK, focused on better alignment and integration with [LSFG-VK 2.0.0](https://lsfg-vk.dev/).

> This release changes how per-game profiles are created and managed. Existing v1 profiles are not compatible with this release and will need to be recreated.



**New Layout and Automatic Organization**

- Separate tabs for Steam Games, Non-Steam Games, Flatpaks, Settings, Config File (optional debug)
- Collapsible lists that automatically organize by LSFG-VK enabled games and not-yet enabled
- No more copy-pasting launch commands for each game!
-  Enabling a Steam or Non-Steam game will automatically configures its steam launch options while preserving existing launch arguments.
- Streamlined flatpack integration and cleanup, does not require any manual launcher pastes in `target` section.
- Enable All and Remove All actions for each category
- Steam Deck "Game Mode" specific workarounds section better organized and managed in…

mubaraknumann/unifideck.name: UNIFIDECK v0.8.0
mubaraknumann/unifideck.body: # UNIFIDECK v0.8.0 **Added support for Xbox PC game downloads, fully native Steam game details layout, and integrated achievement and unlock popups** ## New Features - **Added Xbox PC games (experimental).** Install and play the PC games you own on Xbox or through PC Game Pass, with achievements, offline play and cloud saves. You can turn it on and sign in from Unifideck's settings. Thanks massively to [Xodus](https://github.com/xodus-gaming/xodus) and [Nexus Launcher](https://github.com/domsvoboda/nexus-launcher) projects. - **UI Update** Game pages now use Steam's own layout and UI, including the download bar, cloud play and achievements. - **Added** Steam-style achievement popups for Epic, GOG and Xbox games. GOG achievements are tracked faster with Comet v0.4.1 bump. - **Added** a version picker for Battle.net games with more than one edition installed on the same shortcut. - **Changed** Xbox Cloud Gaming to play streams in Unifideck's own player instead of via Edge. The Microsoft Edge Flatpak is now replaced by a built-in browser. - **Added** Xbox Cloud Gaming for accounts without Game Pass. Free-to-play streams such as Fortnite now sync. - **Added** cloud saves for native Linux GOG games. - **Added** a prompt to claim an itch.io bundle game before installing it, with a button that opens the claim page. - **Added** Steam review scores and tags to game pages. - **Improved** download time estimates so they no longer jump around as often with unstable speeds. ## Major Issues Fixed - **Fixed** sync replacing the names of games you renamed in Steam. - **Fixed** TabMaster tabs built from Unifideck collections breaking after a sync. - **Fixed** the sync progress bar freezing just before the end of a sync. - **Fixed** missing descriptions and publishers on some game pages. - **Fixed** every game crashing when GE-Proton's files were damaged after install. Unifideck now checks and repairs them automatically. - **Fixed** large itch.io libraries timing out during sync, and itch.io sign-ins whose API key cannot read the library. - **Fixed** native Linux GOG games always showing an update, and updates installing the Windows version. - **Fixed** GameVault downloads failing with "That compression method is not supported". - **Fixed** GameVault games with a native Linux build installing without anything to launch. Thanks @kergoth - **Fixed** the Steam Store banner saying you own every Battle.net game, such as Overwatch 2. Thanks @kmturley - **Fixed** the store switcher on a game page showing outdated stores after a sync, and "Group duplicates" occasionally showing the wrong tiles. Thanks @kmturley - **Fixed** itch.io installs failing at the end when your Games folder is a link to an SD card. Thanks @kmturley - **Improved** DirectX 12 games by keeping their shader cache between launches. - **Improved** security: Xbox sign-in now verifies Microsoft's certificates, and itch.io browser games run in their own browser profile, separate from your store sign-ins. Thanks @kmturley **Notes** - If you are already logged in to Microsoft, you might be logged out once you enable experimental Xbox PC. Also, you will need to login twice in the same window. - Warcraft III: Reforged now needs GE-Proton11-7 or newer to sign in. Unifideck tells you if your selected Proton is too old. Thanks @kmturley - Paid itch.io browser games ask you to sign in to itch.io once more, inside the game window. - For any issues with the plugin, open Unifideck QAM Settings then Capture Logs and share them on Discord or on your Github issue. Special thanks to @kmturley and @kergoth for their contributions to this release, and to everyone on Discord who helped with beta testing, specifically @opsidao, @tall_dumb_guy, @kev.benjam, @reactivefuture. Couldn't have done it without you! Join our [Discord](https://discord.gg/s9KVK2jRnp)! If you like our work, please support the project - https://ko-fi.com/mubaraknumann

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.40
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Kingdom Come: Deliverance II is now supported

Kingdom Come: Deliverance II is out of "under construction". It was tested on a Legion Go 2 with the 12 most downloaded mods and the 3 most downloaded collections (QoL & Extras, Henry From Skalitz, and Kingdom Come 2: Refined Experience). Each one was installed through the plugin from a clean game, loaded with no mod errors, and played from a save in Trosky.

Some mods were checked in game, not just loaded: Unlimited Saving II saves with F5, More Carry Weight raises the carry limit, and the Letters From Theresa quest starts on its own.

What the plugin handles for you:

- Mods go into the folder the game loads them from, and mods that update another mod lay over it as they do on Windows.
- LuaDB, the script library some mods need, is installed with any collection that needs it, along with the launch option that loads it under Proton.
- Mods that change game settings are combined into one settings file instead of replacing each other.
- A mod's "required mods" can be installed from its page in one go.

Smaller fixes:

- A collection's installed count now includes its optional mods.

Unofficial and in beta: a community-built plugin, not an official Nexus Mods product. Downloading through the plugin needs a Nexus Mods Premium account.

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.37
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor is supported, and Shadow of War is on the way

**Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor** \* is now supported, contributed by zomars (#48). Mods that replace the game's own files, loader dlls and `.arch05` archives all install from Gaming Mode:

- Files a mod replaces are backed up first, and come back when the mod is uninstalled or switched off. Two mods replacing the same file never cost you the original.
- Archive mods are registered in the game's archive list on install and taken out again on uninstall or switch-off.
- Mods that load through a proxy dll get the Proton launch option they need set for you, added to whatever launch options you already have.

**Middle-earth: Shadow of War** (on the roadmap, not yet supported) has its groundwork in, also from zomars (#47): the DLL Loader and Packet Loader as Step 1, with the game file the loader overwrites backed up and restored on reset, and the loader's console hidden so the game shows in Gaming Mode.…

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.34
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## See more from a mod's author, and mods that come back on their own

**Tap a mod's author to see their other mods** (#46). On a mod page the author's name is now a button: "by Name · more from this author". It opens the store showing all of their mods for that game. To return to every mod, press B, pick "All mods" in the Filter, or use "Show all mods".

**Mods switched off for a missing file come back once it is there** (#36). If a mod was switched off because a file it needs, such as `_ResourcePack.esl`, was not installed, it used to stay off even after the file arrived. Opening My Mods now switches those mods back on as soon as everything they need is on disk. Mods you switched off yourself, or ones switched off for crashing the game, stay off.

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.21.28
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
## Search finds every mod again

Reported in issue #43. The plugin remembers mods it has seen fail on your exact game version and keeps them off the store's front page. It was also hiding them from search, so a mod could vanish even when you searched for it by name. On the reporter's Cyberpunk 2077 that was Virtual Atelier and many other popular mods.

Search now finds every mod. The front page still leaves out mods that failed on your game version.

## Switching a mod back on clears its "broken" mark

If the plugin marked a mod as broken and you switched it back on, the mark stayed until the next game update, even through a reset, so a mod you were happily using stayed hidden from the store. Switching a mod back on now clears the mark. If the mod really is broken, the plugin will notice again the next time you play.

## Problem reports say what kind of trouble

"Report a problem" now says how many marked mods are broken and how many just need an update, rather than one number for…

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.3.0
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
**Script extenders now install the build that matches your game.** If you deliberately downgraded Skyrim or Fallout 4, Step 1 installs the SKSE or F4SE built for your exact game version instead of the newest one, read from the game's own executable.

**Script extenders now appear in the Updates tab.** They never did before - the mod everything else depends on was the one thing the plugin never checked. It also tells you when your game needs an *older* build than you have, which is the normal case after a downgrade.

**And when no build exists for your game at all, it says so.** Bethesda's 27 August Skyrim patch (1.7.104) is newer than any published SKSE, so mods cannot load on it yet. The plugin now tells you that plainly rather than leaving you to discover it from the game's own error box.

**Mods with per-version files pick the right one.** Where a mod publishes separate files per game version - Engine Fixes, Address Library and friends - the file naming your version is now the…

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.2.3
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
**Script extenders now match your game's version.** If you deliberately downgraded Skyrim (or Fallout 4) to protect your mod list, Step 1 now installs the SKSE or F4SE build made for the exact game binary you have, read from the game's own exe, instead of the newest build that only works on the latest patch. The toast tells you which build it picked. (Thanks to everyone who reported this.)

**Adult content now works outside the UK.** Age verification is a UK legal requirement and the verification flow only exists there, but the plugin was demanding it from every country. It now works the way the website does: your account's adult content preference is enough everywhere, and verification is additionally required only where the law says so. Nothing changes for UK users. (Thanks to the reporter from the Netherlands.)

redranger14/decky-nexus.name: v1.2.2
redranger14/decky-nexus.body:
**Games on SD cards and second drives are now found.** The plugin searches every Steam library, not just the internal one, and reads each game's Proton prefix from the library that actually holds it. If your game showed "not found" because it lives on a microSD card, this release is the fix. (Thanks to the player who reported Witcher 3 on a microSD.)

**Battlefront II mods that replace character models now render correctly.** Three bugs in our mod compiler were found by comparing its output byte-for-byte against Frosty's on the same mod, and all three are fixed in compiler build 2. The plugin upgrades your installed compiler automatically the next time you install or toggle a mod. Battle Damaged Darth Vader, The Mandalorian and friends now look like they should instead of a mass of shards.

**Multi-part Battlefront II mods install whole.** Mods that ship as a set (The Mandalorian's base, text and weapon parts) install together without asking; mods that offer alternatives show a…

Updates the Decky controls for Borderless Gaming 2.0.10.

- Keep controls stable while changing presets and reconnecting to game sessions.
- Show preparation progress and prevent older responses from reverting recent changes.
- Support conditional effect parameters, including the controls for Fixed and Adaptive frame generation.
- Use BGFX control protocol v5. Update Borderless Gaming and the plugin together.

Install `BGFX.zip` through Decky's plugin installer. `SHA256SUMS` contains the archive checksum.

TypeScript checks, frontend tests, Python tests and archive validation passed for this release.

andrewmd5/decky-bgfx.name: v1.3.2
andrewmd5/decky-bgfx.body:
Improved connection reliability with Borderless Gaming v2.0.4.

- Finds BGFX through the same shared session registry as the Linux desktop app, including games running inside Steam's container.
- Selects the renderer currently presenting frames when a game creates or replaces its rendering surface.
- Shows whether effects are active, waiting for frames, or reconnecting instead of assuming that an available process means effects are running.

Install Borderless Gaming v2.0.4 and restart the game to use the updated engine and in-game activity indicator.

andrewmd5/decky-bgfx.name: v1.1.1
andrewmd5/decky-bgfx.body:
Requires **Borderless Gaming 1.4.15 or newer**. No app update is needed if you already have 1.4.15 or 1.4.16.

- All effect controls now appear directly in the Quick Access flyout, including scaling, toggles, and sliders.
- Removed the persistent "Waiting for frame generation" label. Technical state remains available in Diagnostics.
- Stabilized FPS columns and status-message space so updates do not move the controls around.
- Kept controls focused during edits and made rapid slider changes responsive without queuing outdated values.
- Fixed initial preset selection when no preset is active.

Install `BGFX.zip` through Decky's **Install Plugin from ZIP** option.

justinca92/spindeck.name: Spindeck 1.4.1
justinca92/spindeck.body:
### What's new in 1.4.1

**New**
- ⬆️ **Update right from the panel.** Press **Check for updates** at the bottom of the Spindeck panel; if there's a newer version, **Update to vX** installs it in place after Decky asks you to confirm once. Your settings are kept. Spindeck only contacts GitHub when you press the button. (This works from 1.4.1 on, so this one update still goes through the zip below.)
- 🖼️ **Hero art v1.3.0 style** (side layout): a new switch in Display brings back the 1.3.0 look of the hero art: in the middle of the screen, with 1.3.0's blurred background and fades (without the thin white line some art showed above and below it in 1.3.0). Off by default.

**Changed**
- 🎡 **Bottom layout: your custom text moves up to just below the hero art**, on the side away from the wheel, with the Ⓨ "Today's game?" button right under it.

**Fixed**
- 🧩 **Home screen error with SteamGridDB.** With SteamGridDB's **Matching Recents Capsule** option on, the home screen could show an error page ("An error occurred while rendering this content", or Steam's own error screen) instead of the wheel, depending on which plugin loaded first. michpalm/game-glance.name: 4.0.0-rc.4
michpalm/game-glance.body:
# Game Glance 4.0.0-rc.4

## Added since 4.0.0-rc.3

This candidate contains 60 commits made since the previous prerelease on 10 November.

### New pages

- **Library.** A hero, grouped game facts, L1/R1 tabs, and dense cover rows. It also introduces the shared page kit used by the new pages. The Library page remains marked **in progress** and unavailable through the settings toggle for this prerelease.
- **Media.** A gallery grouped by day, viewer and full screen, upload and delete actions, and a **Games** tab that groups local screenshots and recordings by game. Screenshot notifications show the captured shot and open it in Media.
- **Settings home.** A grouped list with collapsible groups, live panels, and a direct jump into Steam’s corresponding page.
- **Downloads.** The active download’s art and logo, with disk and peak-speed graphs.
- **Wi-Fi and Storage.** Game Glance versions of Steam’s Wi-Fi and Storage screens.

### Home and game pages

- **All installed games row.** Steam and non-Steam installed games together in one Home row, contributed by [@AlexFigas](https://github.com/AlexFigas) in #90.
- **Game information.** Choose three stats and a featured card: ProtonDB, achievements, play time, or HowLongToBeat.
- **Title size and accent colour.** Choose Small, Medium, or Large titles; use a per-game accent or pick your own.
- **Recommended and Friends.** Steam’s Personal Calendar can be the Recommended row with trailers; Friends uses game-first cards and the hero is frosted beneath the feed.
- **Theme music and return.** NonSteamLaunchers theme music has a single ♪ button, and returning from a game page to Home glides smoothly.
- **Layout scale.** Game Glance renders at 88% on TV and 94% on handheld.

### In-game menu

- **Resume.** The game’s art resumes the game, without the white square.
- **Achievements.** A Game Glance Achievements page with Achievement Sets, pins, and sorting.
- **Power and Navigate.** Power returns to Game Glance with confirmation dialogs in its visual style; Navigate follows its new order.
- **Frost.** Support for SDR games on an HDR display. The true-HDR path is included but remains untested.
- **Pills, pickers, and status.** Player-count pills, status and audio pickers, and a controller battery indicator that no longer blinks.

### Menus and input

- **Context menus.** Steam context menus use Game Glance’s frosted style; the menu dims the screen the same way, and the game menu has improved navigation.
- **Screensaver wake.** B is consumed while waking the screensaver, avoiding Steam’s menu opening as part of the same press. Two repeat checks on the PlayStation build returned without opening it.

## Install or roll back

After this prerelease is published, open **Game Glance → General → Choose version**, turn on **Show prereleases**, select **4.0.0-rc.4**, and confirm through Decky. You can also install the attached `game-glance.zip` through Decky's **Install plugin from ZIP**. To return to stable, choose a stable version from the same picker.

For the original 4.0 preview, see [4.0.0-rc.1](https://github.com/michpalm/game-glance/releases/tag/v4.0.0-rc.1). The existing [screenshot issue](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/gamescope/issues/2416) still applies: close the in-game Game Glance menu before taking a Steam screenshot when compositor frost is active.

Please share how the new pages, Media collections, context menus, and controller navigation feel on your device, and report any unexpected focus or return behavior.

## Near-instant popups and TV placement

Popups now appear about a second after an achievement is earned, instead of 10-15 seconds later.

### What changed since v1.6.2
- **Popups no longer wait on slow downloads.** The icon, unlock percentage, description and game art now load at the same time, and the popup waits for them at most 1 second. ![PS5 Dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard/main/docs/screenshots/home.jpg)

## What's new in 1.10.0

### 🌍 The plugin speaks your language
PS5 Dashboard now follows the language you picked in Steam on each device, in **14 languages**:

English · Português · Español · Français · Deutsch · Italiano · Polski · Русский · Українська · Türkçe · 日本語 · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 繁體中文

- Any other Steam language gets **English**, never the operating system's language.
- Plurals follow each language's rules ("2 дня" / "5 дней", "2 miesiące" / "5 miesięcy"…).
- Translations live in [`src/locales/`](https://github.com/kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard/tree/main/src/locales), one file per language. Spotted something off in your language? Issues and pull requests are welcome!

### 🟦 Rounded corners actually work now
Steam registers a CSS property called `--r` as an angle, and the plugin used that same name for its corner radius, so Steam threw the value away and every tile, card and button came out square. The **Tile corner radius** setting (0–24 px) now rounds the game covers on the home row, the lower rows, the Game Library, the info cards and the buttons.

### ✨ The glass aura follows the corners
The animated edge around the focused game curves with the tile, and its light now shades through grey and the accent blue as well as white and translucent black.

Also includes everything from **1.9.0** (Hide bottom bar setting, header spacing). See the [changelog](https://github.com/kromossomom-debug/decky-ps5-dashboard/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Install

1. Download **`ps5-dashboard.zip`** below.
2. In Game Mode: **Quick Access (`…`) → Decky → ⚙ Settings → General**, turn on **Developer mode**.
3. **Developer → Install plugin from ZIP**, pick `ps5-dashboard.zip`.

Updating? Install the new ZIP the same way; your settings are kept. The plugin panel should then show **v1.10.0** at the bottom. If it still shows an older version, restart Steam.

- **Juegos que se cierran con mods:** En los juegos con antitrampas que cierran al detectar programas no firmados, Panel de Control recomienda ahora una versión que el juego acepta. Si un escalador hace que un juego se cierre nada más arrancar, la próxima vez te recomienda otro. Puedes seguir instalando el que quieras.
- **FSR 4 con las versiones nuevas de OptiScaler:** Con OptiScaler 0.9.5 o posterior, FSR 4 podía acabar funcionando como FSR 3 sin avisar. Ya se configura bien.
- **Gráficas RX 9060 y RX 9070 junto a una gráfica integrada:** Panel de Control ya reconoce la gráfica dedicada y ofrece FSR 4 en su versión completa.
- **FSR 4.1.2 Lite al día:** Las DLL de FSR 4.1.2 Lite se actualizan a su última versión. En gráficas dedicadas RX 7000 hay dos variantes: una idéntica a la de AMD y otra más rápida que no da exactamente la misma imagen.
- **Atajos de otras tiendas:** Los juegos de otras tiendas en los que no se puede instalar un escalador ya aparecen en la lista con el motivo, en vez de desaparecer. Los atajos con algún dato repetido ya no impiden encontrar el resto.
- **God of War Ragnarök:** Panel de Control ya no recomienda HelixSR en este juego, porque hacía desaparecer FSR de su menú de gráficos.
- **Etiqueta del escalador en más temas:** Los temas que dibujan las portadas a su manera ya pueden mostrar qué escalador tiene cada juego.
- **Lossless Scaling en consolas ARM:** Si ya tienes instalada la versión para ARM, Panel de Control la usa y configura cada juego, en vez de descargar una que no funciona ahí.

### What's new

- **FSR 4 in Diablo IV:** If your graphics card supports it, Panel de Control uses Proton's FSR 4, which doesn't touch the game's files. Otherwise it installs a version of OptiScaler the game accepts, because with other versions it closed a few minutes into a match.
- **Games that close with mods:** In games with anti-cheat that close when they spot unsigned software, Panel de Control now recommends a version the game accepts. If an upscaler makes a game close right after it starts, it recommends a different one next time. You can still install whichever you want.
- **FSR 4 with newer OptiScaler versions:** With OptiScaler 0.9.5 or later, FSR 4 could quietly end up running as FSR 3. It's now set up correctly.
- **RX 9060 and RX 9070 cards next to integrated graphics:** Panel de Control now recognises the dedicated card and offers the full version of FSR 4.
- **FSR 4.1.2 Lite up to date:** The FSR 4.1.2 Lite DLLs are updated to their latest version. Dedicated RX 7000 cards get two variants: one identical to AMD's and a faster one that doesn't give exactly the same image.
- **Shortcuts from other stores:** Games from other stores where an upscaler can't be installed now show up in the list with the reason instead of disappearing. Shortcuts with a repeated field no longer stop the rest from being found.
- **God of War Ragnarök:** Panel de Control no longer recommends HelixSR in this game, because it made FSR disappear from its graphics menu.
- **Upscaler label in more themes:** Themes that draw covers their own way can now show which upscaler each game has.
- **Lossless Scaling on ARM consoles:** If you already have the ARM version installed, Panel de Control uses it and sets up each game, instead of downloading one that doesn't work there.

### Novità

- **FSR 4 in Diablo IV:** Se la tua scheda video lo supporta, Panel de Control usa l'FSR 4 di Proton, che non tocca i file del gioco. Altrimenti installa una versione di OptiScaler che il gioco accetta, perché con le altre si chiudeva dopo pochi minuti di partita.
- **Giochi che si chiudono con le mod:** Nei giochi con anticheat che si chiudono quando trovano programmi non firmati, Panel de Control ora consiglia una versione che il gioco accetta. Se un upscaler fa chiudere un gioco appena avviato, la volta dopo te ne consiglia un altro. Puoi comunque installare quello che vuoi.
- **FSR 4 con le versioni nuove di OptiScaler:** Con OptiScaler 0.9.5 o successivo, FSR 4 poteva finire a funzionare come FSR 3 senza avvisare. Ora viene configurato bene.
- **Schede RX 9060 e RX 9070 insieme a una grafica integrata:** Panel de Control ora riconosce la scheda dedicata e offre FSR 4 nella versione completa.
- **FSR 4.1.2 Lite aggiornato:** Le DLL di FSR 4.1.2 Lite passano all'ultima versione. Sulle schede dedicate RX 7000 ci sono due varianti: una identica a quella di AMD e una più veloce che non dà esattamente la stessa immagine.
- **Scorciatoie di altri store:** I giochi di altri store dove non si può installare un upscaler ora compaiono nella lista con il motivo, invece di sparire. Le scorciatoie con un dato ripetuto non impediscono più di trovare le altre.
- **God of War Ragnarök:** Panel de Control non consiglia più HelixSR in questo gioco, perché faceva sparire FSR dal suo menu grafico.
- **Etichetta dell'upscaler in più temi:** I temi che disegnano le copertine a modo loro ora possono mostrare quale upscaler ha ogni gioco.
- **Lossless Scaling sulle console ARM:** Se hai già installato la versione per ARM, Panel de Control la usa e configura ogni gioco, invece di scaricarne una che lì non funziona.

### Neuigkeiten

- **FSR 4 in Diablo IV:** Wenn deine Grafikkarte es unterstützt, nutzt Panel de Control das FSR 4 von Proton, das die Spieldateien nicht anfasst. Sonst installiert es eine OptiScaler-Version, die das Spiel akzeptiert, denn mit anderen schloss es sich nach ein paar Minuten im Spiel.
- **Spiele, die sich bei Mods schließen:** In Spielen mit Anti-Cheat, die sich bei nicht signierter Software schließen, empfiehlt Panel de Control jetzt eine Version, die das Spiel akzeptiert. Wenn ein Upscaler ein Spiel direkt nach dem Start schließt, empfiehlt es beim nächsten Mal einen anderen. Du kannst trotzdem installieren, was du willst.
- **FSR 4 mit neueren OptiScaler-Versionen:** Mit OptiScaler 0.9.5 oder neuer konnte FSR 4 unbemerkt als FSR 3 laufen. Das wird jetzt richtig eingestellt.
- **RX 9060 und RX 9070 neben integrierter Grafik:** Panel de Control erkennt jetzt die dedizierte Karte und bietet die volle Version von FSR 4 an.
- **FSR 4.1.2 Lite aktuell:** Die DLLs von FSR 4.1.2 Lite sind auf dem neuesten Stand. Dedizierte RX-7000-Karten bekommen zwei Varianten: eine, die mit der von AMD identisch ist, und eine schnellere, die nicht ganz dasselbe Bild liefert.
- **Verknüpfungen aus anderen Stores:** Spiele aus anderen Stores, in denen sich kein Upscaler installieren lässt, erscheinen jetzt mit dem Grund in der Liste, statt zu verschwinden. Verknüpfungen mit einem doppelten Eintrag verhindern nicht mehr, dass die anderen gefunden werden.
- **God of War Ragnarök:** Panel de Control empfiehlt in diesem Spiel kein HelixSR mehr, weil damit FSR aus dem Grafikmenü verschwand.
- **Upscaler-Hinweis in mehr Themes:** Themes, die Cover auf ihre eigene Art zeichnen, können jetzt zeigen, welchen Upscaler jedes Spiel hat.
- **Lossless Scaling auf ARM-Konsolen:** Wenn du die ARM-Version schon installiert hast, nutzt Panel de Control sie und richtet jedes Spiel ein, statt eine herunterzuladen, die dort nicht läuft.

### Novidades em português (Brasil)

- **FSR 4 no Diablo IV:** Se a sua placa de vídeo suporta, o Panel de Control usa o FSR 4 do Proton, que não mexe nos arquivos do jogo. Nos outros casos, instala uma versão do OptiScaler que o jogo aceita, porque com outras ele fechava poucos minutos depois de entrar na partida.
- **Jogos que fecham com mods:** Em jogos com anticheat que fecham ao detectar programas sem assinatura, o Panel de Control agora recomenda uma versão que o jogo aceita. Se um upscaler faz um jogo fechar logo depois de abrir, na próxima vez ele recomenda outro. Você continua podendo instalar o que quiser.
- **FSR 4 com as versões novas do OptiScaler:** Com o OptiScaler 0.9.5 ou mais novo, o FSR 4 podia acabar funcionando como FSR 3 sem avisar. Agora ele é configurado direito.
- **Placas RX 9060 e RX 9070 junto com gráfico integrado:** O Panel de Control agora reconhece a placa dedicada e oferece o FSR 4 na versão completa.
- **FSR 4.1.2 Lite atualizado:** As DLLs do FSR 4.1.2 Lite foram atualizadas para a versão mais recente. Nas placas dedicadas RX 7000 há duas variantes: uma idêntica à da AMD e outra mais rápida que não dá exatamente a mesma imagem.
- **Atalhos de outras lojas:** Jogos de outras lojas em que não dá para instalar um upscaler agora aparecem na lista com o motivo, em vez de sumir. Atalhos com algum dado repetido não impedem mais que os outros sejam encontrados.
- **God of War Ragnarök:** O Panel de Control não recomenda mais o HelixSR neste jogo, porque ele fazia o FSR sumir do menu de gráficos.
- **Etiqueta do upscaler em mais temas:** Temas que desenham as capas do seu próprio jeito agora podem mostrar qual upscaler cada jogo tem.
- **Lossless Scaling em consoles ARM:** Se você já tem a versão para ARM instalada, o Panel de Control usa ela e configura cada jogo, em vez de baixar uma que não funciona ali.

### Nouveautés

- **FSR 4 dans Diablo IV :** Si votre carte graphique le permet, Panel de Control utilise le FSR 4 de Proton, qui ne touche pas aux fichiers du jeu. Sinon, il installe une version d'OptiScaler que le jeu accepte, car avec les autres il se fermait au bout de quelques minutes de partie.
- **Jeux qui se ferment avec des mods :** Dans les jeux avec anti-triche qui se ferment quand ils repèrent un programme non signé, Panel de Control recommande maintenant une version que le jeu accepte. Si un upscaler fait fermer un jeu juste après son lancement, il en recommande un autre la fois suivante. Vous pouvez toujours installer celui que vous voulez.
- **FSR 4 avec les nouvelles versions d'OptiScaler :** Avec OptiScaler 0.9.5 ou plus récent, FSR 4 pouvait finir par tourner comme FSR 3 sans prévenir. Il est maintenant bien configuré.
- **Cartes RX 9060 et RX 9070 avec une puce graphique intégrée :** Panel de Control reconnaît maintenant la carte dédiée et propose FSR 4 dans sa version complète.
- **FSR 4.1.2 Lite à jour :** Les DLL de FSR 4.1.2 Lite passent à leur dernière version. Les cartes dédiées RX 7000 ont deux variantes : une identique à celle d'AMD et une plus rapide qui ne donne pas exactement la même image.
- **Raccourcis d'autres boutiques :** Les jeux d'autres boutiques où l'on ne peut pas installer d'upscaler apparaissent maintenant dans la liste avec la raison, au lieu de disparaître. Les raccourcis avec une donnée en double n'empêchent plus de trouver les autres.
- **God of War Ragnarök :** Panel de Control ne recommande plus HelixSR dans ce jeu, car il faisait disparaître FSR de son menu graphique.
- **Étiquette de l'upscaler dans plus de thèmes :** Les thèmes qui dessinent les jaquettes à leur façon peuvent maintenant afficher l'upscaler de chaque jeu.
- **Lossless Scaling sur les consoles ARM :** Si vous avez déjà installé la version pour ARM, Panel de Control l'utilise et configure chaque jeu, au lieu d'en télécharger une qui n'y fonctionne pas.

gillrajvir950-wq/deckyshare.name: DeckyShare v1.3.0

- Decky-only endpoints accept local requests only; uploads are verified and written to temporary files first.

### Connecting
- Phone: scan the QR code. Computer: open the short address (for example `192.168.8.131:8787`) and type the code shown on the Deck.

- Maximum Speed (single stream) plus resumable Turbo (3 parallel streams) and Fast modes, with pause, resume and cancel.

- Cancel transfers from the Deck panel as well as from the phone/computer.
- Re-sending a file you deleted keeps its original name (no more "name (1)").

brenticusmaximus/themedeck.name: ThemeDeck v4.0.0
brenticusmaximus/themedeck.body:
ThemeDeck 4.0 adds playlists for game themes, global ambient music, and Steam Store music, together with a smaller music chooser and controller-friendly playback controls.

### Playlists everywhere
- Add as many songs as you like to each game, ambient music, and store music. Adding another song keeps the existing songs.
- Reorder songs with the arrows, remove individual assignments, or clear a playlist without deleting its files.
- Songs advance in playlist order. Loop the full playlist or stop after the last song.
- Set playlist volume and skip the start of songs.

### One compact music chooser
- YouTube/yt-dlp search, preview, download, and local-file browsing are available for games, ambient music, and store music.
- YouTube search is at the top. **Download** adds the first song; **Download & Add** appends another.
- Playlist settings, local files, and song storage open on the same page, one section at a time.
- Smaller controls and scrolling file lists keep the interface compact.

### Now Playing improvements
- Previous, play/pause, and next buttons, playlist position, and time remaining.
- A flat music-settings icon above the countdown opens the matching music chooser.
- D-pad access to every card button: Up from playback controls reaches the music-settings icon, Down returns, and Left/Right moves between controls. Press A to open music selection.
- Pausing and resuming keep the card size stable.
- Improved visualizer frequency grouping, smoother response, and recovery after loops/seeks, with separate handling for silence and capture failures.

### Storage and upgrading
- Storage management recognizes all playlist members when listing files and deleting downloads.
- Existing songs, single-track assignments, and settings are preserved when upgrading.
- Download **ThemeDeck-v4.0.0.zip** below and install it through Decky Settings → Developer → Install plugin from ZIP. The source-code archives are not the install package.
- If YouTube requests sign-in or verification, use **Update YouTube support** and the optional Firefox-cookie setting as needed.

Tested directly on a Steam Deck: playlist additions, ambient/store YouTube search and preview/download, volume/start-skip/loop settings, and controller navigation. Automated playlist, YouTube audio, storage, background playback, and integration checks also passed.

Includes the YouTube support improvements from v3.1.6 and song storage management from v3.1.5. Existing music and assignments are preserved.

Fixes YouTube previews and downloads failing with **“ffprobe and ffmpeg not found.”** ThemeDeck now downloads M4A audio directly, removing the MP3 conversion step and its FFmpeg/FFprobe requirement. Existing music and assignments continue to work.

valentinebsaa/titledeck.name: TitleDeck 1.4.0 Stable 🌸
valentinebsaa/titledeck.body:
# TitleDeck 1.4.0 Stable 🌸
**Released November 7, 2026.** [Download the tested installer](https://github.com/ValentineBSAA/TitleDeck/releases/download/1.4.0/TitleDeck-1.4.0.zip) · [Release page](https://github.com/ValentineBSAA/TitleDeck/releases/tag/1.4.0) · [Screenshots](https://github.com/ValentineBSAA/TitleDeck/blob/main/docs/SCREENSHOTS.md)

### From a useful title editor to a polished library workshop
1.4.0 builds on 1.2.2 with a more refined **Full Library Manager**, improved game-art loading and focus behavior, a substantial **Typography Studio**, and clearer Steam Home compatibility controls. The basic idea remains simple: make your Steam Deck's library feel like *yours* without touching the actual game files.

### What changed since public 1.2.2
- **Full Library Manager:** artwork placeholders and transitions, Settings refinements, focus/scroll improvements and controller-oriented navigation.
- **Typography Studio:** 10 built-in font-style treatments, expanded presets and HEX/RGB color choices, hue and shade controls, optional text outlines, shadows, glow and high-contrast appearance.
- **Readability help:** light/dark illustrative previews and warnings that respect the exact color you select.
- **Steam Home:** more understandable Above Cards/Below Cards controls and saved offsets when TitleDeck controls layout.
- **Art Hero:** reads Carousel Font Height, shows a guide and makes Art Hero placement **intentionally read-only** when the theme is on.
- **Quick Access:** improved visual organization and developer branding, retaining the profile link added in 1.2.2.
- **Local data safety:** Steam/non-Steam title aliases, custom descriptions, backups, restoration and native editing shortcuts all remain.

[Before-and-after explanation](https://github.com/ValentineBSAA/TitleDeck/blob/main/docs/UPDATE_FROM_1.2.2.md) · [Full feature reference](https://github.com/ValentineBSAA/TitleDeck/blob/main/docs/FEATURES.md)

### A deliberate Art Hero limitation
Earlier 1.3.x builds experimented with updating CSS Loader's Art Hero settings. Reading could work, but cross-plugin writes did not reliably change the on-device position. Version 1.4.0 keeps Art Hero position **visible but not editable** in TitleDeck. For adjustments open CSS Loader → Art Hero → Carousel Font Height. When Art Hero is off, use TitleDeck's own placement controls.

### Verification
The maintainer reports personally testing the available 1.4.0 features on a physical Steam Deck, with this Art Hero limitation accepted. Independently run on the matching supplied source: **79 passing JavaScript and five Python tests**, version checks, syntax checks, package-integrity and 13-file installer/source parity. The published installer SHA-256 is:

`bf1b6108d0861246337915011fd1348ec51475dd042ae1d62c3226777266b588`

The GitHub-hosted screenshot ZIP was also checked against the uploaded organized archive. [Full verification record](https://github.com/ValentineBSAA/TitleDeck/blob/main/docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md)

### Known limitations
- Art Hero settings must be changed in CSS Loader, not TitleDeck.
- [Issue #8](https://github.com/ValentineBSAA/TitleDeck/issues/8): built-in Deck right-stick scrolling in Game Info descriptions remains open.
- The previously observed Quick Access focus quirk is not marked fixed.
- Importing arbitrary custom ZIP/TTF fonts is not supported.
- Theme, SteamOS and controller combinations vary.

### Thank you ❤️
Thanks to the Steam Deck community for the ideas, real-world testing, bug reports, thoughtful suggestions, downloads and encouragement. From people who inspired the first title/description editing features to those who have tried the 1.4.0 builds, your feedback helped shape this project. Thank you as well to everyone simply enjoying the plugin.

TitleDeck is community-made, free, MIT licensed, and not affiliated with Valve.

Your Titles. Your Deck!

valentinebsaa/game-theme-music.body:
🎵 Game Theme Music 4.6.7

Stability, Performance & Customization

Stable Release | November 6, 2026

Hey everyone, Valentine here!

GTM 4.6.7 is here, bringing a collection of bug fixes, performance improvements, customization options, and better integration with ResonaDeck.

This update focuses on making the features already in GTM more reliable, responsive, and enjoyable to use.

A lot of work has gone into refining how GTM interacts with Steam, Decky Loader, and other plugins. Several of these improvements also came directly from community feedback.

Thank you to everyone who has been using GTM and reporting issues!

✨ What’s New?

🎛️ Customizable Library Context Menus

You can now independently control which GTM shortcuts appear in Steam’s Library context menus.

Available options include:

* Change Music
* Change Ambient Playlist
* Change Store Playlist

Each shortcut has its own visibility toggle.

Want to keep Change Music but hide the Ambient and Store options? You can!

These settings only affect the visibility of GTM’s shortcuts. Your playlists and music features remain available.

This improvement addresses community-reported GitHub Issue #10.

🧭 Improved Quick Menu Navigation

Navigating GTM is now easier.

* Added the Browse All Pages A–Z dropdown for direct page navigation.
* Preserved LB/RB controller paging.
* Improved focus handling between sections.
* Reduced unnecessary scrolling and page movement.
* Improved Quick Menu responsiveness.

These changes are particularly useful when navigating GTM with a controller.

🛍️ Store Music Reliability

Store Music has received several important fixes.

Both Steam’s native Store and the Decky Plugin Store now have improved detection and playback handling.

Improvements include:

* More reliable Store Music startup.
* Better recognition of the Decky Plugin Store.
* Improved detection when entering and leaving Steam’s native Store.
* Reduced delays when stopping Store Music after navigating away.
* Improved recovery from stalled playback initialization.
* Better handling of changing Steam navigation states.

Store Music also respects ResonaDeck’s audio priority.

If you’re already listening to music through ResonaDeck, GTM won’t interrupt it just because you open a Store page.

These improvements were verified on a physical Steam Deck without requiring a system restart.

🌈 GTM + ResonaDeck Visualizer Integration

GTM’s shared visualizer integration has received additional improvements.

When paired with ResonaDeck 1.5.7:

* Visualizers respect the user’s ON/OFF controls.
* Saved preferences no longer act as unwanted startup activation commands.
* Visualizers remain hidden when there is no eligible music playback.
* Enabled visualizers can appear when supported music begins playing.
* Disabling visualizers does not stop music playback.
* ResonaDeck can provide music-reactive frequency information to compatible GTM visualizers.

The goal is simple: music and visualizers should work together without fighting over settings.

⚡ Performance Improvements

We’ve also reduced unnecessary background activity.

Improvements include:

* Fewer redundant playlist-state storage writes.
* More efficient Ambient and Store state synchronization.
* Reduced unnecessary Steam interface observation.
* Better cleanup of background listeners.
* Improved plugin initialization and reload handling.
* Reduced unnecessary interface work.

These changes are intended to make GTM lighter without removing existing functionality.

🔧 Preserved Features

This update retains GTM’s existing music features, including:

* Steam and non-Steam game soundtracks.
* Ambient/Home Music.
* Steam Store and Decky Plugin Store Music.
* Music playlists and crossfading.
* Custom visualizers and visualizer packs.
* Optional AI-versus-AI Arcade Spectator scenes.
* CSS Loader theme compatibility.
* Sleep and wake handling.
* ResonaDeck audio coordination.
* YT-DLP downloading functionality.

YT-DLP and its required bundled components have not been removed.

✅ Testing & Verification

GTM 4.6.7 underwent multiple rounds of development testing and physical Steam Deck verification.

Confirmed working during the maintainer’s testing:

* Independent Library context-menu visibility controls.
* Quick Menu page navigation.
* Steam Store Music startup.
* Decky Plugin Store Music startup.
* Store Music stopping after leaving Store pages.
* ResonaDeck audio priority.
* Visualizer visibility controls.
* Store Music functionality without restarting Steam after installation.

Additional automated checks covered JavaScript/Python syntax, package integrity, Store navigation behavior, and preservation of bundled downloader components.

Testing does not guarantee identical behavior across every SteamOS version, Decky Loader release, or CSS Loader theme.

📦 Installation

Download Game-Theme-Music-4.6.7.zip from the Assets section below.

Install using Decky Loader’s manual ZIP installation option.

Please download the actual plugin ZIP rather than GitHub’s automatically generated source-code archive.

Your existing GTM settings and playlists are intended to remain intact when updating normally.

A Steam Deck restart is not normally required. If older interface components remain after updating, restarting Steam may help.

❤️ Thank You!

GTM has grown considerably since its earlier releases.

Although I’m focusing more on maintenance and stability now, I’m still paying attention to feedback and improving what we’ve already built.

If you discover a reproducible problem, please open a GitHub issue and include your GTM version.

Thank you for downloading, testing, and supporting Game Theme Music.

Enjoy the music!

Valentine
Developer of Game Theme Music

valentinebsaa/resonadeck.name: ResonaDeck 1.5.7
valentinebsaa/resonadeck.body:
🎧 ResonaDeck 1.5.7

Quick Menu Performance, Stability & GTM Integration

Stable Release | November 6, 2026

Hey everyone, Valentine here!

ResonaDeck 1.5.7 is now available!

This release focuses on improving Quick Menu responsiveness, fixing interface rendering issues, reducing unnecessary background activity, and improving compatibility with Game Theme Music.

ResonaDeck has grown into a full-featured music player for Steam Deck Gaming Mode, and keeping that experience reliable is just as important as adding new functionality.

This update focuses on polishing what we already have.

✨ What’s Improved?

⚡ Faster Quick Menu Rendering

One of our biggest priorities was reducing the amount of work ResonaDeck performs when opening Quick Access.

Previously, ResonaDeck could spend unnecessary time recalculating theme colors, observing Steam interface changes, and rebuilding portions of its interface.

We’ve made several improvements:

* Reduced unnecessary theme calculations.
* Improved reuse of previously detected colors.
* Reduced redundant background monitoring.
* Improved initialization of the Quick Menu interface.
* Reduced unnecessary visual updates.
* Improved cleanup of background tasks during plugin updates.

These changes aim to make ResonaDeck feel more responsive while preserving its appearance and functionality.

🎨 Quick Menu Styling Fixes

ResonaDeck’s premium interface has also received important rendering corrections.

An earlier optimization caused some styles to load outside the plugin’s rendering environment.

This could result in oversized album artwork, overlapping labels, and incorrectly positioned controls.

The original styling behavior has been restored while retaining compatible performance improvements.

ResonaDeck continues to support:

* Artwork-inspired colors.
* Adaptive Steam/CSS Loader themes.
* Frosted-glass interface elements.
* Controller-friendly navigation.
* Full player controls.
* Album artwork and playback information.

The interface was verified again on a physical Steam Deck after these corrections.

🌈 Improved Game Theme Music Integration

ResonaDeck’s visualizer integration has received additional synchronization improvements.

When paired with Game Theme Music 4.6.7:

* Visualizer controls remain available from both plugins.
* Saved settings no longer automatically force unwanted startup activation.
* Enabled visualizers remain hidden when no eligible music is playing.
* Visualizers can become active when supported playback begins.
* Disabling visualizers does not interrupt Plex music.
* Music-reactive audio analysis and GTM communication remain supported.

The integration includes diagnostic information for audio capture and communication.

During testing, music-reactive behavior was successfully restored by refreshing the visualizer connection through the ON/OFF switch.

If visualizers appear but do not initially react to music, switching GTM Visualizers OFF and back ON in ResonaDeck can refresh the connection.

🎵 Better Background Efficiency

ResonaDeck now performs less unnecessary work while running alongside other Decky plugins.

Improvements include:

* Reduced redundant power-state polling.
* More selective theme-change monitoring.
* Better cleanup of background listeners and timers.
* Improved management of visualizer bridge resources.
* Reduced repeated interface color calculations.

The goal is to reduce unnecessary background activity while keeping music playback dependable.

🧹 Interface Cleanup

The previously introduced Cash App donation button and associated artwork have been removed.

ResonaDeck’s interface remains focused on music playback, library browsing, and player controls.

🎼 Existing Features Preserved

ResonaDeck 1.5.7 retains its existing functionality, including:

* Plex music libraries.
* Jellyfin integration.
* Audiobooks and podcasts.
* Surprise Me music discovery.
* Keep Playing and continuous queue replenishment.
* Favorites and saved listening options.
* Music crossfading.
* Long-duration track handling.
* Sleep and wake recovery.
* Full ResonaDeck Manager.
* Album artwork and playback controls.
* Music-reactive GTM integration.
* Controller-friendly navigation.

Previous improvements to multi-hour playback and crossfade countdown accuracy are also preserved.

✅ Testing & Verification

ResonaDeck 1.5.7 builds on several rounds of testing and fixes.

The following behavior has been confirmed during development and Steam Deck testing:

* Quick Menu styling displays correctly.
* Album artwork and player controls render in their intended layout.
* The player interface remains functional after the styling corrections.
* Visualizers remain hidden without eligible playback.
* Visualizers can activate during supported music playback.
* Music-reactive communication can function after refreshing the GTM visualizer connection.
* ResonaDeck playback takes priority over GTM Store Music when already playing.

Automated checks also covered JavaScript/Python syntax and ZIP integrity.

Not every Plex/Jellyfin configuration, media format, SteamOS version, or CSS Loader theme has been tested.

📦 Installation

Download ResonaDeck-1.5.7.zip from the Assets section below.

Install through Decky Loader’s manual ZIP installation option.

Use the named plugin ZIP rather than GitHub’s automatically generated source-code archive.

Existing settings, libraries, and preferences are intended to remain intact during normal updates.

A full Steam Deck restart is not normally required. If the interface retains old styling after an update, close and reopen Quick Access or restart Steam if necessary.

For the latest shared visualizer improvements, use Game Theme Music 4.6.7.

❤️ Thank You!

ResonaDeck started with a simple idea: bringing a dedicated Plex music experience directly into Steam Deck Gaming Mode.

Since then, it has grown considerably, with more playback controls, discovery features, library management, and integration with Game Theme Music.

I’m continuing to focus on making ResonaDeck reliable, responsive, and enjoyable to use.

Thank you to everyone who has downloaded it, tested it, or shared feedback.

Your support helps keep these projects moving forward.

Enjoy your music!

Valentine
Developer of ResonaDeck

beallio/decky-metadata.name: v0.6.8 — Add Steam HLTB overrides, PR Testing tab, and Settings UI polish
beallio/decky-metadata.body:
Add Steam HLTB overrides, PR Testing tab, and Settings UI polish

### Added

- **Choose a HowLongToBeat game for Steam games.** When **Show HowLongToBeat
  times** is enabled, Steam games now show **Edit Metadata...** in their menu
  and open directly to the **HowLongToBeat** tab, so you can search for or pin
  the right HowLongToBeat entry when automatic matching misses (for example,
  *Gothic 1 - classic*). Per-game HLTB choices are stored separately from
  non-Steam metadata and apply only to Library game pages; Steam Store pages
  continue to use automatic matching.
- **Testing tab for pull request builds.** Under **Updates → Developer**,
  turn on **Enable Testing tab** to show a **Testing** tab in Settings. It lists
  open pull requests from this repository (plus fork pull requests opted in with
  the `test-build` label), lets you sort and open them on GitHub, and verifies
  the build published to the `pr-builds` GitHub prerelease against its manifest
  and SHA-256 checksum before handing the GitHub Releases ZIP to Decky Loader
  to install.

### Changed

- **SteamOS-style Updates UI.** **Settings → Updates** now matches SteamOS's
  **Software Updates** layout: a single **Software Updates** row shows the
  installed version and last-checked status with one morphing button (**Check For
  Updates** → **Checking...** → **Up-to-date** / **Apply** → **Applying...**),
  paired with an **Update Channel** dropdown (**Stable** / **Development**).
- **Focusable Metadata stats and Settings layout polish across ProtonDB, HLTB,
  and Game trailers.** In **Settings → Metadata**, **Detected non-Steam games**,
  **Metadata saved**, and **Missing metadata** are now selectable and focusable
  like **Versions**. In **Settings → ProtonDB badges**, **Game view** and
  **Store** sit directly below **Enable ProtonDB badges**, followed by a **Game
  covers** subsection for **Home game covers**, **Library game covers**,
  **Covers only on focus or hover**, and **Cover badge position** (the last two
  are enabled only when **Home game covers** or **Library game covers** is on).
  In **Settings → HLTB times**, controls below **Store** are grouped into
  **Stats**, **Style**, **Customize**, and **Cache** subsections. In
  **Settings → Game trailers**, **Video quality** and **Big Picture display**
  sit below **Enable trailers** ahead of **Detail view** and **Home view**,
  turning off **Detail view trailers** or **Home view trailers** disables its
  connected controls, and **Big Picture display** shows status text only for
  actionable warnings or errors.

### Fixed

- **Keep Refresh metadata progress inside the Quick Access Menu.** The
  refresh progress bar now lays out below inside a `PanelSectionRow` with
  clamped wrapping so long game titles stay within the right edge of the panel.
- **Match Steam Store styling and fix first-pass loading for the Store info row.**
  HowLongToBeat numbers now use Steam Store blue, the ProtonDB tier label matches
  Steam Deck Compatibility's font and color, only the new **View details** button
  inside the ProtonDB card is focusable (matching Steam's **Learn more** button),
  and first-visit Store page navigation now observes nested DOM mounts and polls
  faster until attached.
- **Refresh Settings automatically when the plugin reloads.** Updating or
  installing a PR build from **Settings** now refreshes the open Settings page in
  place while keeping the active tab instead of leaving stale UI mounted.

mdeguzis/decky-proton-pulse.name: Proton Pulse v1.15.0
mdeguzis/decky-proton-pulse.body:
Proton Pulse v1.15.0

- Accept Armada, Pocknix, and Android as valid OS entries, letting Retroid Pocket / AYN Odin / AyaNeo Pocket DS and DroidDeck users submit reports (refs mdeguzis/proton-pulse-web#544)
- Multi-config-per-app: a game can now hold any number of named launch-option profiles ('Default', '60fps low', 'framegen', etc.). Save creates a new profile when the name differs; matching names still upsert. Storage keyed by (appId, profileName); Supabase user_proton_configs schema migrated to a composite (voter_id, app_id, profile_name) primary key.
- Save vs Apply split in the Config Editor: Save persists to storage + cloud without touching Steam launch options or bumping the active slot. Apply writes to Steam launch options + promotes the profile to ACTIVE. Save-only profiles no longer steal ACTIVE from a profile you are currently playing.
- ACTIVE badge on the row whose profile is currently applied. Playtime attributes to that specific profile.
- Per-config Pending Approval / Published pills. Two profiles on the same game no longer both light up when only one was submitted; each row reflects its own report state via config_key. Legacy null-key submissions from before this fix light up only the ACTIVE profile as a fallback.
- Submit modal fires onSubmitted so the Manage tab refreshes the row status without waiting for a remount.
- Submit modal is passed configKey so the DB row's config_key is populated. Report status becomes truly per-profile going forward.
- Plugin submits now set game_owned=true. The admin report detail no longer shows 'Game Owned: false' for plugin-sourced reports.
- 'Applied X ago' meta line now ticks live: ManageTab subscribes to onConfigSaved (immediate refresh after Apply / Reapply) plus a 60s tick so the relative label doesn't go stale.
- Draft pill hidden when there is no submitted report for a profile. SYNCED green badge already covers the cloud state; the extra 'Draft' gray pill next to it read as noise.

necrosiak/steamcord.name: v1.48.4
necrosiak/steamcord.body:
### Fixes

- Fullscreen video and the video grid no longer inherit the offset of Steam's modal animation. Fullscreen temporarily removes the animation and ancestor containing-block constraints, then restores the borrowed styles when it closes (#105).
- Chat Mix preserves the current mixed volume if a temporary device snapshot cannot resolve the playback output, instead of briefly restoring the original game volume. Explicitly disabling Chat Mix still restores the original level (#107).

### Options

- General settings: **Open links in the external browser** opens HTTP(S) message links in your system's default browser. It is off by default, shared by the QAM and expanded view, and uses the Linux desktop-session environment or the Windows default URL handler. Select Firefox as your OS default if that is where you want links to open. This does not add a Roblox-specific launcher (#116).
- General settings: **Swap DMs and Servers** reverses their current order in both views. It is off by default, preserving each view's existing order and opening-page preference (#120).

### Maintenance and diagnostics

- Modal layout compatibility and style restoration now live in a dedicated module, with shared exports for existing components (#119).
- Overlay logs record actual window/monitor geometry after size changes, helping investigate the remaining centered-overlay report (#92). This diagnostic addition does not claim to fix that report.

### Validation

- Local build passed; 105 JavaScript tests, 14 menu lifecycle checks and 204 Python tests passed (2 Python tests skipped).
- A real Steam modal on the BC250 was checked at the viewport origin, covering all four corners, with borrowed styles restored after closure. An isolated PipeWire test confirmed that a mixed stream remains at 50% during a simulated missing-output snapshot and recovers without a volume-event loop.
- Linux and Windows link-launch boundaries are tested without launching a browser. Live Windows/browser testing and confirmation that all intermittent long-call spikes are resolved remain pending. The broader audit in #119 stays open.

### Thanks

Thanks to [@numeraltrace](https://github.com/numeraltrace) for the fullscreen, audio and navigation follow-ups, and [@EasyAs123ABC](https://github.com/EasyAs123ABC) for clarifying the external-browser use case.

jinzhongjia/decky-music.name: v1.1.7
jinzhongjia/decky-music.body:
## 修复

- 修复左侧 Steam 菜单注入的 wrapper 递归：复用 `<Ie>` element 时不再重复包裹，避免栈深度累积导致 Steam UI 报 `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`（#83）。
- 左侧菜单注入改为 fail-closed：`fe.type` 保持 FunctionComponent，真正的 React ErrorBoundary 作为子组件；注入 render 有硬深度上限，异常时永久熔断并还原 `fe.type`。注入自身异常不会再升级成整个 Steam UI 错误页。
- 旧版本残留的、无法解链的 wrapper 会直接断开，避免历史 wrapper 链继续递归。

## 验证

- `pnpm build`、`pnpm lint`、`pnpm test:ui`（51/51）通过。
- 20,000 次复用同一个 `<Ie>` element 渲染：wrapper 不加深；v1.1.6 旧实现会直接 `RangeError`。
- 原始 `fe` / `Ie` 抛异常、clone 失败、递归渲染均有回归用例。
- Steam Deck 真机（Decky v3.2.10-pre1）：v1.1.7 侧载后左侧菜单显示「音乐」；连续开关菜单 60 次（30 开 / 30 关）无错误页、无 `RangeError`；点击「音乐」进入 `/music` 推荐页正常；bridge 日志无 WARN/ERROR。
- player / provider 重新构建，GLIBC 检查通过。

## 说明

本次 player / provider 无行为变更，仅随版本重新构建并更新二进制指纹。

mimed95/decky-voxtype.name: 0.2.0 Fixed naming and build pipeline
mimed95/decky-voxtype.body:
## Changes

- **Plugin identifier unified as `decky-voxtype`.** Appears under that name in Decky Loader; previously registered as "Voxtype", which diverged from the directory, package name, and zip filename.
- **Single source of truth for the name.** Defined once in `plugin.json`; consumed at runtime via `@decky/manifest`, in packaging via `jq`, and in CI via a metadata step.
- **Release pipeline fixed.** The `0.1.0` release shipped with no zip attached because the CI upload gate was `refs/tags/v*` and the tag was `0.1.0`. Both the trigger filter and the upload gate now accept any tag.
- **Packaging hardening.** `scripts/pack.sh` now copies `dist/*.js` (not only `index.js`), guarding against future Rollup code-splitting.
- **Dependency alignment.** Pinned `@types/react-router@5.1.20` to match Decky Loader upstream and `@decky/api`'s own devDeps — resolves a dangling type import under `tsc --noEmit`.

mimed95/decky-voxtype.name: First Release 0.1.0

# Voxtype v0.1.0 — voice dictation comes to Steam Deck Game Mode

  **The first voice-typing plugin for Decky Loader.** Press a controller button, speak, release — and the
  transcription lands on your system clipboard, ready to paste into any text field on your Deck. Fully local,
   fully offline, built on [voxtype](https://github.com/peteonrails/voxtype) and [whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggerganov/whisper.cpp).

  No cloud. No API key. No account. Your voice never leaves the Deck.

  ## Highlights

  - **Controller-native push-to-talk.** Bind any button (or a two-button chord) directly through the plugin's
   settings. No fiddling with Steam Input keyboard mappings; the plugin listens at the Steam Input layer
  itself. Default: **R4** back grip.
  - **Vulkan acceleration on the Deck's GPU.** Ships with both an AVX2 CPU build and a Vulkan-enabled build
  of voxtype. One toggle switches between them — no `pacman`, no read-only root gymnastics, no lingering
  system…

### Fixed
- **Volume-routing boot delay**: after a reboot, the guide+stick volume shortcut sometimes fell back to SteamOS's normal volume slider instead of routing through this plugin, until a volume slider was touched manually. SteamOS only checks once, at Gamescope session start, whether the HDMI output supports external volume control — WirePlumber is now always restarted as the very first step of plugin startup (not only when its config changed) so the check has the best chance of succeeding on its own. Confirmed fixed across a real reboot.
- **TV sync blueprint**: none of the TV actions (Steam device turning on, volume buttons, mute, guide button) touch the TV anymore while it's on and showing something other than the configured HDMI input — previously the guide button and volume buttons would act on the TV regardless of what was currently on screen.
- **Blueprint crash**: leaving the volume buttons / guide button / Steam Link streaming entity inputs unset could crash automation validation ("Entity ID is not a valid entity ID"), since Home Assistant rejects an empty string as a target entity_id for the `event.received` trigger. Those inputs now default to a syntactically valid but nonexistent placeholder entity instead, which simply never fires.

Detected via `SteamClient.RemotePlay.RegisterForDevicesChanges` (undocumented, community-reverse-engineered, see the README note).
- The [TV sync blueprint](blueprints/automation/steamos_tv_sync.yaml) uses it: starting a stream turns the TV off (only if it's on the right HDMI input), ending the stream turns it back on — with a fix so the existing "TV off suspends the Steam device" rule doesn't fire because of this new TV-off action.

### Fixed

jjuuzzii/decky-ha-mqtt-plugin.name: v0.5.0 - Current app sensor + update notifications

hostsrc/decky-prysm.body:
# Prysm v0.2.0 - First Public Release

Stream your Steam Deck screen to any browser on your network. One-tap start from Game Mode.

## Features

- **Two streaming methods** - choose in QAM settings:
  - MPEG-TS (~500ms latency) - stable, works on any browser
  - WebRTC (~200ms latency) - lower latency via MediaMTX
- **VAAPI hardware encoding** - H.264 on AMD GPU, near-zero CPU usage
- **Quality presets** - 480p30, 720p30, 720p60, 1080p30, 1080p60
- **Live stats in QAM** - viewers, bytes sent, encoder status
- **Auto-restart** on capture failure
- **Native Decky UI** - all standard Steam Deck components

## Install

1. Download `Prysm-v0.2.0.zip`
2. Extract `Prysm/` folder to `~/homebrew/plugins/` on your Steam Deck
3. Restart Decky Loader: `sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader`

Or one-liner:
```bash
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hostsrc/decky-prysm/main/install.sh | bash
```

## Requirements

- Steam Deck running SteamOS 3.5+
- Decky Loader installed
- Game must NOT have `ENABLE_GAMESCOPE_WSI=0` in launch options

## Performance (720p30 over WiFi/Ethernet)

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Bitrate | ~5 Mbps |
| Decoded FPS | 29 fps |
| Dropped frames | <1% |
| Buffer | 0.4s |
| CPU usage | <3% (VAAPI) |

## What's New

### Streaming
- kmsgrab capture with VAAPI H.264 hardware encoding
- HTTP MPEG-TS server with mpegts.js viewer (low-latency tuned)
- MediaMTX WebRTC backend as alternative streaming method
- Auto-restart on FFmpeg/capture failures
- TS packet-aligned reads to prevent sync errors
- ThreadingHTTPServer for non-blocking stats

### QAM Plugin
- Clean single-panel layout with Start Streaming as primary action
- Method selector (MPEG-TS / WebRTC)
- Quality presets (480p30 to 1080p60)
- Audio toggle
- Live stats: viewers, total sent, encoder status
- All native Decky UI components

### Infrastructure
- GitHub Actions CI/CD (build + release pipelines)
- Makefile with build/dist/deploy targets
- Distribution zip matching Decky Plugin Store requirements
- Full GPL-2.0 license

## Contributors

- [@hostsrc](https://github.com/hostsrc)
- Claude Opus 4.6 (AI pair programmer)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/hostsrc/decky-prysm/commits/v0.2.0
