kentronix57/decky-loader-xgmobile-manage.name: xgmobile-manager v0.3.0
kentronix57/decky-loader-xgmobile-manage.body:
## XG Mobile Manager 0.3.0

The first stable release since 0.2.4. It brings a new compact panel, CachyOS support, a much more reliable Enable and Eject, and **support for SteamOS 3.9.5**.

> **SteamOS users, please read:** SteamOS 3.9.5 moved to a new kernel (7.2) that older plugin versions can't build the NVIDIA driver for. After installing 0.3.0, open the plugin → **▸ Setup & Maintenance** → **Install NVIDIA Drivers**, then reboot. 0.3.0 installs NVIDIA driver **620.70.06**.

### Highlights
* **SteamOS 3.9.5 support:** NVIDIA 620.70.06 for kernel 7.2. Booting with the XG Mobile enabled works again: the boot service notices when the driver loaded before its firmware was readable and reloads it (about 3 seconds on those boots).
* **A compact panel:** a status line (Active / Connected / Not connected), one Enable/Eject button, live temperature, power (`used / limit W`), VRAM and load, with colours. Details are behind ⓘ pop-ups, and rarely used buttons are under ▸ Setup & Maintenance.
* **CachyOS support:** an NVIDIA driver installer that uses CachyOS's own packages, plus fixes for its login manager.
* **A safer Eject:**
  * Eject now asks before closing your game.
  * Changing the power profile can no longer "click through" to the Eject button.
  * Bazzite's `cardwired` service is restarted instead of killed (killing it left Game Mode stuck at login).
  * The eGPU is released in a safe order, and the session returns to Game Mode reliably.
* **Full power on the RTX 4090:** the NVIDIA power services start after the eGPU is up, so Performance reaches 150 W.
* **A boot safety net:** powering off with the XG Mobile enabled and booting without it no longer leads to a black screen.
* **Clearer errors:** pop-ups say what went wrong and what to do, including a separate message when the NVIDIA driver doesn't build for a new SteamOS kernel.
* **Logs in their own folder:** `~/homebrew/logs/xgmobile-manager/activity/`. Old logs are moved there automatically.

### Upgrading
* **SteamOS:** install 0.3.0, then **Install NVIDIA Drivers** and reboot (see above). After every future SteamOS update: Reset Driver Environment → update → reboot → Install NVIDIA Drivers.
* **Bazzite:** nothing to do; the drivers come with the bazzite-deck-nvidia image.
* **CachyOS:** if you haven't yet, **Install NVIDIA Drivers** once. After that, the drivers update with `sudo pacman -Syu`.

Quick install (latest stable):
```bash
curl -sL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/refs/heads/main/bin/install.sh" > /tmp/install.sh && bash /tmp/install.sh
```

### Tested on
ROG Ally (RC71L) + RTX 4090 XG Mobile, on a 4K TV (resolution set to 2K):
* SteamOS 3.9.5 (kernel 7.2.7), NVIDIA 620.70.06 installed by the plugin
* Bazzite 45.20261112 (bazzite-deck-nvidia), NVIDIA 620.70.06
* CachyOS Handheld (kernel 7.2.9 deckify), NVIDIA 615.78.08

**Hardware I don't own** (AMD XG Mobile, RTX 3080, ROG Flow laptops) relies on community testers. Thanks to @tanayabhay-creator for the RTX 3080 reports and measurements.

### Known issues
* **Bazzite + NVIDIA:** waking from sleep with the eGPU active forces a hard reboot (upstream). Eject before sleeping.
* **4K and ultrawide in Game Mode** may not work fully (gamescope). Desktop Mode supports more resolutions.
* **On SteamOS, Steam's performance overlay** shows 0 °C / 0 MHz for the XG Mobile. The plugin's panel shows the real values.

See the [README](https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager#readme) for details. Starting with 0.3.0, development is AI-assisted (see [AI-Assisted Development](https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager#ai-assisted-development)).

## What's Changed
* feat: descriptive SteamUI pop-ups with actionable error messages by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/19
* test: Tier 0 no-hardware test harness (pytest + bats + vitest, CI) by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/20
* fix: CachyOS session compatibility and egpu-enable robustness by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/21
* feat: automated NVIDIA driver install and session fixes for CachyOS by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/23
* fix: eject release order, boot safety net, and failures that outlive the panel by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/24
* feat: plugin logs in their own folder, with automatic migration of old logs by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/26
* fix: start the NVIDIA services after the eGPU is up, so the XG Mobile gets its full power by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/27
* fix: hardware pass 2 follow-ups (desktop-eject black screen, logs, power docs) by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/28
* fix: desktop Eject returns to Game Mode, restart an eGPU-tainted user manager, boot sync waits for the card by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/29
* feat: compact Quick Access panel with status colours and telemetry limits by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/30
* ci: rewrite the release workflow around build.sh with a Tier 0 gate by @Kentronix57 in https://github.com/Kentronix57/Decky-Loader-XGMobile-Manager/pull/22

ag69075/steamos_plugin_achievements.body:
fix: hide badge/bubble for 5 min on game launch

Remove RegisterForGameActionEnd and RegisterForAppLifetimeNotifications
handlers from registerGameActionTracking — both fire within seconds of
launch and were clearing the "launching" state prematurely, causing the
badge/bubble to reappear almost immediately.

Now rely solely on a 300 000 ms safety timer (5 min) started on

beallio/decky-ui-restored.name: v0.2.6 — Brings back Steam's own mini achievement row on the game-details page and updates
beallio/decky-ui-restored.body:
Brings back Steam's own mini achievement row on the game-details page and updates
development dependencies with security fixes.

### Fixed

- Stop drawing a plugin-owned achievement row. Steam's native mini achievements row returns
  because the plugin supplies the `onSeek` prop that the Gaming Mode game page omits
  ([#13540](https://github.com/ValveSoftware/steam-for-linux/issues/13540)), so Steam's own
  layout, count format, progress bar, navigation, and visibility rules apply on all three
  game-details routes. Turning the feature off hides the row without a reload. The approach
  matches Decky Metadata v0.6.2.

### Security

- Update `happy-dom` from 20.11.6 to 21.0.4, `vitest` and `@vitest/mocker` from 4.1.11 to
  4.1.12, `vite` from 8.3.0 to 8.3.6, `fast-uri` from 3.1.6 to 3.1.9, and `source-map-js`
  from 1.2.1 to 1.2.2, resolving 18 GitHub Dependabot alerts in development-only
  dependencies. The `deepmerge` advisory (GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4) has no patched release and
  affects only the build-time `@rollup/plugin-node-resolve`.

beallio/decky-ui-restored.name: v0.2.5 — Releases the old game-details page promptly when navigation removes the whole PlayBar
beallio/decky-ui-restored.body:
Releases the old game-details page promptly when navigation removes the whole PlayBar.

### Fixed

- Detect when navigation detaches the row's entire PlayBar and remove the injected row,
  observer, and stale page references instead of retaining them until another event.

beallio/decky-ui-restored.name: v0.2.4 — Restores the mini achievement progress row on the November 2026 Steam client and updates
beallio/decky-ui-restored.body:
Restores the mini achievement progress row on the November 2026 Steam client and updates
the frontend test toolchain.

### Fixed

- Restore the achievement progress row beside Play Time after Steam removed its native
  `MiniAchievements` component. The plugin draws the row in Steam's PlayBar layout from
  Steam's achievement progress cache, keeps it hidden when totals are unavailable or an
  uninstalled game has no unlocked achievements, and does not duplicate a native row
  ([#14](https://github.com/beallio/Decky-UI-Restored/issues/14)).
- Poll Steam's achievement progress cache on a bounded retry schedule after requesting an
  update, so a response that arrives late still appears without navigating away. Ported
  from the Decky Metadata fix (`fab5c51`, `6e4d8ac`).

### Security

- Update `vitest` and `@vitest/mocker` from 4.1.10 to 4.1.11, preventing path traversal
  and arbitrary file reads through redirect mocks (GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9).

cwtechshiz/nordvpn-decky.body:
# NordVPN Decky Loader Plugin - v1.1.0 🚀

### 🌟 What's New
* **NordVPN Auto-Detection Guard:** The plugin now dynamically checks if the NordVPN CLI service is installed and running on your Steam Deck. If it's missing, it will gently prompt you with setup requirements instead of silently failing.
* **Custom Polling Interval Slider:** Take control of your resource usage. You can now adjust how frequently the plugin checks your connection status directly from the settings menu.
* **Settings Persistence:** The plugin now securely remembers your custom polling settings across Deck reboots and Game Mode restarts.

### 🔧 Bug Fixes
* **Resolved Polling Race Condition:** Fixed a bug where the background auto-refresh loop would instantly wipe out connection error texts before you had a chance to read what went wrong.

### 📦 Fast Installation / Update
To install or update to this version, run this one-liner in your Steam Deck's Konsole terminal (Desktop Mode):
```bash
curl -L [https://github.com/cwtechshiz/nordvpn-decky/raw/main/install.sh](https://github.com/cwtechshiz/nordvpn-decky/raw/main/install.sh) | sh

rayekkk/deckyvibrancehdr.body:
### ✨ Added

- **About:** **Use Rayek's store** makes Rayek's store Decky's store channel after you confirm, so Decky's Store
  tab lists Rayek's plugins and offers their updates.

### 🔧 Changed

**Menu**
- Descriptions use plain words instead of terms such as LUT, EDID or gamut. Control names are unchanged.
- **Last applied** replaces "Last LUT sent" under **Now** and also appears for SDR on screens that use the
  additional colour table above 200%.
- While the plugin starts, the menu shows a spinner.
- If the plugin cannot start, it says **Decky Vibrance HDR unavailable** with the reason, a **Try again**
  button and the Updates section, so a broken install can still be updated.
- Texts use American spelling ("colors") and a single "…" character.
- While an external display is connected, it explains that your saved settings apply again once you
  unplug it.
- It checks for changes every 3 seconds while idle, and every second while colors are being prepared or
  something needs attention.

**Errors**
- A setting that fails after you close the menu now shows a **Decky Vibrance HDR** message with the
  reason, instead of the slider silently moving back the next time you open it.
- A change the plugin refuses now also says why under that switch, slider or **Back to defaults**, until
  you use that control again.

**About**
- It is the new last row of the menu. Its page shows the version, author and license, with **Updates** at
  the bottom; Updates is no longer on the main menu.

**Updates**
- Wording now matches the other plugins: **Installed version**, **Checking GitHub…**,
  **Download <version>** and **<version> downloaded**, with the saved file shown as `~/Downloads/…` and a shorter
  install hint.
- A failed check or download shows **Could not complete** with the reason in the section instead of a
  message over the screen.
- When no release can be offered (none published yet, or its ZIP is not ready), the section says why
  instead of "Up to date".

**Sliders**
- A switch or reset no longer jumps ahead of a slider change you made before it; changes reach the
  plugin in the order you made them.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Display**
- Disabling the plugin or restarting Decky puts the original colors back even when the plugin was in the
  middle of another display change.
- A screen that reports no EDID at all is treated as standard gamut, as gamescope does, so 101% no longer
  jumps to the strongest SDR setting there.
- An unusual HDR entry in a screen's EDID no longer hides what the rest of the EDID says about HDR.
- When the plugin starts while docked and the display server answers slowly, it no longer takes its
  color calibration from the external display.

**Sliders**
- Slider and switch changes wait less for background display checks when the display server answers
  slowly.

**Settings**
- Settings survive a power cut right after a change, and files left by an interrupted save are cleaned
  up.
- A damaged settings file no longer resets everything: the plugin goes back to the last good copy it
  keeps beside it, keeps the damaged file as `settings.json.corrupt-…` and says so in the menu.

**Updates**
- Downloads accept only the release ZIP GitHub lists for this plugin, with the exact size and SHA-256
  GitHub reports, and every file in it is checked before saving.
- A download is refused unless the release is newer than the installed one.
- Stopping or updating the plugin no longer waits for a slow or stuck update check.
- A download that ends early is reported as failed instead of being kept, and a download in progress
  stops when the plugin stops.

**Errors**
- Messages in the menu no longer show folders that contain your user name; the full details are in the
  Decky log.

### 🔧 Changed

**Menu**
- A backend that is slow to answer is shown as **Waiting for backend** (a change) or
  **Backend unavailable** (a read) instead of a silent spinner, also after the panel was closed and reopened.
- The **Retry** button is gone; the open panel already asks again every second, so it never did anything
  extra.
- Clearer wording for what to do when a setting cannot be applied, and for the SDR and HDR slider
  descriptions.

**Updates**
- The result fields can be reached with the gamepad, and the section keeps its focus when the plugin
  becomes ready or loses its display.

**Install**
- Instructions now match Decky: turn on Developer mode, choose **Browse** next to
  **Install Plugin from ZIP File**, accept Decky's warning and confirm. That replaces the installed version itself,
  so there is no need to uninstall first, and settings are always kept.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Settings**
- An empty settings file no longer keeps the controls paused forever. It can be left by an…

### 🐛 Fixed

**Settings**
- Saved settings are protected when the plugin cannot read them or Decky stops during startup.
  Controls now wait for settings to load instead of replacing your choices with defaults.
- Startup and display checks no longer get stuck on invalid settings or display-information files.

**Errors**
- Startup errors now explain what failed. A settings-file problem is no longer described as a missing
  Game Mode connection or a failed save.

**Menu**
- Slow or missing backend replies no longer let repeated status checks build up a queue of requests.
- Status checking resumes when the pending call finishes, keeping newer choices made after reopening the
  menu or using **Back to defaults**.

**Updates**
- Update checks and downloads keep their progress when you close and reopen the Quick Access Menu.
  Completed download paths and errors remain available.
- Reopening the menu no longer starts duplicate update requests, buttons from a closed menu cannot start…

### 🔧 Changed

**Performance**
- Much faster controls on Armada devices running Decky through emulation. On Odin 3, saturation
  changes took about 0.6 seconds for HDR and 0.7 seconds for SDR, and turning an effect off during a build took
  41–121 ms. Results may vary by device and workload; ordinary SteamOS keeps its existing execution path.
- Faster color-LUT generation, and recent results are reused when you return to a previous
  saturation value. LUT resolution and color calculations are unchanged.
- Fewer repeated display checks, unnecessary saves and rebuilds, leaving more room for the controls
  to respond to your next change.

**Errors**
- Connection problems and failed changes are shown more clearly, and the plugin retries operations that
  could not be completed.

**Display**
- Better recovery after sleep, temporary display connection problems and changes between the built-in
  screen and an external monitor.
- Better detection of the panel's color capabilities and HDR…

### 🔧 Changed
- **HDR:** the status shows the saturation of the last LUT successfully sent, without claiming gamescope has
  confirmed loading it.

### 🐛 Fixed

**Display**
- Failed HDR and SDR look builds or replacements are retried. An older working file no longer counts as
  a completed slider change.

**Errors**
- SDR, SDR look and HDR errors are kept independently. A successful operation on one control no longer
  hides another control's failed apply or reset.

**SDR**
- Enabling again after a failed release preserves the original baseline instead of capturing the plugin's
  own value.
- Missing SDR properties and failed initial SDR writes are retried. A missing property is recreated only
  after confirming gamescope is still reachable.
- The standard-gamut SDR look above 200% now converts gamescope's generic source gamut to BT.2020 for ICtCp
  and back before clipping. Native white from EDID is adapted to D65; unreadable white falls back to D65.

**Sliders**
- Pending edits…

parvagans/achievement-companion.body:

# v0.42.0

## RetroAchievements in the STEAM menu and shared Steam pins

Open achievements and guides while playing a RetroAchievements game, and manage the same Steam pins from Steam or Achievement Companion.

### What's New

**In-game RetroAchievements and Guides**

- Press **STEAM** while a matched RetroAchievements shortcut is running. Select the game and open **Achievements** to see base-set progress, locked and unlocked achievements, and your current pin. Turn on **Pin Achievements** and press **X** to pin or unpin.
- Open **Guides** between **Achievements** and **Notes**. The native dialog can open community mastery guide, or the game's discussion when available. Press **B** to return to **Guides**.

**RetroAchievements in the Steam library**

- Open Steam's native achievement list from the **Achievements** icon beside **Play** or through **Your Stuff**. Use **All Sets** to browse verified subsets. The base set and each subset have their own progress and pin.
- In Steam's **All Achievements** view, turn on **Pin Achievements**, focus a locked achievement, and press **X**. Your pin also appears in Achievement Companion's **Up Next** and **Pinned Achievements**. The **Your Stuff** preview still offers **Y** where shown.

**Shared pins for Steam games**

- Pin or unpin in Steam or Achievement Companion to update the same list for the signed-in Steam account.
- If a game has an unfinished Steam pin, choose which one appears first in Achievement Companion's **Up Next**. Existing Achievement Companion pins are added to Steam's list when you next open the corresponding game in Achievement Companion.

### Additional Improvements

- **Steam compatibility hotfix from v0.41.1.** The Steam client update changed where **Your Stuff** and **My Achievements** read achievement data. The hotfix restored RetroAchievements totals and rows in both views, including grayscale artwork for locked achievements. [Issue #4](https://github.com/parvagans/achievement-companion/issues/4)
- **Native achievement navigation.** **Activity** and **Up Next** open the exact achievement in Steam's list. Press **B** to return to the originating tile or recommendation.
- **Library layout during launch.** The Achievement Companion badge and **Up Next** preview stay aligned and hide together when Steam shows the launch screen.

santojon/deck-shelves.name: Deck Shelves v3.4.2-beta.1
santojon/deck-shelves.body:
- **Simpler text**: tips, descriptions and help pages are shorter and plainer in every language, and the Filters help no longer says that Store tag, Friends and Achievements filters don't work yet.

- **A new filter editor**: each condition is a section that opens to edit it. Closed, its header shows the type, the value, whether it is negated, and a check mark or an X beside the arrow for complete or not. Negate, remove and add are icon buttons, choosing whether all or any of the conditions must match takes one press, and the focus stays in the list as you add or remove conditions.

- **Any condition can be negated**: every filter type offers Negate, for shelves like "everything except…". The Integrations tab no longer marks filter types as invertible, and the source resolver inspector says "negated".

- **Grouped conditions stay safe**: a condition that holds others keeps them when you switch it to another grouping type, and it cannot change to a type that would drop them.

- **A cleaner Quick Access panel and dialogs**: list rows open their actions from a compact menu button, action bars spread their buttons evenly, and the panel, its lists and the dialogs are restyled. Collapsible sections in dialogs get the panel's look and a visible focus ring.

- **Clearer labels**: the shelf editors' title reads "Edit shelf:" with the shelf's name, the sort label reads "Order by", and the name field is the client's own labelled text field.

- **For theme authors**: several CSS classes have new names; the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) lists each one.

- **Collection shelves show exactly what the collection holds**: the shelf reads the collection by its id from the Steam client and shows its current games, dynamic collections included. Collections with similar names no longer mix.

- **Sorting by size, release date, metacritic or review score works on the Deck** without the online enrichment, and the templates that pick small games or well-reviewed ones (Short battery, Travel mode, Low battery, Forgotten gems) find their games again.

- **Conditions, sort keys and templates read what the Steam client really has**: store tags (by name in your language or by id), friends who own a game, achievements (count, percentage, not completed), Family Sharing, the "at least N of", "any of" and "none of" groups, the Almost finished, Couch gaming, Co-op ready and Party games templates and the Dynamic collections source. Options that read data the client never provides are gone (launch counts, session length, install date, storage device, executable type, DLC and soundtrack ownership, the launcher libraries); duplicates are rewritten to the option they repeat when your settings load. A shelf that still names a removed option stays empty and shows "Unavailable" in the editor.

- **Dynamic collections are marked** with a bolt in the collection picker.

- **Steam features and purchase date conditions**: filter by the features Steam lists for a game (single-player, co-op, cloud saves, controller support…) and by the date you bought it; store tags can require any or all of the tags, and release dates can be "unknown".

- **TabMaster 3.1 tabs import whole**: every filter of a TabMaster tab becomes the matching condition here, dates, achievements, friends, tags, features, SD card and install folder included.

- **Pinned games first, then recently played**: a new "Source order" sort lists the sources of a shelf one after the other, each with its own sort, and built-in lists (pinned games, play history, the queues) and smart shelves can now be added as sources. Pinned games come last pinned first; reverse the sort to start from the first one.

- **A sort and a game limit for each source**: each source of a multi-source shelf can pick its own games with its own sort and limit, under any shelf sort, for example the three most played installed games and the two latest pinned ones; the shelf's sort and game limit then order and cut them all.

- **Arrange each source by hand**: set a source of a multi-source shelf to Manual, choose Arrange games and move its games in the preview, for example four chosen launchers first and then a collection by last played. The source's game limit keeps the first ones.

- **The Quick Access side panel opens again**: on the current Steam client the extra settings column next to Quick Access shows up again. Its dropdowns show their options over the Home, and the side panel comes back on that setting once you pick one or go back.

- **Hidden gems is back**: never-played games with a high review score, best first.

- **The discount badge can show the sale price**: choose the percentage, the price as the store writes it in your currency, price and discount, or discount and price, and choose separately what the selected card shows, for example the discount on every card and the price too on the one you select. Set it in the Visual settings for every shelf, or choose "Per shelf" there and set it in each shelf's Display tab. With both values the badge is a compact two-part tag instead of a long line of text.

- **The Home opens on the recent games row**: with "Use shelf as Recents" on, or with Steam's own recent games shown, the focus stays on that row when the Home opens, after a restart or back from a game, instead of jumping to the first shelf below it a moment later.

- **Back on the game you opened**: after opening a game from one of the plugin's shelves, the focus returns to that game's card when you come back within ten minutes, instead of landing on the recent games row or the first shelf.

- **"Use shelf as Recents" works when the first shelf is empty**: if your first shelf has no games at the moment, for example one that lists downloads and updates, the row shows the next shelf that has games, and goes back to the first one as soon as it fills.

- **A manual order keeps your top games when you lower the game limit**: the games you placed first stay first and the limit cuts the end of the list. Before, they could move to the end of the editor preview with a "+" mark and disappear from the Home.

- **The side navigation looks like Steam's own Settings list**: the row under the cursor gets Steam's highlight, and themes that restyle Steam's list apply to it too, while the shelf on screen reads in bold. The recent games row is listed again whenever it shows on the Home, also when a shelf fills it. The tab at the top of the Quick Access side panel looks like Steam's page tabs.

- **Settings save with only smart shelves**: after every regular shelf was removed, a smart shelf with its own sort made every change fail to save.

- **Filter shelves keep the order you chose**: sorted by Deck compatibility, controller support, app status, friends, achievements or Family Sharing, a filter shelf was listed by name.

- **Focus stays on the card you came back to**: right after Steam starts, or after opening the same game twice in a row, the Home no longer moves the focus away from it.

- **Turning off Hide recents always brings the Recent Games row back**, also after a plugin reload or update in the first seconds after hiding it.

- **Shelves stay below the Recent Games row** when one of your shelves has "Recent Games" in its name.

- **Offline mode stays offline**: Deck Shelves no longer looks up missing descriptions, ratings or platform data on the Steam store; what was fetched before is still shown.

- **Clearing the theme class cache** in Advanced settings no longer drops the native card look from shelves until the next restart.

- **Other plugins fit in**: filter types, sort options and smart-shelf modes added by other plugins appear in the shelf editors beside the built-in ones. A shelf that uses one shows "Unavailable" and stays empty while that plugin is not running, and keeps the setting for when it is back. The "External source" type appears only when a plugin provides a source, and shelves that picked a built-in list there now show that list.

- **Non-Steam games in smart shelves**: Roulette, Daily Pick and Weekly Rotation include them; Recently Played, Long Sessions, Backlog Rescue and Rediscover when Steam tracked their play time; Couch Gaming, Party Games and Co-op Ready when Steam reports the store category; On Deck and Picks for this device when the minimum compatibility is Any. Shelves that need an empty play history, disk size, ratings or the purchase date leave them out.

- **Filter the combined result of a multi-source shelf**: "Combined result filters" in the editor's filter tab apply after the sources are joined or intersected (for example Wishlist + Store at 30 % off or more, then only shared or split screen games), and saved filters work there too. Games whose store data has not arrived yet are left out until a later refresh, and the preview says so. With Online features off or Offline mode on, only data already on the device is used. An earlier version that opens and saves the shelf drops these filters.

- **Play together**: conditions for local multiplayer, local co-op and local versus on the same screen (LAN, online-only and Remote Play Together games never count), for your library and Store games. Templates build shelves from them for My library, Steam Store or both, optionally only borrowed games in the library part, and a Borrowed games template lists what your Steam family lends you. Store games come from the deals, free and popular lists Deck Shelves already reads.

- **Store prices keep your currency**: discount and price shelves no longer switch a game's price back to US dollars after the store list is read again.

- **Online shelves fill sooner after you connect**: a wishlist or store shelf that came up empty while offline or before sign-in tries again after about a minute instead of ten.

- **Moving a shelf from a game's menu on the Home** follows the same list as Quick Access: with the unified list on, every shelf can move, and Move up or Move down steps past shelves that are hidden or have nothing to show, so the shelf really moves on screen. The focus stays on the same game.

- **Big Art with a shelf logo**: the first shelf stays where it was and the logo sits in the art above the shelf title, instead of pushing the games under the button bar.

- **Back on the same game with "Use shelf as Recents"**: coming back from a game's page to a shelf below the recent games row puts the focus on that game again instead of on the row.

- **Store shelves cope with Steam's request limit**: when the Steam store stops answering game details for a while, Deck Shelves waits before asking again instead of asking on every refresh, and Refresh cache on an online shelf reloads the store list together with the game names.

- **A shelf's menu from the Quick Access side panel** closes the side panel first, so the menu shows over the Home and Quick Access steps aside, as it does for Steam's own menus.

- **One look for the Quick Access notices and the library location icons**: the update, safe mode and error notices share the welcome notice's layout (title, short text, Steam's buttons) and keep their own colors; the update notice has short Download and Dismiss buttons side by side, and the library location condition shows drive, SD card and network icons instead of emoji.

- **Cloud sync no longer saves over and over**: on a device that synced a shelf or profile deletion more than 60 days ago, settings kept being saved several times a second; they now settle after one round.

- **Safer updates**: an update download is checked against the published release and discarded if it doesn't match.

- **A smart mode as a shelf's source**: a new regular shelf can take a smart mode, such as Recently played or Hidden gems, as its main source, with the shelf's own sort and look.

- **The editor preview shows your discount badge choices** (price, discount or both, and the selected card's style) while you create or edit a shelf.

- **A roomier shelf editor**: it uses the dialog's full width and scrolls to every option and to Save and Cancel with the controller. Options are grouped by what they change: Source for which games show (now with "Deduplicate by name"), Visual and Display for the look, and a new Auto tab for auto-pin and auto-collapse.

- **Smaller fixes**: Move up and Move down in the unified shelf list keep the shelf within that list, as dragging does, and the profile row's button hint reads Actions instead of Apply.

- **Daily Pick and Weekly Rotation change at your midnight**: they used to change at midnight UTC (for example 21:00 in Brazil).

- **Both shelf editors are laid out the same way**: in the smart shelf editor, "Deduplicate by name" is in Source and auto-pin and auto-collapse are in the Auto tab, as in the regular editor; dialog buttons keep Steam's own size; and the editor tabs have shorter names (Online, Extra, Smart, Auto) so they fit on one line. The tabs are centred with L1 and R1 hints at the ends, L1 and R1 cycle from the last tab back to the first, and the title, name field, result count and preview line up with the options.

- **Readable drive names in the library location condition**: a drive shows its volume label, and an SD card with no name shows Steam's own "MicroSD Card" instead of a long id.

- **Fewer pointless prompts and toasts**: a clean install no longer asks whose settings to use when there is nothing to adopt, that question no longer stays on screen after the plugin reloads, and "Settings updated from another device" only shows when something you can see changed, and a profile switch toast only appears when the profile actually changes. After closing a question at startup, or when the shelf used as Recents fills in, focus stays at the start of the Home instead of jumping to the second shelf.

santojon/deck-shelves.body:
- **Profiles say whether they switch your shelves**: a profile that also switches your shelves is marked "Includes shelves", you can turn that on or off at any time, new profiles include the shelves by default, and every profile text and prompt now says what applying it really does.

- **A restore point before every risky change**: switching profiles (by hand or by a trigger), importing anything and signing in with a different Steam account first save a snapshot, labelled with what made it.

- **Snapshots are easy to find**: the Backup tab explains backups and snapshots, says when the last one was made and has a **Restore a snapshot** button; recovery notices lead there. The snapshot screens say when snapshots are made and how long they are kept.

A new account is asked whether to copy the current shelves or start fresh; nothing is ever deleted. Prefer one set for everyone? Turn off **Separate settings per Steam account** in Settings → Backup. Your account ID is never stored or sent, and clearing the Steam client's storage no longer makes every account choose again.

moi952/decky-quick-tab.body:
## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- support Steam's new ES-module client via DFL.findVar fallback (moi952)
  Steam's beta client replaced webpack with native ES modules (Vite chunks),
  so findModuleByExport no longer finds the QAM renderers: they are now plain
  module-scope variables. Keep the legacy webpack lookup first and fall back to
  DFL.findVar (new Decky Loader), so a single build works on both old and new
  Steam/Decky.
- follow the active theme on tab rows, icons and action buttons (moi952)

## 🔧 Chores

gooorooox/ce-decky.name: v0.9.35
gooorooox/ce-decky.body:
# CE Decky 0.9.35

A table that worked on a non-Steam game is now remembered as working for as long as the game's executable stays the same, and FearLess search is ready about an hour after a first install instead of more than five.

## New

- A table that worked on a game with no version number, which is common for non-Steam games, is marked **Worked with this executable** with the solid green ring. It asks for a retest once the game's executable changes.

## Fixes

- FearLess search no longer misses a game whose topic the forum had just moved, and finds a topic titled only in another script for a game that also has an English name.
- A cheat with a fixed list of values offers only that list in **Configure cheats**, with no field to type another, and nothing outside the list is written into the game.
- A value saved outside such a list by an earlier version no longer stops **Apply** and **Load last table & cheats** for the whole table. The cheat's row says so, and choosing a value from the list replaces it.
- A cheat whose only choices are Disabled and Enabled is a plain on/off switch rather than a list.
- In **Advanced…**, **Table sources**, a FearLess refusal is counted once rather than twice, and background reading is no longer counted as a search.

## Changed

- FearLess search stays up to date with far fewer requests to the forum, usually one page a day, so it is refused less often.
- Opening the panel while Cheat Engine is running shows what pinned values hold in the game now, not what they held when the panel was last open.
- **Configure cheats** moves helper scripts that change nothing in the game by themselves behind **Scripts**. The values inside them stay in the list and show their current value without you switching anything on.
- The record of tables that worked is converted once when this version first starts, with every mark kept. An older version cannot read it, so going back to one means every working table asks for a retest.

## Install

Close any running game, then update from the CE Decky panel. If the panel does not offer it, open **Advanced…**, then **Plugin updates**, and press **Check now**. On Decky Loader 3.3.0 that needs 0.9.30 or later installed: an older version cannot reach the network there, so turn on **Developer mode** in Decky and install `CE-Decky-v0.9.35.zip` from the file. Your tables, authorizations and profiles are kept. The previous record of tables that worked is kept beside the new one as `table_compatibility.before-schema-4.json`.

Requires Decky Loader 3.2.8+, Proton, ~230 MB free. Offline and single-player games only.

<!-- ce-decky:notes-end -->

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/goooroooX/CE-Decky/compare/v0.9.34...v0.9.35

alyenax/gabecubeaura.name: GabeCubeAura 1.6.1
alyenax/gabecubeaura.body:
### JSAUX PIXEL Faceplate compatibility

Some newer Faceplates have a 32 KiB limit for GIF transfers. When a GIF is too large, the panel can reject the transfer before the animation starts. This release keeps GIFs prepared by GabeCubeAura strictly below that limit, at **32,767 bytes or less**, including with 180° rotation.

GabeCubeAura tries lossless compression first. If an animation still exceeds the limit, it uses fewer frames and holds the remaining frames longer to keep the same total duration. Weather animations and Dashboards that previously failed were reported working with the beta 5 build. This update should fix transfer failures caused by the size limit. [Beta 5 test result](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/issues/14#issuecomment-6900579017)

### Weather and recovery

- Refresh weather after system sleep and keep the Faceplate off if you switched it off in GabeCubeAura.
- Stop retrying an image when the Faceplate rejects it before transfer begins. Show the failure and offer **Resume stored picture** when a power-only recovery is available.

### Local diagnostics

- Export a local report with the installed version, transfer and recovery status, and available USB information.
- Use the optional **Faceplate GIF transfer test** under **Settings > Advanced > Diagnostics** to test a GIF of up to 32,767 bytes.

### Update in Decky

Select **Stable** under **Settings > Updates > Preferences**, then check for **1.6.1**. If you’re on beta 5, choose **Stable** to stay on the stable channel.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/Alyenax/GabeCubeAura/blob/v1.6.1/CHANGELOG.md#161--2026-11-20)

### Local diagnostics

The Faceplate GIF transfer test now includes a **32,767-byte** probe. If a scene failed on an earlier beta, try that scene first and let us know if it still fails.

## More handhelds, more RGB

Ambideck 1.3.0 adds screen-following RGB implementations for Lenovo Legion Go/Go S/Go 2, MSI Claw, compatible AYANEO/AYN Loki/Zotac Zone kernel LEDs, and selected OneXPlayer/OneXFly/AOKZOE models.

- Colours adapt to the available lighting zones: four corners, left/right colours or one shared colour.
- Devices without a native rainbow use one static colour averaged from the last screen colours, with soft white before the first frame.
- Device detection, reconnect recovery and output rate limits keep lighting writes away from screen capture.
- Quick Access shows the detected device and its lighting capability. HueSync handback remains specific to Ally.

**Hardware validation is still outstanding for the new backends and output worker.** Support depends on the exact model, controller firmware/mode and available kernel interfaces. See [RGB compatibility and exclusions](https://github.com/michpalm/ambideck/blob/release/1.3.0/docs/rgb-protocols.md).

Validation: 146 Python tests passed (1 Linux-only test skipped on macOS), 66 frontend tests passed, TypeScript passed and the production bundle was verified.

### Install

In Game Mode, enable Decky Developer mode, then use **Install plugin from ZIP** with `ambideck.zip`. Existing settings are preserved.

Changes: [PR #3](https://github.com/michpalm/ambideck/pull/3).

jedirhymetrix/decky-bluetooth-order.body:
## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-11

Initial public release of **Bluetooth Order**.

### Features

- Reorders Steam's existing paired Bluetooth rows in Quick Access and Settings.
- Native order, most recently connected, name A–Z, and name Z–A modes.
- Optional connected-first priority and independently enabled menu overrides.
- Passive, persisted successful-connection history; disconnects retain recency.
- Redacted diagnostics, history reset, and one-button restoration of native order.

### Reliability and distribution

- Scoped mounted-QAM attachment with owned-reference restoration; no root reset
  or automatic service restart.
- Settings adapter recognizes verified shared Decky renderer-patch chains.
- Stale panels disable their controls and explain how to reopen after updating.
- Bounded backend waits, render-loop regressions, isolated QAM session tracking,
  and a hash-checked XML fallback for Decky's frozen Python runtime.
- Immediate observer shutdown skips subscription/retry work when cancellation
  races a completed connection on Python 3.11.
- Complete ESM release ZIP, pinned dependencies, checksums, and CI/release checks.

### Verification and known limits

- User confirmed QAM and Settings working on the tested Deck with Decky 3.2.10.
- Automated frontend, backend, and packaging tests cover sorting, lifecycle,
  observer behavior, archive safety, and release metadata.
- Connection history starts with observed transitions; it cannot reconstruct
  earlier use. Fresh installs default both overrides off.
- Steam UI changes and other plugins' route patches can affect attachment.
  Every TabMaster registration order is not verified.
- Interaction can hold visible ordering. Exact QAM unload restoration can remount
  native rows on a later render. Full boot/resume acceptance remains incomplete.

For installation, privacy, and rollback instructions, see the repository README.
```

nukeador/deckyup.name: v0.2.4

lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.name: v1.7.10
lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.body:
This release fixes Steam's in-game Media and Decky settings pages closing while AlarMe is installed, and makes the in-game overlay easier to place and read.

### Highlights

- **In-game pages fixed**
  - With AlarMe installed, opening Media or Decky settings from the Steam button no longer closes them, and the volume keys no longer make them flash. AlarMe only asks Steam to draw its overlay while the overlay or screensaver needs to be shown.
  - The modal layering override now applies only while the screensaver is showing.
- **Overlay placement**
  - Settings → Overlay → Position has an Anchor dropdown: top left, top center, top right, bottom left, bottom center, or bottom right. Offsets are measured from the chosen edge, and the center anchors take an offset from the middle.
  - Existing overlays keep their top-left position.
- **Overlay text color**
  - Settings → Overlay → Appearance has a Text color picker with a reset. The default grey is unchanged.
- **Overlay no longer fades**
  - The in-game overlay moves a few pixels for burn-in protection without fading out. The screensaver keeps its fade.

### Notes

- If Steam's Media or Decky settings pages still close in a game, restart Steam once after updating.

  - The sleep inhibitor device is cleaned up on plugin unload and on setup failure.
- **Screensaver on/off and profiles**
  - The per-item Screensaver toggles (timers, alarms, reminders, stopwatch, Pomodoro) and Standalone mode are now the on/off switches; the global "Off" background mode is gone. Existing "Off" setups migrate to Dim with item toggles turned off, so nothing new appears.
  - A Profile picker under…

This release ships optional screensaver weather, OLED-safe drift for static daily wallpapers, and a rework of in-game overlay composition so Quick Access stays usable over a running game.

### Highlights

- **Screensaver weather**

lemossilva/alarme-decky-plugin.name: v1.7.2

This release improves Screensaver 2.0 usability and wallpaper handling, with a focus on faster activation and clearer controls.

### Highlights

- **Wallpaper prefetch and cache flow revamped**
  - Wallpapers are prefetched into runtime cache before activation, reducing loading delays when screensaver opens.
  - Provider cache paths and local folder paths are now visible in settings.

  - Rotation now runs in random shuffled cycles.
  - Pool-size changes are debounced to avoid repeated downloads while dragging the slider.

outpox/bluetooth.name: v3.1.0
outpox/bluetooth.body:
Fixes from the 3.0.0 testing round. Thanks to @zomars, @jwhitlow45 and @paulverbeke for the reports.

### Interface

- the device row now refreshes once the connect or disconnect really finishes, instead of straight away

- labels reuse Steam's own localized strings where they exist

### Backend

- D-Bus error replies are detected and logged instead of being read as data. This is what made the battery read as `o`, and it could…

moyoez/decky-localsend.name: v0.45.2
moyoez/decky-localsend.body:
Fixes interoperability with the official LocalSend CLI and reduces memory use when sending large files from the Deck.

- Use the existing device certificate for outgoing HTTPS requests and advertise its complete fingerprint. This fixes discovery and transfers with LocalSend CLI 1.18.2.
- Stream batch uploads from disk instead of loading each whole file into memory.
- Keep multi-file transfers in file history when the last completed file is a text file.
- Update Sonic to 1.15.5 and its loader to 0.5.3; builds checked with Go 1.25.7 and 1.26.3.

Verified on a Steam Deck with Decky 3.3.1: official CLI transfers in both directions, Chinese filenames, 1 MiB and 64 MiB files, and a 32-file text batch. Received file contents were compared byte for byte. The 64 MiB send sample used 29.6 MiB peak RSS, down from 93.8 MiB in the compatibility-only build. Transfer times were 1.20 s and 1.15 s respectively; this is a memory reduction, not a claimed speedup.

Both amd64 and arm64 backends are included. ARM64 was cross-compiled but not tested on hardware. Existing settings and certificates are retained; the corrected full fingerprint may cause a peer to rediscover the Deck.

Install or update using `decky-localsend.zip`. The tag and package version are both 0.45.2.

cat-in-a-box/decky-translator.name: Decky Translator 0.9.1
cat-in-a-box/decky-translator.body:
## Translation cache

The plugin can now save the sentences it has already translated and reuse them to speed up the whole process. 
Results are saved in a local database and follow the general rule - results can only be reused by the same translation engine "tier" or a weaker one

There's also a new screen where you can browse saved translations for your reference

The feature is now enabled by default, but can be turned off if you do not need it

## Initial support for Big Picture Mode (in Desktop mode)

Screen capture is no longer limited to Game Mode. The plugin now detects a working screenshot method - the regular PipeWire capture in Game Mode, KDE's Spectacle in desktop mode, or the desktop portal as a fallback and tries to work with it. 

Experimental feature, especially on non-steamos distros, but can work for someone who likes Desktop more than Game mode

## Other improvements

### Steam Controller support and more fixes for external gamepads

Plugin now works with the Steam Controller - grip buttons, stick clicks and touchpad touches can now be correctly read. 

Also added some fixes for how controllers are handled for #30. 

### Norwegian language support (Thanks @a3f!)

Norwegian is now available in the language selection and should work with all OCR and translation methods. 

### On-Device translation improvments

Handful of text-handling improvements for NLLB-200 model that should make it a bit more accurate

- Lines that are not in your source language (like English UI text in a localized game) should no longer come out as nonsense
- Casing, punctuation and wrapped lines are handled better
- Broken output (repeated words, untranslated copies of the original) is better filtered out 

### Other stuff

- The progress indicator now shows which method is doing the work ("On-Device", "Google Translate", "Gemini Vision", etc)
- Several improvements to how api keys are handled - potentially should resolve #27 or at least provide more info on why it's failing
- Manual edits to the settings file are no longer overwritten when the plugin saves a setting
- Screen capture no longer fails completely on systems missing the GStreamer PNG encoder - the plugin still grabs the raw frame and encodes it itself. Should help with #31 
- Another SteamOS update - another broken layout. Plugin UI renders correctly again
- Removed an invisible focus element at the bottom of the Translation tab

cat-in-a-box/decky-translator.name: Decky Translator 0.9
cat-in-a-box/decky-translator.body:
## Offline translation

You can now translate your games fully offline! Previously on-device recognition already worked without internet, but the new offline translation option based on Meta's NLLB-200 model makes the stack fully complete. 
One-time 1.4 GB model download is required, then it runs entirely on your Deck . 

It handles all the languages at once, so no need to install many different packages for each language pair.

The quality of translation is obviously not the same as with web-based translation, but sometimes you just dont want anyone to know what games you are translating ;) 

## Chrome Screen AI - amazing on-device recognition accuracy

A new on-device text recognition option arrived, backed by Chromium "Screen-AI" library. It runs locally like RapidOCR, but provides much better and quicker results. It is now the default OCR option for the plugin

## Gemini Vision is also available!

It handles both recognition and translation in a single API call.…

cat-in-a-box/decky-translator.name: Decky Translator 0.8
cat-in-a-box/decky-translator.body:
## Better on-device text recognition

Plugin packages got updated to the most recent version for on-device recognition - RapidOCR 3 with PP-OCRv5 models. 
Instead of one generic model trying to handle every language, it now picks the right recognition model for what you're actually translating - there are separate models for each language family. Recognition quality should be better across the board, especially for non-Latin text.

And the way the plugin groups nearby text boxes together has been completely redone, using a more accurate logic for figuring out which text regions belong together. 

**Also squashed a bug when Japanese, Korean or Chinese text was not recognizing properly.** 

Your waifu's name will now display correctly. You're welcome

## Controller support + new quick buttons (L3 and R3)

You can now trigger translations with external gamepads - Xbox, PlayStation, whatever you've got plugged in or paired over Bluetooth. 

And new L3 and R3 shortcuts…

datbird/docky.name: v1.4.11
datbird/docky.body:
Make the unload synchronous so the fan hand-back actually runs
An await inside _unload never resumes. Decky stops ticking the event loop after the stop request, so no timer fires and no thread result is collected, and the plugin is SIGKILLed at 5 seconds. Measured with a probe writing to a file: execution reached the first await and sat there until the kill, even with a 2 second timeout on a call whose work takes 0.02 seconds. The 1.4.10 timeouts bounded nothing. _unload now hands the fan back inline, cancels the watchers and returns without awaiting. Measured on the Deck with jupiter-fan-control stopped first: unload returns in 0.031 seconds and Decky reports stopped in 0.1s with no SIGKILL, against 5.1 seconds before.

nikitaclicks/decky-multi-user.name: v1.1.1
nikitaclicks/decky-multi-user.body:
## Fix

Fixes #2 — "Switch User & Play" button not showing for some games.

The button's visibility previously relied on stale local-file heuristics:

- `LastOwner` in the appmanifest actually tracks the last account that *launched* the game, not the license owner. If the current user ever launched a borrowed/shared game once, they became `LastOwner` and the button disappeared permanently.
- Hiding the button when the current user had `PlayTime > 0` for the game ("played before") does not mean they can play it now.

Neither signal can distinguish "owns the license" from "played once while borrowing", which caused the button to be missing for games owned by other local accounts (including the inconsistent behavior with family-shared games).

The plugin now asks the Steam client directly:

- `appDetailsStore.GetAppDetails` → `bIsSubscribedTo` + `eAppOwnershipFlags` (`Borrowed` bit) for the current user's actual license status
- `SteamClient.FamilySharing.GetAvailableLenders` → the accounts that actually own the game's license, used to pick the switch target

The button now shows whenever the current user doesn't hold their own license (no license at all, or borrowing via family sharing) and another local account can be offered. Target priority: license owner → manifest `LastOwner` (only if it isn't you) → installer → another local user who played the game.

# SuggestMe v1.5.1 - Release Notes

## Bug Fixes

### Release Date Filter Incorrect Results (#29)
Fixed an issue where games released outside the specified date range could still appear in suggestions. The filter now correctly falls back to the cached `release_date` from the library when the live Steam client data is unavailable.

bkohler616/tunneldeck.name: BUILD-1.0.4
bkohler616/tunneldeck.body:
## What's Changed
* Add prioritized network information by @bkohler616 in https://github.com/bkohler616/TunnelDeck/pull/3

We will now display what is considered the prioritized network that will be used (via TCP/IP pings to steampowered.com)

How do we determine that? 
1. Collect the steam IP (getent ahosts steampowered.com)
2. ask the OS how it would route that call (ip route get <steam_ip>).
3. collecting the device used from ip route, that is what is considered the "priority interface".

Why do we want that?
It is not easily available to determine if the VPN is working or not, even in normal desktop mode. But at least in desktop mode you could go to a browser and ask it what your IP is, or what your geolocation is.

Because we don't have a browser (easily) available, having this all in the plugin to determine "is my VPN working" helps with informing you if it works at all quite a bit easier, without having to go too far outside of your way to debug issues.

---…

b-ostrov/hiddify-steam-deck-vpn.name: v1.3.18 — refresh over VPN + installer taskbar fix
b-ostrov/hiddify-steam-deck-vpn.body:
## Stable release: refresh over VPN + installer taskbar fix

Promotes `v1.3.18.1-beta` after successful Steam Deck testing with no regressions. Adds **update servers while the VPN is connected** (the long-requested [#13](https://github.com/denmrnngp-cloud/hiddify-steam-deck-vpn/issues/13) catch-22 for geo-blocked users) and fixes the **installer hiding buttons under the taskbar** ([#12](https://github.com/denmrnngp-cloud/hiddify-steam-deck-vpn/issues/12)).

Thanks again to everyone who tested the betas — especially the on-device verification of the zero-drop reload.

### Added

- **Update servers while the VPN is connected (#13).** Pressing the ↻ refresh button while connected now downloads the subscription **through the active tun0** and **hot-applies the new servers immediately with no VPN drop**. sing-box reloads via its Clash-compatible control API (`PUT /configs?force=true` on `127.0.0.1:16756`) without tearing down the TUN interface — verified on sing-box 1.13.1, `tun0` stayed UP across the reload. This finally solves the geo-blocked catch-22 (a subscription that is only reachable through the VPN itself): you can refresh it *while* the VPN is up and the new servers take effect right away. The toast reports the real status: *“Servers updated and applied: N”* when applied live, *“Servers updated: N”* when applied offline.
- **Rollback safety.** The previous `current-config.json` is backed up before the reload. If the Clash reload fails or `tun0` drops, the backup is restored and reloaded so the active session keeps working — toast: *“Update downloaded, but hot-reload failed — reverted to the previous config.”*

### Fixed

- **Installer no longer hides buttons under the taskbar (#12).** On SteamOS, `Gdk.Monitor.get_workarea()` returns the full screen (the compositor does not expose panel positions to clients), so neither workarea-based sizing nor `maximize()` alone can keep the window clear of a taskbar on an arbitrary side. The Already-Installed window’s Reinstall/Uninstall radio list is now wrapped in a `ScrolledWindow`, so Next/Cancel stay reachable at the bottom of the window regardless of which side the panel is on. Both windows are also `maximize()`d so KWin places them inside its real work area when it can.

### Preserved

- v1.3.17’s server-selector pills, the v1.3.16 HTTPS subscription-download fix (SteamOS CA bundle), the controller-first `Focusable` focus highlight, and all SteamOS authorization fixes for DNS/domain/default-route changes after reinstall or reboot.

> ⚠️ Requires **Decky Loader 3.2.6+** — v1.3.16+ uses the Decky `Focusable` component for gamepad focus, which is undefined on Decky 3.2.3 and crashes the QAM with React error #130. If you’re on Decky 3.2.3, update Decky first, then install this release.

### Install (from Konsole, Desktop Mode)

```bash
cd ~/Downloads
curl -L -o Hiddify-linux-x64-v1.3.18.bin \
  https://github.com/denmrnngp-cloud/hiddify-steam-deck-vpn/releases/download/v1.3.18/Hiddify-linux-x64-v1.3.18.bin
chmod +x Hiddify-linux-x64-v1.3.18.bin
bash ~/Downloads/Hiddify-linux-x64-v1.3.18.bin
```

Manual plugin-only install (debug):

```bash
cd ~/Downloads
curl -L -o decky-hiddify-v1.3.18.zip \
  https://github.com/denmrnngp-cloud/hiddify-steam-deck-vpn/releases/download/v1.3.18/decky-hiddify-v1.3.18.zip
sudo rm -rf /home/deck/homebrew/plugins/decky-hiddify
sudo unzip -o decky-hiddify-v1.3.18.zip -d /home/deck/homebrew/plugins/
sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader
```

**Assets**
- `Hiddify-linux-x64-v1.3.18.bin` — full installer
- `decky-hiddify-v1.3.18.zip` — Decky plugin bundle (manual/debug install)

## v1.3.17-beta — Game Mode server selector polish

### What's new

It now uses the same compact `Focusable` pills as the profile row — green active dot, white active pill, gamepad focus highlight, `Hiddify default · auto` plus one pill per server with a type badge.

- **Fixed duplicated toasts/actions.** Decky `Focusable` fires both `onActivate` and `onClick` on one gamepad press, so refresh / switch-profile / switch-server ran twice. Added a per-control dedupe guard.

b-ostrov/hiddify-steam-deck-vpn.body:
## Game Mode subscription refresh — update your servers without leaving Steam

This release adds a **server update button** to the Decky plugin, implementing the feature requested in #8.

Huge thanks to **@SRMUFA01** for filing the request with a clear HAPP example, and for the continued Steam Deck testing. 🙌

### ⭐ New: refresh subscription from Game Mode (#8)

- New circular **↻ refresh button** next to each remote profile. It re-downloads the latest subscription and rebuilds the server list **without leaving Game Mode** — handy when your VPN starts to slow down and you just want fresh servers.
- The button appears only for remote (subscription) profiles, and is disabled while the VPN is connected so it never mutates a live config.

### 🔒 Fixed: HTTPS subscription download (CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED)

- Decky runs the plugin on its own bundled Python, which did not resolve the SteamOS system CA store — so HTTPS subscription downloads failed TLS verification.

hooandee/decky-colores.body:
### Novedades

- **ROG Xbox Ally:** El aro del joystick derecho ya no se queda en azul o apagado cuando el sistema repinta las luces. Colores vuelve a poner tu color en los dos aros, también con efectos y Ambilight.
- **Ambilight y el modo de audio vuelven a arrancar:** En algunos sistemas no llegaban a empezar y las luces se quedaban quietas. Ahora funcionan.

### What's new

- **ROG Xbox Ally:** The right joystick ring no longer stays blue or dark when the system repaints the lights. Colores puts your color back on both rings, with effects and Ambilight too.
- **Ambilight and audio mode start again:** On some systems they never started and the lights stayed still. They work now.

### Novità

- **ROG Xbox Ally:** L'anello dello stick destro non resta più blu o spento quando il sistema ridipinge le luci. Colores rimette il tuo colore su entrambi gli anelli, anche con gli effetti e Ambilight.
- **Ambilight e la modalità audio ripartono:** Su alcuni sistemi non si avviavano e le luci restavano ferme. Ora funzionano.

### Neuigkeiten

- **ROG Xbox Ally:** Der rechte Stick-Ring bleibt nicht mehr blau oder dunkel, wenn das System die Beleuchtung neu setzt. Colores setzt deine Farbe auf beiden Ringen wieder, auch mit Effekten und Ambilight.
- **Ambilight und Audiomodus starten wieder:** Auf manchen Systemen starteten sie gar nicht, und die Beleuchtung blieb stehen. Jetzt funktionieren sie.

### Novidades em português (Brasil)

- **ROG Xbox Ally:** O anel do analógico direito não fica mais azul ou apagado quando o sistema repinta as luzes. O Colores volta a colocar sua cor nos dois anéis, também com efeitos e Ambilight.
- **O Ambilight e o modo de áudio voltam a funcionar:** Em alguns sistemas eles nem chegavam a começar e as luzes ficavam paradas. Agora funcionam.

### Nouveautés

- **ROG Xbox Ally :** L'anneau du joystick droit ne reste plus bleu ou éteint quand le système redessine l'éclairage. Colores remet votre couleur sur les deux anneaux, y compris avec les effets et Ambilight.
- **Ambilight et le mode audio redémarrent :** Sur certains systèmes, ils ne démarraient pas et l'éclairage restait figé. Ils fonctionnent maintenant.

twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.name: v0.1.27
twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.body:
## Remote Play Protection

- Adds an optional Decky toggle that detects active Steam Remote Play sessions from Steam's local streaming log.
- Suppresses toolkit CEC wake/input switching and Gamescope Recovery while a stream is active.
- Restores normal local controller input switching when the stream ends.
- Preserves an enabled Remote Play Protection monitor across reinstall/update.

## Gamescope Recovery

- Makes clear that recovery restarts the active Game Mode session and can end local games or streams.
- Remote Play Protection prevents recovery from interrupting an active Steam Remote Play session.

twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.name: v0.1.26
twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.body:
## Changes
- Add configurable SteamOS sleep/shutdown CEC action.
- Default remains HDMI-CEC Standby for existing behavior.
- Add Inactive Source mode for TVs that cold-boot or hard shutdown on CEC Standby.
- Expose Sleep TV Action in the Decky plugin configuration.
- Keep CEC Volume Buttons reboot caveat documented: reboot once after enabling/disabling before judging Quick Settings UI.

## Validation
- Tested on martin-steambox regression flow.
- npm run build passed.
- bash syntax checks passed.
- Python compile check passed.
- git diff --check passed.

twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.name: v0.1.25
twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.body:
## Changes

- Fix CEC volume addressing so the normal path uses the SteamOS adapter logical address with kernel validation instead of raw spoofing by default.
- Preserve explicit TV-originated spoofing for receivers/soundbars that require it.
- Fall back to TV logical address 0 for TV-speaker setups when no Audio System is present.
- Add optional LG SIMPLINK handshake support for LG TVs that ignore standard CEC volume keys.
- Add Decky configuration for Auto Volume Initiator and LG SIMPLINK Handshake.
- Update installer output, README, and troubleshooting docs for the new volume setup.

## Validation

- Tested existing receiver/soundbar spoof path on a Panasonic TV + Audio System setup: 0 -> 5 still transmits correctly.
- Tested Auto path on the same setup: Playback Device -> Audio System transmits correctly.
- bash syntax checks passed.
- Python compile check passed.
- Decky build passed.
- Release asset checksums verified.

twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.name: v0.1.24
twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.body:
Release v0.1.24

- Improves CEC wake/input activation after SteamOS resume by restarting and waiting for SteamOS cecd, calling cecd Wake, and keeping raw CEC active-source fallback.
- Logs raw CEC send failures during resume instead of hiding them.
- Adds configurable resume cecd settle/restart settings.
- Improves installer progress output around CEC audio and WirePlumber restart.
- Documents Bluetooth wake troubleshooting for systems that resume to ping-only/no display/no SSH.

twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.name: v0.1.23
twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.body:
Hotfix and installer UX update.

Changes:
- Fix SteamOS Start Wakes TV toggle in the Decky plugin. It now enables/disables the boot-wake oneshot for the next session start instead of starting the CEC retry loop immediately from the toggle.
- Add clearer install progress output after sudo, including root helpers, systemd/udev files, sudo permissions, ExternalVolume, user services, CEC permissions, selected services, and audio restart.

This avoids the previous timeout/error when enabling SteamOS Start Wakes TV from the plugin.

twsts/steamos-cec-toolkit.body: Experimental prerelease, not recommended. This build tested a dedicated resume-wake service and was pulled back after suspend/resume instability during real HTPC testing. Use the latest stable release instead, currently v0.1.17. Main has been reverted to remove this experiment.

featherwolf/enhancedgv.name: EnhancedGV v0.21.0
featherwolf/enhancedgv.body:
- **Artwork for non-Steam games, with no setup.** Games matched through
  Hasheous now get IGDB's cover art, screenshots, genres, developers and
  release dates through EnhancedGV's own Hasheous app. IGDB credentials are now
  optional, and only a fallback: the app answers first.
- **Updates from Quick Access.** When a new version is out, press **Update**
  in Quick Access and confirm in Decky's dialog. The plugin reloads without a
  Steam restart. **Install another version** offers every release from 0.20.0
  on, stable or beta. Each download is checked against the checksum GitHub
  recorded for it before Decky installs anything. Needs Decky Loader 3.0 or
  later.
- **A tidier Quick Access panel.** It's much shorter. Section choices and older
  versions open in their own dialogs. The match editor and IGDB account fold
  away until you need them. Diagnostics sit behind one switch.
- **Portuguese (Brazil) interface.** EnhancedGV's own menus and labels now come
  in Brazilian Portuguese too. They follow your Steam language, or you can pick
  one under **Language** in Quick Access. Store content still follows Steam.
  Contributed by @btd1337.
- **Update history for Switch games.** Non-Steam Switch games now show the
  changes from their three newest releases, from perfectly-nintendo.com, with a
  link to the full article. Contributed by @btd1337.
- **Emulated games matched on the right system.** EnhancedGV now reads which
  system a non-Steam game is for from its shortcut (the ROM's file type, its
  ROM folder or the emulator) and only accepts IGDB and Hasheous listings on
  that system. A Game Boy ROM gets the Game Boy game, not its Color remake, and
  a Switch game is no longer matched to a Game Boy dump, a rom hack or a
  soundtrack. Automatic matches made before are checked again once; ones you
  set yourself are left alone. Quick Access → This game shows the system.

  EnhancedGV's Hasheous app searches IGDB itself, so games Hasheous' ROM index
  lacks (Kirby and the Forgotten Land, Metroid Dread) are found with no setup.
  A saved IGDB account is now only the fallback, for finding games and for
  their artwork. An edition or add-on found instead of the game itself (Super
  Smash Bros. Ultimate's Special Edition box) leads to the game.
- **Steam's newest beta.** Steam rebuilt its interface in its latest beta, and
  EnhancedGV can't yet find where to place its panel there. Instead of quietly
  showing nothing, Quick Access now says so. Steam's Stable channel is
  unaffected.
- **Fullscreen trailers no longer break Big Picture.** On Windows and Linux
  desktops, leaving a fullscreen trailer or screenshot used to drop Big Picture
  into a normal window until Steam was restarted. Fullscreen media now fills
  Big Picture's screen without touching its window, on every system, the Steam
  Deck included. Y or B leaves fullscreen, and so does Esc.
- **Smaller fixes.** Very long paragraphs in update history scroll with the
  D-pad; Quick Access no longer asks GitHub for updates every time it opens;
  games matched straight to IGDB load with one request instead of two.

starkka15/gamevault.name: v1.4.1 — fixes EA and Ubisoft games on Steam's new client
starkka15/gamevault.body:
## Fixes games failing to launch after Steam's 64-bit client update

Steam's new 64-bit client (rolling out to SteamOS now) changed how a game's compatibility tool is cleared. GameVault cleared it the old way when it installed a game or when you used **Reset Launch Options**. On the new client that *assigned* Steam's default Proton instead, so stores that run their own launcher (EA Play through Maxima, Ubisoft through Optima) were wrapped in a second Proton and the game never started.

GameVault now leaves the compatibility setting alone for those games. A game that was never given a tool runs directly on every Steam client, old or new. The old clearing call is only sent when the game actually has a tool assigned, which still works on older clients.

**If a game already stopped launching:** restart Steam once, then use **Reset Launch Options** on it. If you picked a compatibility tool for it yourself in Steam, the new client can't set it back to "none" through any API, so a Steam restart is what clears it.

Also: when no default Proton is configured, games that need Proton fall back to *Proton Stable* instead of failing. That code path called a Steam function the new client removed.

## Related updates
- **EA Play extension:** Maxima [v0.14.4](https://github.com/Starkka15/Maxima/releases/tag/v0.14.4) fixes `unrecognized subcommand 'register-install'` launch failures. Update the EA extension, or reinstall it, from **About → Extensions** to pick it up.
- **Ubisoft extension 1.1.0:** sign in on Ubisoft's real login page in Steam's browser, with Ubisoft Connect set up for you. Update it from **About → Extensions**.

## Hide the store tabs you don't use

Adds **About → Store Tabs**, with a toggle for each store. Turn off the ones you
don't use and they leave the tab bar — handy on a TV, where every extra tab is
another R1 press.

Hiding is presentation only. A hidden store keeps its login, its installed games
and its Steam shortcuts, and comes back unchanged when you turn it on again.

- Defaults to everything visible, so existing installs are unaffected.
- A newly installed store appears on its own rather than arriving hidden.
- Turning every tab off falls back to showing them all, so you can't strand

is not included in this release.

### Under the hood

Tab visibility is keyed on each tab's `ActionId`, not its title or position. The
tab bar previously remembered the active tab by array index, so filtering the
list would silently move you to a different store; tabs are now keyed by…

- Offline Hotspot: A friend request with no lobby connection is held. It then goes through once you share a room or the next time both connect via the lobby server.
- Removed the "Was this you?" new-device alert.
- When the host of a room selects Host & Play and the guests aren't readied up, a notification dialog is shown with the warning. It can be turned off right from the dialog if the host no longer wants to see the warning, and turned back on in **Options > Play Together > Show Ready Notification**.

- Added a Mapped Shortcut and a Quick Menu shortcut for Play Together. This can be configured in Options if you wish to map it to a button or add it to the Quick Menu.
- Play Together is no longer listed in Utilities, as it's more of a full flagship feature now than a utility or tool. It remains accessible through Notifications (accessed via the bell in the upper right corner) or the above methods.

- A new friend shows no status until it's known instead of showing the "Offline" placeholder.
- The "1 new" message badge lines up with the text above it when a friend's name wraps in the Play Together Friends tab.
- Fixed a flickering issue with the friend request buttons.
- Fixed unnecessary mounting and unmounting of the QAM panel during the first-time message that shows for Play Together upon entering.

danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler.name: v0.0.7
danielcamilo1/decky-optiscaler.body:
FSR 4 on the Steam Deck, and the compatibility list is whole again.

### Added

- **FSR 4.1.1b — Steam Deck**, in the Basic upscaler dropdown. One choice
  downloads the community RDNA 2 build of the FidelityFX upscaler, checks it
  against a hash pinned in the plugin, puts it next to the game and switches on
  the INT8 override that reaches FSR 4 on RDNA 2. Close the game first; it
  applies on the next launch. Frame generation is left exactly as it was.
  Thanks to [@drewboardman](https://github.com/drewboardman), who built this and
  tested it on a Deck.
- Setup names which upscaler build is in the game folder, identified by its bytes
  rather than its version — the community build reports the same 4.1.1 the
  released SDK does — and will put the bundled one back.

### Fixed

- **297 of the 695 games on the compatibility list were answering "no wiki entry
  matched".** One row on the wiki was saved without its leading `|`, which the
  parser read as the end of the table, so everything after Metro Exodus was
  invisible: Monster Hunter Wilds, the Resident Evil entries, Stalker 2, The
  Witcher 3 and 293 others. A row that lost its first character is now read as
  the row it is. Bundled list regenerated — 698 entries.
- Games listed under *Upscaler mods support* and *Luma Unreal Engine* no longer
  claim OptiPatcher support they do not have, and their notes are their notes
  rather than the images column. Those two tables have one column fewer than the
  main one, and were being read as though they did not.
- The refreshed list adds Onimusha: Way of the Sword to the games that need
  REFramework in place before OptiScaler can do anything.
- All six FSR 4 quality presets are offered. The reference INI writes them as one
  comma-separated line, of which two were being read, so Quality, Performance,
  DRS and Ultra Performance were rejected by the settings writer and never
  reached the file.
- Choosing an FSR version on RDNA 2 no longer turns on the FSR 4 upgrade path.
  That path forces the FP8 model, which such a GPU does not have, and OptiScaler
  answers with a silent FSR 3 fallback.
- Verification recognises a community upscaler by hash, and reinstalling keeps it
  instead of overwriting it with the bundled build.
- Replacing the upscaler is atomic and rolls back the DLL, the INI and the
  manifest together if any part of it fails. It refuses while the game is
  running, and on an install this plugin did not make.
