# Decky EnvTest - Release Notes

## Version 1.0b

 - Initial Release 🚀

### Overview

Decky EnvTest is a debugging tool for Decky that logs game-specific details from Decky's SteamClient.Apps and extracts Heroic configuration data. This first release provides essential logging and data extraction capabilities, making it easier to analyze game environment details within Decky.

### Features

- ✅ **Game Data Logging** – Retrieves and logs detailed information about installed Steam games.
- ✅ **Heroic Data Retrieval** – Fetches and filters configuration details from Heroic.
- ✅ **Clean Data Display** – Removes unnecessary fields and presents a structured, readable format.
- ✅ **Export JSON Data** – Save logged game data as a JSON file for offline inspection.
- ✅ **Decky Integration** – Works seamlessly within Decky UI with minimal setup.

1. **Install ZIP or from URL in Developer Settings** from the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/wowitsjack/deckyloader-envtest/releases).

3. **Restart Decky** and access the plugin via the UI.

1. Open the **Decky EnvTest** plugin from Decky.

4. Use **Export JSON** to download the log data.

### Known Issues

- 🔹 Some non-Steam games may not appear in the logged data.
- 🔹 Heroic data may be unavailable if the game is not configured in Heroic.

### Future Improvements

- 📌 Support for additional game platforms.
- 📌 More filtering and search capabilities.

### Acknowledgements

- Thanks to the **Decky Team** for their great plugin platform.

hrhnick/decky-romsync.name: ROM Sync 1.9.0
hrhnick/decky-romsync.body:
Turns a ROM folder into Steam shortcuts with artwork and per-system
collections. Runs inside Game Mode, uses Valve's own React components, and
never touches `shortcuts.vdf`.

## Installing

ROM Sync is not in the Decky plugin store yet, so install is manual:

1. Install [Decky Loader](https://decky.xyz) if you do not have it.
2. QAM → **Decky** → gear icon → **General** → turn on **Developer Mode**.
3. Download the `ROM-Sync-*.zip` attached below, onto the Deck itself.
4. Decky settings → **Developer** → **Install Plugin from ZIP File**, and pick
   the archive.

Full instructions, including a Desktop Mode fallback, are in the
[README](https://github.com/hrhnick/decky-romsync#installing).

## What is in the archive

The seven files that run on device — `plugin.json`, `package.json`, the four
Python modules and the compiled `dist/index.js` — inside a single `ROM Sync/`
folder. TypeScript sources and build config are not included; build them with
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm run build`.

## Notes

- Everything defers to the next Sync. Toggling a system, excluding a ROM or
  changing a core takes effect then, not immediately — removing a shortcut
  discards its Steam playtime and cannot be undone, so a mis-tap costs nothing.
- Shortcuts already imported by Steam ROM Manager are adopted rather than
  duplicated.
- Artwork needs a SteamGridDB key, set on the Settings page. Without one the
  sync still runs; art is filled in on a later sync once a key is present.

feelsrat/decky-task-manager.name: Decky Task Manager v0.1.20
feelsrat/decky-task-manager.body:
## New UI
- Compact tab bar with badges for running plugins and plugins with problems
- **Overview:** health summary, CPU/RAM tiles with recent history, live/snapshot freshness, a needs-attention list and top plugins that jump straight to details or logs, plus a Refresh button when live monitoring is off
- **Plugins:** grouped into running, idle and disabled. Select one to see current vs peak CPU/RAM and Disable/Enable, Stop and Logs buttons
- **Logs:** plugins ranked by severity. Select one to see known problems, the most frequent error lines and how fast the log is growing
- Confirmation dialogs before disabling, stopping, clearing all logs, starting a fresh capture or installing an update
- Buttons are native Steam buttons laid out for D-pad navigation, so they work with the physical controls
- Problems already showing when you open the panel no longer pop up as alerts; several new ones are combined into one

## Fixes
- **Security:** update checks and downloads now verify HTTPS certificates (verification was previously turned off while installing as root)
- Plugins that stop running no longer stay listed as active with old CPU/RAM values
- Log scanning matches exact plugin folder/file names, so one plugin no longer picks up (or clears) another plugin's logs
- A failed update check is no longer cached for 24 hours
- Enabling/disabling a plugin writes Decky's loader.json atomically and keeps its ownership

## Performance
- Live monitoring reads the plugin list once per sample instead of five times, and scans the log folder once per pass

sauliiin/jedi-lsfg-vk.body:
## O que mudou

- **A atualização pelo plugin agora funciona.** Na 1.2.0, tocar em **Update** (ou no aviso de versão nova) não fazia nada: a janela de confirmação do Decky abria atrás do menu de acesso rápido e nunca aparecia. Agora o próprio plugin baixa a versão nova, confere o checksum, baixa o MAKO se faltar, se instala e pede ao Decky para recarregá-lo. Não há mais janela para confirmar.
- Se algo der errado no meio (download, checksum, arquivo sem permissão), nada é sobrescrito e o plugin continua na versão atual, com uma mensagem dizendo o que aconteceu.

## Instalação

1. Baixe o **Jedi LSFG-VK.zip** abaixo.
2. No Decky: **Developer Mode** → **Developer → Install Plugin from Zip**.
3. Abra o plugin e toque em **Install MAKO Renderer**.

Quem tem a 1.2.0 precisa instalar esta versão por cima uma vez pelo mesmo caminho, porque o botão de update da 1.2.0 é justamente o que não funcionava. A partir desta versão, as próximas atualizações se instalam pelo próprio plugin.

---

**English:** the Update button and the update toast did nothing in 1.2.0, because Decky's install prompt opens behind the Quick Access menu. The plugin now downloads the release, checks its SHA-256, fetches a missing MAKO archive, installs itself and asks Decky to reload it. If anything fails, nothing is overwritten. Install this version from ZIP once; later updates install from the plugin.

## O que mudou

- **O FPS alvo agora é um mínimo, não um teto.** Antes, o jogo ficava limitado à metade do alvo. Agora os FPS reais nunca são limitados: se o jogo roda a 65 FPS com alvo de 60, você vê os 65 reais, sem frames gerados. Abaixo do alvo, a geração só completa os frames que faltam, até 4x.
- **Fim do travamento em 15 FPS.** Com alvo de 30, o jogo ficava preso em 15 FPS reais, e quando a geração de frames não entrava ele ficava nisso. Agora, se a geração não entrar, o jogo roda nos FPS normais dele.
- **FPS alvo de 60 a 120.** Perfis antigos com alvo abaixo de 60 passam para 60 automaticamente.
- **Volta para os frames reais quando o jogo melhora.** A cada 3 segundos, o plugin confere se o jogo já consegue rodar mais rápido sozinho e reduz a geração quando consegue.
- **Perfis antigos são atualizados sozinhos** quando o plugin carrega, antes de qualquer jogo abrir.

Sem o limite, o jogo renderiza tudo o que consegue, então a GPU trabalha mais e a bateria pode durar menos em…

# StripMine v0.1.1

StripMine v0.1.1 turns the Steam Machine's 17-LED light bar into a persistent mining city while improving the full-screen game, Decky control room and integration with SignalBar.

## Highlights

- Cooperative LED ownership with SignalBar v0.7.1 for Artwork, Performance, Weather, Controller displays and Light Events.
- A complete **Exit Game** lifecycle that saves and parks the campaign, releases the physical bar, stops the game worker and audio, and returns to the Steam library.
- A full-screen layout fitted to Decky's real 16:9 route area without scrolling or bottom cropping.
- A denser 512 x 384 Dot Matrix with five rotating story cards.
- Improved worker animation, pickaxe proportions, impact timing, reward sounds and television-scale action labels.
- Music and SFX enabled by default, with independent persistent volume controls.

## Install

StripMine requires [Decky Loader](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader#-installation).

1. Open **Decky Settings**.
2. Under **General**, enable **Developer mode** only if the **Developer** section is not already visible.
3. Open **Developer**, choose **Install Plugin from URL**, and paste:

   `https://github.com/Albusquerque/StripMine/releases/download/v0.1.1/StripMine-v0.1.1.zip`

Alternatively, download `StripMine-v0.1.1.zip` from this release and select it with **Install Plugin from ZIP File**. Do not extract the archive and do not use GitHub's automatically generated source archives.

If StripMine does not immediately appear, reload or restart Decky Loader, or reboot the device. Then open **Quick Access (`…`) > Decky > StripMine > Open Full Game**.

## Hardware note

The package, ownership protocol and automated tests are validated off-device. Physical LED direction, diffuser behaviour and long-duration coexistence still require confirmation on the target Steam Machine.

catvitalio/shoehorn.name: Shoehorn v0.1.1
catvitalio/shoehorn.body:
Install mods and fan translations into your Steam games without leaving Gaming Mode.

A mod almost always ships as a Windows `setup.exe` that wants to write into the game's own
folder. Shoehorn runs it inside that game's Proton prefix, straight from the couch: pick
the game, pick the installer, press Run. The installer opens on screen like any other
game, and leaves your library again when you close it.

## Install on SteamOS

Turn on **Developer mode** in Decky's settings, open the **Developer** tab and use
**Install from URL**:

```
https://github.com/catvitalio/shoehorn/releases/latest/download/Shoehorn.zip
```

On NixOS, add the flake instead — see the [README](https://github.com/catvitalio/shoehorn#nixos).

## What you need

- [Decky Loader](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader)
- The game installed, and launched at least once, so Steam has created its Windows
  environment

The plugin follows your SteamOS language and reads the language the installer was written
for, so its text stays readable instead of turning into mojibake.

## Changes since v0.1.0

- The check for whether a game's prefix is still in use no longer requires `fcntl` to be
  present in Decky's bundled interpreter: it is imported where it is used, and the plugin
  loads either way.

snakethedev/decky-capture.name: v0.1.0 - experimental test build
snakethedev/decky-capture.body:
## Test build - experimental, never run on hardware

**Every line of code in this release was written by an AI coding agent**
(**OpenCode**, model `Space Bunny Free`). There is no human-written code in it.

It has **never been run on a Steam Deck.** No gadget has been created, no frame
captured, no host enumerated. 61 unit tests pass.

### What it does

Turns the Deck into a USB camera, so another machine sees the Deck's screen over
one cable. No capture hardware, and nothing installed on the host.

```
Deck screen ──DRM──▶ ffmpeg ──MJPEG──▶ /dev/videoN ──USB──▶ host
```

The same trick the controller emulation uses, one USB class up: a configfs
gadget with a `uvc.0` function instead of `hid.0`. A host with a capture-card app
— Meta Quest's HDMI Link, for one — will then show what this streams.

MJPEG only, and that is what makes it possible at all: YUYV at 1080p is about
186 MB/s and does not fit USB 2.0, while MJPEG is roughly 4 MB/s.

### Three unknowns, in the order you will hit them

1. **Game Mode will not work.** `kmsreadout` needs the DRM master and gamescope
   owns it. **Exit to desktop mode first.**
2. **The host may refuse a bare UVC webcam.** Meta's docs say "UVC and UAC
   compatible capture card", which is not quite the same thing. This gadget has
   no EDID and no HDMI identity.
3. **The kernel may not ship the UVC gadget module.** First thing to check:
   `lsmod | grep uvc`. If `g_webcam` is missing, nothing else matters.

### If it does enumerate

The plugin reports the negotiated link speed, because that decides whether
better compression could ever be viable. `High (USB 2.0)` is expected;
`SuperSpeed` would be a surprise worth reporting.

### If you report a problem

The plugin log at `~/homebrew/logs/decky-capture/` is the most useful thing,
along with `lsmod | grep -E 'uvc|libcomposite'` and `cat
/sys/class/udc/*/speed`.

annacode747/deck-web-terminal.name: v1.1.0
annacode747/deck-web-terminal.body:
**Type a path in the file panel.** `/` in the panel's top bar (or `Ctrl+L`) swaps the
breadcrumbs for a path box that behaves like a shell: `Tab` completes, `↑↓` pick a
suggestion, `Enter` goes, `~` and relative paths work, and an empty box lists recently
visited directories. Typing a file's path opens its directory with the file selected.
Getting to `/run/media/deck/…` no longer takes six clicks.

**Behaviour change: the shell's locale now follows your system instead of being forced to
Chinese.** `LANG` inside the terminal was hardcoded to `zh_CN.UTF-8`, so every user got a
Chinese-speaking `ls`, `git` and `man` regardless of the seven UI languages. It now
resolves from the plugin setting, then `$LANG`, then the desktop's own locale
(`~/.config/plasma-localerc`), then `/etc/locale.conf`, falling back to `C.UTF-8`; only
UTF-8 locales the system has actually generated are accepted. A **Terminal language**
dropdown in the QAM panel makes it switchable without editing files. It applies to new
sessions only — tmux fixes a session's environment when the session is created.

Fixes

- Clicking **Copy** on the on-screen key bar with nothing selected threw a `TypeError`
  instead of showing a message (a `var` declaration shadowed the translation helper).
- Dragging a protected location (your home directory, a mount point) onto another folder
  in the file panel moved it. The guard existed but was only wired into delete, despite
  its own documentation saying it stopped exactly this.
- A session name with a trailing newline was accepted, producing a tmux session that was
  invisible in the session list and impossible to close while still occupying one of the
  24 slots.
- `Content-Disposition` for a filename ending in a backslash produced an unterminated
  quoted-string, which strict parsers read as swallowing the rest of the header.
- The idle auto-stop could silently fail to run: the shutdown task was created without
  keeping a reference, and the event loop only holds a weak one.
- The PWA manifest hardcoded Chinese app names for every language.

Development

- CI now runs the build, type check, ESLint, Ruff and the unit tests on every push and
  pull request; releases verify that the tag matches `package.json`.
- New `tests/unit.py`: 268 pure-function checks that run anywhere, covering path handles,
  session-name namespacing, locale resolution, path completion and the same-origin check.
  The 127 end-to-end checks still need a real Deck; several of them turned out to pass
  regardless of whether the code worked, and were rewritten to actually test what their
  names promise.
- Source comments are now in English.

annacode747/deck-web-terminal.name: v1.0.1
annacode747/deck-web-terminal.body:
Licensing fix, no functional changes.

`bin/web/term.js` concatenates the minified xterm.js UMD bundles, which carry no copyright
headers of their own — so the distributed file was missing the notices MIT requires. The build
now reads the license texts out of `node_modules` and

- prepends them to `term.js` as a banner, so the file carries its notices even on its own, and
- emits `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` covering everything bundled into `term.js` and `dist/index.js`
  (xterm.js and its four addons, `@decky/api`, `qrcode-generator`, `react-icons`, `tslib`).

Both the release archive and `deploy.sh` now ship that file. Two end-to-end checks guard it.

annacode747/deck-web-terminal.name: v1.0.0
annacode747/deck-web-terminal.body:
First public release.

A full Steam Deck terminal in any browser, equivalent to SSH. Scan a QR code and you're in;
no client to install. Sessions live in tmux, so disconnects, sleep and closing the browser
don't interrupt anything.

**What's in it**

- **Real PTY** — `pty.fork()` + `execve`, interactive login shell, so `nvm` and `.bashrc` load
  normally. `vim`, `htop`, `claude` and other full-screen TUIs work properly.
- **Persistent, independent sessions** — one tmux session per browser tab. Close the browser and
  the processes keep running; reconnect and you're back. Two windows don't mirror each other.
- **Copy & paste like a real terminal** — copy on select, right-click / middle-click to paste, no
  confirmation dialogs. `Ctrl+C` is always an interrupt. OSC 52 lets vim and tmux write straight to
  the browser clipboard.
- **File transfer by dragging** — drag between your own file manager and the Deck. Drop onto the
  terminal and it lands in whatever directory you're `cd`'d…

snakethedev/decky-display.name: v0.1.0 - experimental test build
snakethedev/decky-display.body:
## Test build - experimental, never run on hardware

**Every line of code in this release was written by an AI coding agent**
(**OpenCode**, model `Space Bunny Free`). There is no human-written code in it.

It has **never been run on a Steam Deck.** No gadget has been created, no frame
captured, no host enumerated. 40 unit tests pass, covering the parts that do not
need hardware: V4L2 struct layouts and ioctl encoding, player discovery,
command construction, and every process failure path.

### What it does

Shows a USB capture adapter's input fullscreen on the Deck's panel.

```
other PC ──HDMI──▶ capture card ──USB──▶ Deck
```

The Deck is not a display adapter and cannot be made into one: Linux has no
DisplayPort or HDMI gadget, and the Deck's USB-C only sends video. What works is
the other direction, which is why nothing needs installing on the other machine.

### Three things to try, in order

1. Plug a UVC capture adapter in and press **Rescan**. If nothing appears, that is
   the end of it — the adapter is the hard requirement.
2. The **Diagnostics** panel says which players were found and whether `/dev/dri`
   is present. Most SteamOS installs have `mpv` already.
3. "Draw on the Deck's panel" needs mpv and takes DRM away from gamescope, so it
   only works outside Game Mode. It is off by default because it is experimental.

### If you report a problem

The most useful thing is the plugin log at
`~/homebrew/logs/decky-display/`, plus the Diagnostics panel contents.

chenpx976/steamproxy.name: Steam Proxy v1.0.0
chenpx976/steamproxy.body:
## Steam Proxy v1.0.0

Steam Deck Decky 插件 —— 只代理被墙站点，国内流量与游戏下载 CDN 直连。

### 功能

- 🇭🇰 香港节点 `url-test` 自动选优（每 5 分钟测速切换）
- 94 条分流规则：Steam / Google / GitHub / npm / PyPI / Docker / OpenAI / Claude / X / Telegram / Discord / Reddit
- 游戏下载 CDN 直连（`steamcontent.com`、`st.dl.*`），下载速度不受影响
- 局域网直连，保护 SSH / Steam Link / 投屏
- 插件内开关服务、切换节点、并发测延迟（0.2s）
- 插件与 clash 服务解耦，卸载 Decky 不影响加速

### 安装方式一：一键脚本（推荐）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/chenpx976/steamproxy.git
cd steamproxy
sudo ./install.sh /tmp/your-clash-config.yaml
```

自动完成：安装 Decky → 下载 mihomo 内核 → 导入配置 → 部署插件 → 注册开机自启 → 连通性验证。

### 安装方式二：手动（仅更新插件）

```bash
unzip SteamProxy-v1.0.0.zip -d /tmp/
scp -r /tmp/SteamProxy deck@<deck-ip>:/tmp/
ssh deck@<deck-ip> 'sudo rm -rf ~/homebrew/plugins/SteamProxy && \
  sudo cp -r /tmp/SteamProxy ~/homebrew/plugins/SteamProxy && \
  sudo chmod -R a+rX ~/homebrew/plugins/SteamProxy && \
  sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader'
```

### ⚠️ 需要自备节点

本仓库和 Release **不含任何节点凭据**。配置文件选择：

- 有 Surge 配置：`python3 tools/gen_clash_config.py your.conf /tmp/clash.yaml`
- 有 clash 订阅：导出为 yaml
- 从零开始：参考 `config.example.yaml`

`proxy-groups` 里必须有一个名为 **`香港加速`** 的组。

### 已修复

- `test_all_delay` 从串行改并发（最坏 60s → 0.2s），避免触发 Decky 调用超时

详见 [README](https://github.com/chenpx976/steamproxy#readme)

hffgzktbcc-blip/deckstream.name: DeckStream v1.0.0 - Handheld Gaming Runtime
hffgzktbcc-blip/deckstream.body:
# 🎮 DeckStream v1.0.0 - Handheld Gaming Runtime

**DeckStream** is an open-source, on-demand virtual filesystem gaming runtime for the Steam Deck and handheld Linux PCs (SteamOS 3.5+).

Instead of filling limited local handheld storage with 100+ GB installations, DeckStream mounts your personal remote game libraries (WebDAV, Nextcloud, TrueNAS, Unraid, or S3/MinIO) over an unprivileged Copy-on-Write FUSE layer, launching titles natively through Proton while streaming only the file blocks the game reads during gameplay.

---

### ✨ Highlights & Key Capabilities
- **⚡ FUSE On-Demand Streaming**: Play large PC titles directly from personal remote storage with chunk-level VFS caching.
- **🛡️ Copy-on-Write Sandbox (`fuse-overlayfs`)**: Remote storage stays 100% read-only. Game writes, INI tweaks, and DirectX/Vulkan shader caches land in an isolated upper layer on local MicroSD or NVMe storage.
- **🎮 Handheld Decky Loader Integration**: Native SteamOS Gaming Mode QAM plugin to monitor throughput, check cache consumption, clear cache, and toggle per-game battery modes.
- **🔋 Per-Game Deck Mode**: One-tap toggle in the Decky panel capping framerate at 30 FPS and setting low graphics presets for up to 130% longer battery life.
- **⚡ Range-Request Hedging**: Built-in hedge proxy monitors range requests and automatically races duplicate connections if a remote chunk stalls past 200 ms.
- **🌙 Overnight Startup Warmup**: Pre-fetches startup profiles for recently played titles while on the charger dock.
- **💾 Automated Save Snapshots**: Post-session save backups via **Ludusavi** preserve progress across Proton prefix updates.
- **🛠️ Self-Healing Doctor**: Built-in `doctor.py` diagnostic tool checks Wi-Fi power-saving toggles, DNS latency, VFS responsiveness, and systemd service health.

---

### 🚀 Quick Installation on Steam Deck
Switch to **Desktop Mode**, open **Konsole**, and run:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hffgzktbcc-blip/deckstream/main/daemon/install.sh | bash -s -- https://deckstream.local deck-main
```

---

### 🔒 Cryptographic Checksums (SHA-256)
```text
5d4ed60936a566bc65be2db171ae5866430c15e2b1959455994f18284ae05b8b  deckstream-decky-plugin-v1.0.0.zip
```

Complete Codex App Server handshake.

- Sends the required `initialized` notification after `initialize`.
- Prevents the App Server from resetting a successfully opened WebSocket session.
- Skips chats currently owned by another Codex client and opens the first available chat.
- Keeps the responsive offline controls and persisted-chat fixes from v0.1.34.

Download `CodexRemote.zip` from the release, extract it, and copy the `CodexRemote` folder to:

```text
/home/deck/homebrew/plugins/CodexRemote
```

Then restart Decky Loader:

```bash
sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader.service
```

## Notes

This is an alpha release. Codex App Server WebSocket support is experimental upstream, so expect protocol changes.

the412banner/fusionhud.name: FusionHUD for Decky 0.3.2
the412banner/fusionhud.body:
# FusionHUD for Decky 0.3.2 (DroidDeck)

FusionHUD as an overlay in DroidDeck's Steam session: a Decky plugin you install from a ZIP, with no change to the DroidDeck app. Steam's own performance overlay (MangoHud) stays off, and FusionHUD draws over your games instead. You switch it on and set it up from the plugin's panel in Steam's quick menu.

## What you get
- **All five FusionHUD sizes:** Full, Tiles, Pill, Minimal and Mega, drawn the same way as in Bannerlator.
- **The same settings as Bannerlator's HUD:** size on screen, opacity, colour (Soft / Mid / Vivid), outline and outline colour, plus a switch for every metric the chosen size draws (FPS, graph, GPU, GPU temperature, CPU, RAM, VRAM, temperature, battery, power, lows, per-core CPU, swap, network, resolution, Proton, session, engine, clock), temperature unit and danger colours. Added for Decky: position (corners or top centre) and accent colour.
- **Readings:**
  - the game's real frame rate and frame times, from gamescope;
  - GPU load, clock and temperature;
  - CPU load, clock and temperature, total and per core;
  - RAM, VRAM and swap;
  - battery %, temperature and watts;
  - network speed, resolution and refresh rate;
  - the engine (e.g. DXVK) and the Proton build the game runs on.
- **Optional:** "Steam overlay styles" gives Steam's own overlay levels 1–4 FusionHUD's colours, if you'd rather keep using it.

## Install
1. DroidDeck → Steam settings → Decky: install Decky and turn it on.
2. With Steam closed: **Plugins → Install from ZIP** and pick `FusionHUD-decky-0.3.2.zip`.
3. Start Steam and set **Performance Overlay Level to OFF** in the quick menu (Performance). gamescope shows one overlay at a time: FusionHUD shows while Steam's level is OFF, and Steam's overlay takes over when you pick a level.
4. Open the quick menu → Decky → **FusionHUD** to switch it on and change sizes and settings. Changes apply straight away.

## Good to know
- The overlay doesn't get touch input, so instead of tapping and dragging the HUD, size and position are set in the panel.
- **VRAM** comes from DroidDeck's own reading, which DroidDeck refreshes while Steam's overlay is visible, so with Steam's overlay off it may stay at its first value.
- **Tiles** with everything switched on is tall (about 88 % of a 720p screen), as in Bannerlator.
- In Steam's menus the frame rate jumps between 0 and the refresh rate, because Steam only redraws when something changes. In games it shows the game's rate.

## Tested
On an AYANEO Pocket FIT (Adreno 750) with DroidDeck and Decky 3.3.1:
- **0.3.1, all five sizes and their switches:** checked in Steam's menus, and in Dead Cells (DXVK label, Proton line, temperature colours).
- **Temperatures:** checked against AYANEO's own side panel.
- **0.3.2:** only adds the Engine switch back to the panel; that build hasn't been installed on the device yet.

## Credits
- [FusionHUD](https://github.com/The412Banner/FusionHUD) by The412Banner (layout, colours and settings from FusionHUD / Bannerlator).
- The overlay window and gamescope frame-time queue follow [MangoHud](https://github.com/flightlessmango/MangoHud)'s mangoapp (MIT).
- Drawing: [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui) (MIT) and [GLFW](https://www.glfw.org) (zlib).
- Plugin layout from the [Decky plugin template](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-plugin-template) (BSD-3-Clause).

GPL-3.0 with a §7(b) attribution term, as FusionHUD (see `ATTRIBUTION.md`).

beallio/sdh-ludusavi.name: v0.5.3 — Stock CSS Loader themes reload again
beallio/sdh-ludusavi.body:
Patch release. Save checks, backups, and restores work exactly as they did in v0.5.2, and this release fixes theme reloading for people on the stock CSS Loader.

## Fixed

- **The stock DeckThemes CSS Loader reloads updated themes again.** Since v0.5.1, if you ran the stock DeckThemes CSS Loader with the SDH-Ludusavi status-bar theme, an update could leave you with the message "CSS Loader could not reload the updated theme", and the status-bar theme was not reloaded. The plugin now falls back to Decky's older plugin call route, and only after Decky rejects the newer call with that exact reported cause. Any other failure is reported exactly as before, so real problems are not hidden. Checked on a Steam Deck virtual machine with the stock CSS Loader 2.1.4: v0.5.2 showed the warning and reloaded nothing, while this release showed no warning and CSS Loader reloaded its themes.

## Added

- **The Decky Loader fork's own debug setting now turns on the plugin's debug log.** If your Decky Loader fork has the plugin's debug option enabled (decky-loader v3.3.1-rust.1-rc.3 and later), SDH-Ludusavi now writes its detailed debug lines even when the plugin's own debug setting is off. Nothing changes if you had both off, and nothing changes on standard Decky Loader.

## Internal

- The decky-plugin SDK was updated to the current decky-loader build, 192cedc, which is what lets the loader's debug setting reach the plugin.

## Install

Download `SDH-Ludusavi-v0.5.3.zip` below and install it through Decky Loader. Verify the download against `SDH-Ludusavi-v0.5.3.zip.sha256`:

```bash
sha256sum -c SDH-Ludusavi-v0.5.3.zip.sha256
```

If you already have SDH-Ludusavi installed, updating keeps your settings, your save history, and your Ludusavi backups in place.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/beallio/SDH-Ludusavi/compare/v0.5.2...v0.5.3

beallio/sdh-ludusavi.name: v0.5.2 — Quitting a game now runs its save check
beallio/sdh-ludusavi.body:
Patch release. Save checks, backups, and restores work the same way as they did in v0.5.1, and this release fixes a bug that could skip the check when you quit a game.

## Fixed

- **Quitting a game again runs the exit save check.** Since v0.5.0, some games did not get their automatic save check when you quit them. Steam can note a game's start and its exit under different internal labels, and the plugin only matched exits by the label it recorded at start. When the labels did not match, the plugin ignored the exit, so no check ran and no backup was made. The plugin now matches the exit to the game it knows is running, so the check runs as it should. If a quit event still cannot be matched, the plugin only warns when the app is one you track or one that was actually running.


beallio/sdh-ludusavi.name: v0.5.0 — A new backend for save management
beallio/sdh-ludusavi.body:
SDH-Ludusavi now uses a native program to manage its save checks, backups, and restores. You can use the same plugin package with standard Decky Loader or the Decky fork that starts native plugins directly.

Ludusavi now comes with the plugin, so you no longer need to install it from Discover. The Ludusavi shortcut in the plugin opens the included copy, where you choose your backup folder. If the included copy cannot start, the plugin uses the Ludusavi Flatpak instead, if you have it installed.

bakapute/armadalsfg.body:
# Armada LSFG v0.1.5

## 🇫🇷 Français

### Nouvelle gestion des profils

- Les profils LSFG ne sont plus tous affichés les uns à la suite des autres.
- Ajout d'une liste repliable pour choisir un jeu possédant déjà un profil.
- Ajout d'une liste séparée pour les jeux pouvant être ajoutés à LSFG.
- Les paramètres du jeu sélectionné apparaissent directement sous la liste.
- La sélection manuelle reste affichée après la modification d'un réglage.

### Détection automatique du jeu en cours

- Armada LSFG détecte automatiquement les profils LSFG utilisés par les jeux en cours d'exécution.
- Le jeu en cours apparaît automatiquement dans l'interface sans devoir être sélectionné manuellement.
- Lorsqu'un autre jeu est sélectionné, les deux profils peuvent être affichés simultanément.
- Le jeu sélectionné manuellement est affiché au-dessus du jeu en cours afin de faciliter la comparaison des réglages.
- Un même profil n'est jamais affiché deux fois.

### Interface

- L'interface reste automatiquement en français sur les appareils francophones.
- L'anglais reste utilisé par défaut sur les autres appareils.
- Les réglages existants restent modifiables :
  - activation LSFG ;
  - exécutable ;
  - multiplicateur ;
  - Flow Scale ;
  - Performance Mode ;
  - suppression du profil.

### Compatibilité

- Aucun changement au format des profils existants.
- Les profils, paramètres et caches créés avec les versions précédentes restent compatibles.
- Les bibliothèques Steam multiples et les jeux installés sur microSD restent pris en charge.

### Important

- Armada LSFG ne modifie pas les Steam Launch Options.
- Cette version ne modifie pas le fonctionnement de LSFG-VK.

---

## 🇬🇧 English

### New profile management

- LSFG profiles are no longer displayed one after another in a long list.
- Added a collapsible list for choosing a game that already has a profile.
- Added a separate list for games that can be added to LSFG.
- The selected game's settings appear directly below the list.
- The manual selection remains visible after changing a setting.

### Automatic running-game detection

- Armada LSFG automatically detects LSFG profiles used by currently running games.
- The running game appears automatically without requiring manual selection.
- When another game is selected, both profiles can be displayed at the same time.
- The manually selected game is displayed above the running game to make setting comparisons easier.
- The same profile is never displayed twice.

### Interface

- The interface remains automatically French on French-language devices.
- English remains the default on all other devices.
- Existing settings remain editable:
  - LSFG enable state;
  - executable;
  - multiplier;
  - Flow Scale;
  - Performance Mode;
  - profile removal.

### Compatibility

- No change to the existing profile format.
- Profiles, settings and caches created by previous versions remain compatible.
- Multiple Steam libraries and games installed on microSD remain supported.

### Important

- Armada LSFG does not modify Steam Launch Options.
- This release does not change LSFG-VK behavior.

danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.name: v1.2.0
danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.body:
Links installed plugins to the repo they came from, so checking for updates no
longer means typing a repo for each one by hand.

The official store builds every plugin from a submodule in its plugin database,
and that database records which repo each plugin comes from. Bazaar now reads
that index and matches it against the folder a plugin is installed under, which
resolves every plugin currently in the store. Anything the store has never
carried falls back to the files the plugin itself ships.

- **Find repos for your unlinked plugins** appears in the panel whenever
  something is unlinked. One press links everything it can work out, and leaves
  the rest alone.
- **Links say where they came from.** One matched against the store's database
  is taken as fact. One worked out from a plugin's own files is marked
  *detected*, because those can still name the repo a plugin was forked from
  rather than the one it is maintained in today — worth a glance, and one press
  to correct.
- **An automatic link reports updates immediately**, comparing the version on
  disk against the latest release instead of waiting for you to mark which
  release you are on. Any older link with no release recorded benefits too.
- **Plugins hosted outside GitHub are skipped** rather than guessed at, and a
  branch the store builds from is not mistaken for the branch releases are
  tagged on.


## Installing

Install in Decky Loader with **Settings → Developer mode → Install Plugin from URL**, using the `.zip` link below, or download it and copy it to the Deck.

Already running Decky Bazaar? Add `danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar` to it and let it update itself.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar/compare/v1.1.2...v1.2.0

danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.name: v1.1.2
danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.body:
Fixes 1.0.9 being treated as newer than 1.0.10.

Releases were taken in the order GitHub returned them, which is the order they
were created rather than which version is highest. A plugin sitting on 1.0.9
could be reported as up to date with 1.0.10 already published, and the release
picker could offer an older release at the top of the list.

- **Releases are now ordered by version**, so the latest release is the highest
  one — 1.0.10 after 1.0.9, and a pre-release before the release it leads to.
- **An update is only offered when it is actually newer.** A release cut for an
  older line no longer shows up as an update waiting to be installed.
- Tags that carry no version number at all still fall back to publish date.


## Installing

Install in Decky Loader with **Settings → Developer mode → Install Plugin from URL**, using the `.zip` link below, or download it and copy it to the Deck.

Already running Decky Bazaar? Add `danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar` to it and let it update itself.…

danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.name: v1.1.1
danielcamilo1/decky-bazaar.body:
Fixes a branch showing up empty when its releases are pre-releases.

Picking a branch hid pre-releases before it ever considered the branch, so a
branch that ships previews — a `testing` or `beta` branch, which is most of the
reason to pin one in the first place — looked like it had no releases at all,
and the dialog blamed the branch for it.

- **Pre-releases are now counted per branch**, and the dialog says how many it is

tipsilva/egpu-switch.name: egpu-switch 0.3.4: final release (security fixes, discontinued)
tipsilva/egpu-switch.body:
**This is the last release of egpu-switch.** The project continues as
**[Yby eGPU](https://github.com/TiPSilva/yby-egpu)**, which provides GPU switching
and safe eject without depending on all-ways-egpu, plus a desktop app and
additional controls. Its installer removes egpu-switch from Decky. Update
to 0.3.4 if you still use egpu-switch, then migrate to Yby eGPU.

### Security fixes

- **High: a user-writable file was executed as root.** The plugin runs as root
  and executed `all-ways-egpu` from `~/bin` (and from any user's
  `/home/*/bin`) every few seconds. Any program running as a user could
  replace that file and gain root without a password. The plugin, and the
  shutdown hook in `extras/`, now only run all-ways-egpu when the file and
  every folder above it belong to root and nobody else can write to them.
  If yours is in `~/bin`, the panel shows a command to install it
  for the whole system.
- **Medium: root followed a link when saving settings.** `settings.json`
  lives in a folder the user owns; replacing it with a link made root
  overwrite arbitrary system files, and the settings screen could read any
  JSON file. Settings are now read and written without following links,
  through a temporary file, and only the two known options are kept.
- **Low: fixed file names in `/tmp`.** The shutdown hook wrote its errors to
  predictable files in `/tmp` as root. It no longer uses `/tmp`.
- **Low: Deep rescan could pick a bridge in another PCI domain.** On
  machines with more than one PCI domain it could reset the wrong bridge. It
  now matches the domain too.

These issues were identified during the review for the Yby eGPU release.

tipsilva/egpu-switch.name: eGPU Switch v0.3.3 (stable)
tipsilva/egpu-switch.body:
First stable release since v0.1.0, with everything learned from real hardware testing on an AyaNeo (AMD Ryzen 7840U) and an ROG Ally X folded in.

## Highlights since v0.1.0

- Safe eject flow: unloads NVIDIA modules and removes the eGPU from the PCI bus before you disconnect the Thunderbolt cable, instead of only switching boot VGA.
- Deep Rescan option for cases where a plain PCI rescan does not bring the eGPU back after reconnecting.
- Automatic HDMI audio rebind after a rescan re-adds the eGPU, gated on actual ELD health instead of a fixed sleep.
- Connection diagnostics panel: connection type (Thunderbolt or PCIe), link speed and width, Thunderbolt controller and peripheral names, and boot/sleep freeze fix status.
- Friendly GPU and Thunderbolt controller names parsed from machine-readable lspci and boltctl output, picking the authorized peripheral instead of just the first one listed.
- Settings persistence for the auto-eject and deep rescan toggles.
- Documented fix for AMD…

tipsilva/egpu-switch.name: v0.3.3 (dev, unstable)
tipsilva/egpu-switch.body:
Unstable dev-branch build, not the recommended release for most users (use [v0.1.0](https://github.com/TiPSilva/egpu-switch/releases/tag/v0.1.0) for that). Published specifically so testers on different hardware can try recent fixes and new options.

## Changed since v0.3.2

- **Fixed a real audio bug**: eject the eGPU, then click Switch to eGPU directly (without a manual Rescan first) could bring video back on the TV with no audio, and restarting the display manager didn't help. The plugin used to decide whether to repair audio based on whether a rescan had been "needed" for the video side, which is the wrong signal: automatic Thunderbolt hotplug can re-add the eGPU (video and audio both) before you press anything, so the video side already looked fine while the audio codec was still broken from that same re-enumeration. It now checks the ALSA card's own ELD state directly and repairs audio whenever it's actually broken, regardless of what triggered the reconnect. Confirmed fixed on…

tipsilva/egpu-switch.name: v0.3.2 (dev, unstable)
tipsilva/egpu-switch.body:
Unstable dev-branch build, not the recommended release for most users (use [v0.1.0](https://github.com/TiPSilva/egpu-switch/releases/tag/v0.1.0) for that). Published specifically so testers on different hardware can try recent fixes and new options.

## Changed since v0.3.1

- **Data loss guard**: nothing previously checked for mounted storage before detaching PCI devices. Some NVIDIA boards expose their own USB-C controller as a sibling function, and Deep rescan removes an entire parent bridge, so an enclosure carrying an NVMe or a USB storage controller next to the GPU was one eject away from losing it mid-write. Eject and Deep rescan now refuse upfront (before the display manager is even touched) when mounted storage sits behind the target.
- **Concurrency fix**: `rescan_pci` now takes the same operation lock as every other action. It had grown from a single, safe sysfs write into an operation that can remove a PCI bridge, reauthorize a Thunderbolt tunnel and rebind a driver, while…

## Changed since v0.3.0

- **Fixed the Deep rescan safety check.** Tester logs (Strix Halo / CachyOS Handheld) showed that after an eject, the system can automatically re-add the eGPU as a broken, half-initialized device: it exists on the PCI bus but is not actually usable (no working `boot_vga`, the same `bridge window ... can't assign; no space` allocation issue). The previous check saw "device exists" and skipped the deep path exactly when it was needed, which also made **Switch to eGPU** give up without doing anything. Deep rescan now triggers whenever `all-ways-egpu` does not report the eGPU as connected and no driver is bound to it, covering both "missing from the bus" and "re-added broken".

failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.body:
This release brings the Status and Logs tabs over from my other project, CheevoDeck, offering more info on each freeze mitigation event. Also ports the system over where this plugin now checks for updates, allowing you to install updates easily through the desktop updater or link copy method.

## New

- The main section now becomes the Status tab, showing your protection status, as well as basic status such as how many QAM freezes were prevented and how many QAM freezes were recovered from.

- A Logs tab has been added that shows you the last 200 mitigation/recovery events, along with basic logging info.

- Stormbreaker now checks GitHub for a new release twice a day. When an update is available, you will be notified once with a toast, the new update message will show in-app, and download options will appear.

That's all for today. Since this is pretty stable, there shouldn't be many updates after this point unless a SteamOS update breaks it. In that case, I will be sure to release…

failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.name: Stormbreaker 1.0.1
failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.body:
This is a small patch release with a variety of fixes that came from review of the same code from my other project, CheevoDeck. Everything still works the same, but it is more stable now.

## Fixes

- Stormbreaker and Automatic Recovery now only run in Game Mode, so they won't unnecessarily run in Desktop Mode. It makes sense because the QAM freeze issue can only occur in Game Mode anyway.
- Fixed a problem where Automatic Recovery failed to restart Steam's interface while a game with a non-Latin name was running.
- Fixed a problem at startup where Stormbreaker stays off for a whole session if Steam's menus weren't ready when the plugin loaded.
- Fixed an issue where reloading the plugin at the wrong time would leave CheevoDeck thinking Stormbreaker was still running after it was gone, so neither plugin would break a storm until Steam restarted.
- Settings and recovery logs are now saved in a way that can't be pointed at another file on your system.

failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.name: Stormbreaker 1.0.0
failinator5000/decky-stormbreaker.body:
This is the first release of Stormbreaker, ported from my other project, [CheevoDeck](https://github.com/FAILINATOR5000/decky-cheevodeck).

Stormbreaker is a Decky Loader plugin for SteamOS platforms that both prevents and recovers you from a rare SteamOS bug related to the Quick Access Menu (QAM), where in rare cases upon opening, it gets stuck and becomes unresponsive. While rare, it is devastating as controls also become unresponsive, so usually it results in hard resetting the device, losing game progress in the process.

woodsi3/forza-dualsense-decky.name: Decky Forza DualSense Haptics v1.0.0
woodsi3/forza-dualsense-decky.body:
## Forza DualSense Haptics v1.0.0

The first stable release of Forza DualSense Haptics for Decky Loader.

This plugin converts Forza UDP telemetry into meaningful DualSense adaptive-trigger and haptic feedback natively in Game Mode on SteamOS.

### Manual Install Instructions:

1. Download the latest release ZIP.
2. Extract the `forza-dualsense-haptics` folder into:
   `~/homebrew/plugins/`
3. Restart Decky Loader (or safer, reboot the Steam Deck).
4. Enable UDP telemetry in Forza and configure it to send telemetry to your Steam Deck on IP 127.0.0.1, Port 5300.
5. Launch the game and enjoy.

The plugin will automatically create its settings on first launch.

Further detail on manual Decky plugin installation can be found [here](https://wiki.deckbrew.xyz/en/user-guide/settings).

moi952/decky-nvidia-update.name: v0.5.0
moi952/decky-nvidia-update.body:
## ✨ Features

- rework driver channels, translate help and add 0.5.0 changelog (moi952)
  - Arch packages are the recommended source; NVIDIA-only releases split
    into Recommended, NFB and Beta with live counts
  - Version and source tags on separate lines in the picker

  - Add v0_5_0 What's new entry, keep the banner last in the panel
- add scrollable logs and contextual control help (60plus)

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- preserve SteamOS configuration across driver changes (60plus)
  Keep user configuration in the writable overlay, isolate pacman build inputs, and scope BLAKE2b hook compatibility to initramfs generation. Add migration regressions and document verified driver changes on SteamOS 3.9.5.
- show only Close in driver release notes (60plus)
- merge NVIDIA production and NFB release catalogs (60plus)
- let controller navigation reach the log Close button (60plus)
- keep the native L3 hint visible in live log mode (60plus)
- preserve operation logs across Decky log rotation (60plus)
- switch log history with L3 and read right-stick scrolling (60plus)
- center log dialog and use native controller hints (60plus)
- explain and reject already installed driver requests (60plus)
- preserve deleted configuration when staging a driver (60plus)
- report filesystem read failures and retain requested driver (60plus)
- improve driver operation recovery and progress (60plus)
  Restore pending rollback after a Decky reload and check the actual boot selection before offering a restart. Track transaction phases instead of nested worker counters, and require the matching completion receipt before reporting 100 percent.
  Distinguish launch failures from busy operations, reconnect status without repeating an installation request, and detach only the observer on unload. Add backend and frontend regression coverage with English messages.

## 🔧 Chores

- update decky-ui-kit to 0.7.1 and decky-plugin-toolkit to v0.1.1 (moi952)

## 📦 Other

- Merge pull request #3 from 60plus/improve-update-reliability (moi952)

- support Main driver staging and guard EFI shutdown migration (60plus)
  Omit empty Arch pin arguments and recognize Valve's complete Main finalizer
  loop before inserting the driver repair hook.
  Arm a verified runtime systemd override before staging on the affected Main
  implementation. Keep EFI mounts in a private namespace during shutdown,
  preserve custom overrides, and let the guard expire automatically at reboot.
  Validate with 109 Python tests, namespace probes, frontend checks, and a real
  Main 610-to-615 Decky update and reboot on a 5 GiB read-only root. Record the
  hardware scope and remaining unrelated preparation warnings.
- migrate legacy builds and collect only unpinned driver caches (60plus)

## 🔧 Chores

- add the 0.4.0 what's new entry (moi952)
- reset version to 0.3.0 for the 0.4.0 release (moi952)
- use upstream decky-ui-kit 0.6.1 without local patch…

  Adds a separate build path (bin/steamos-nvidia-build.sh +

- adopt decky-plugin-toolkit for settings & self-update (moi952)

  like decky-quick-tab already does. Driver settings stay on the main

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- use pnpm version --message and --no-git-checks (moi952)…

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.4.1-beta.3 — Free DLC and the base game
koua29/decky-fsg.body:
**Free DLC now tells you when it needs the base game.** Spotted on *Dying Light: The Beast — Discharge Weapon Pack* (€4.99, free right now): Steam only hands a free DLC to owners of the game it belongs to.

## What's new
- 🧩 FSG reads the game a DLC belongs to and checks whether it is in your library. If it isn't, the card says **"Needs <game> in your library"**, the add button is disabled, and a second button opens the base game on Steam.
- 🤖 Auto-add skips those DLCs instead of retrying them and failing.
- 💬 If you claim one anyway, the message explains it: *this DLC is free, but Steam only gives it to owners of <game>*.

## Also in this 0.4.1 line
- 🟢🔴 Steam session light at the top of the list, with a button to open the Steam Store when it is red (beta.2).
- 🔁 A redirect from Steam is no longer reported as a failure; clearer messages and a better log line when a claim really fails (beta.1).

## How to update
Options → **Beta versions** on, then **Check for updates** → **Update**, at the bottom of the panel.
From a stable version without the beta option: Decky → ⚙️ Settings → General → **Developer mode**, then ⚙️ → **Developer** → **Install plugin from URL** with the link below.

## Download
**`FSG.zip`** — test build, `beta` branch.

## What's new
- 🟢🔴 **Session light** at the top of the free games list: green when FSG finds your Steam session in Steam's own browser, red when it doesn't, grey before the first check. It is refreshed every time you open the panel.
- 🛒 **"Open the Steam Store" button** appears when the light is red, so you can sign in right where FSG reads the session, then come back and claim.

## Also in this 0.4.1 line (from beta.1)
- 🔁 A redirect from Steam is no longer reported as a failure: FSG always checks your licence list afterwards, and says **Added to your library** whenever the game landed there.
- 💬 Clearer messages when a claim really fails (sign-in needed, redirect, HTTP error, not confirmed yet), each with what to do next, and the HTTP status plus redirect target written to `~/homebrew/logs/FSG`.

## How to update
Options → **Beta versions** on, then **Check for updates** → **Update**, at the bottom of the…

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.4.1-beta.1 — A redirect is no longer a failure
koua29/decky-fsg.body:
**Fixes the "Steam refused the request (HTTP 302)" message** reported on r/deckyloader.

## What changed
- 🔁 **A redirect is not a failure.** Steam often answers the claim request with a redirect instead of a body, and a redirect says nothing about the result. FSG now always checks your licence list afterwards — if the game landed in your library, you get **Added to your library**, whatever HTTP status came back.
- 💬 **Clearer messages** when the claim really fails, each with what to do next:
  - *Steam sent the request to its login page* → open the Steam Store on the console and make sure you are signed in.
  - *Steam answered with a redirect / HTTP xxx and the game is still missing* → open the Store once and try again, or claim the game from its Steam page.
  - *Steam took the request but the game is not in your library yet* → wait a few seconds and refresh.
- 🧾 **Better log line**: the HTTP status and the redirect target are written to `~/homebrew/logs/FSG`, so a failure can be…

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.4.0 — Statistics, stick navigation, visible updates
koua29/decky-fsg.body:
**Statistics, smoother stick navigation and easier-to-spot updates.** Everything tested through 11 betas on a Legion Go 2, where FSG has already added two 100%-off games on its own.

## What's new
- 📊 **Statistics view**: press **See the statistics** to open a dedicated view inside the panel, with a way back (B button works too).
  - **Value claimed**: the normal price of every game FSG added for you, in total and game by game.
  - **Your Steam library**: number of items and estimated value (priced items vs. items at €0: demos, free-to-play…).
  - Computed **only** when you press **Recalculate the statistics**: nothing runs in the background on your console.
- 🔄 **Updates are easier to spot**: the update button now sits under **Check for updates**, at the bottom of the panel, and every check shows a notification (up to date / update found / GitHub unreachable).
- 🗂️ **Clearer panel order**: free games to keep, Refresh, Options, upcoming promos, statistics, updates.

## Fixes
- 🕹️ **Stick navigation**: moving up with the stick now scrolls the panel all the way to the top (the logo and game cards are focusable, and the panel follows Steam's gamepad focus).
- ↩️ After an update, the panel closes and reloads on the new version instead of staying on the old code.

## How to update

### From v0.2.0 or later (built-in updates)
1. Open FSG in the Decky menu and press **Check for updates** (bottom of the panel).
2. Press **Update to 0.4.0** (in v0.2.0 to v0.3.1, it shows up in the **Update available** section at the top of the panel).
3. Decky shows its confirmation window, checks the zip's checksum and reloads the plugin.

Beta users get this version too.

### From v0.1.0 (no built-in updates): reinstall by hand, once
v0.1.0 can't update itself. If your panel has no **Check for updates** button, install v0.4.0 over it:
1. Decky → ⚙️ Settings → General → turn on **Developer mode**.
2. Decky → ⚙️ → **Developer** → **Install plugin from URL**, paste this link and confirm:
   ```
   https://github.com/koua29/decky-fsg/releases/latest/download/FSG.zip
   ```
   Or download `FSG.zip` below and use **Install plugin from ZIP file**.
3. From then on, new versions show up right in the panel.

Settings and history are kept either way.

## Download
**`FSG.zip`** — a SteamOS console with Decky Loader. Install by URL or from the ZIP file (developer mode).

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.4.0-beta.11 — Stick scrolling (real cause)
koua29/decky-fsg.body:
**The right cause, this time.** Steam moves a *virtual* focus: the target item never receives a browser focus event.

## Fixes
- 🕹️ The scrolling added in beta 9 never started, because it was hooked to the browser's `focus` event — which Steam does not fire when navigating with a controller. It is now hooked to **`onGamepadFocus`**, the event actually fired. The logo, game cards and statistics lines therefore bring the panel to them.

## How to update
From beta 10, with the **Beta versions** option on: *Updates* section, at the bottom of the panel.

## Download
**`FSG.zip`** — test build, `beta` branch.

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.3.1 — "Beta versions" option
koua29/decky-fsg.body:

- 🧪 **Options → Beta versions**: FSG also looks at test builds published on GitHub (`vX.Y.Z-beta.N` tags). Without this option, nothing changes: only stable versions are offered.
- ↩️ **Going back is possible**: if you turn the option off while a beta is installed, the panel offers to go back to the latest stable version.
- 🔢 Fixed version comparison: a beta is correctly ranked before the final version with the same number (`0.4.0-beta.2`, then `0.4.0`).

## How to update
Open FSG in the Decky menu and press **Update** (or Options → **Check for updates**). Decky shows its confirmation window, checks the zip's checksum and reloads the plugin. Settings and history are kept.

## Download
**`FSG.zip`** — a SteamOS console with Decky Loader. Install by URL or from the ZIP file (developer mode).

koua29/decky-fsg.name: v0.3.0 — English interface
koua29/decky-fsg.body:
FSG now speaks **English and French**: the interface, game names and prices automatically follow Steam's language.

## What's new

- 🏷️ **Game details in your language**: names, struck-through prices and promo end dates are requested from the Steam store in that same language.

pacificsilent/decky-screen-colors.name: Screen Colors v1.0.0

wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.name: GFG Extreme 3.6.0
wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.body:
# What's new in GFG-Extreme 3.6.0

- **Cleaner camera reversals.** The generator tracks changes in camera speed across real frames and uses their actual timestamps. In the 1280×800 Courtyard reversal test at ×3, blocks with large errors fell from 4.46% in Courtyard 3 to 3.44% in Courtyard 4. [Scene and measurements](https://github.com/wavessevaw/GFG-Extreme/tree/95398f2f795bbf08b8e8f1533af2e54d2c415e03/docs/courtyard4)
- **More definition in dark detail.** Kedavra Focus deepens softened stitches, fur and fine dark lettering in SDR. Use **Graphics → Kedavra Focus**, with frame generation on or off. [Images and motion comparisons](https://github.com/wavessevaw/GFG-Extreme/tree/53c40ff8bb422b1671d8dcce1ec0a116beeeb381/docs/focus-dark-detail)
- **Steadier HUD and pacing.** The engine protects stationary HUD strokes on every SDR pair. At 90 Hz the scheduler checks the source cadence before advancing a ready real frame after a hitch. Automatic 30→60 ×2 continues to work at 60 Hz.
- **Fix. Colour filters follow your profile.** Vibrance, Levels Plus and other selected colour effects stay active in Quality, Balanced, Battery and Autopilot. The GFG overlay yields to the Steam interface.

Install **GFG-Extreme-v3_6_0.zip** in Decky, reinstall Gamescope in Setup and restart the Deck. To roll back, install the [previous official package](https://github.com/wavessevaw/GFG-Extreme/releases/tag/v3.5.0), reinstall its Gamescope and restart.

The comparisons use software Vulkan. Focus can accentuate existing interpolation errors. Steam Deck GPU time, latency and game-specific results for this build remain unmeasured.

wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.name: GFG Extreme 3.5.0
wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.body:
## What's new in GFG Extreme 3.5.0

**Resource Manager gives background work a lower priority while you play.** Open **Engine** to see which services are using CPU time or reading and writing to disk. When background work competes with your game, GFG can lower the priority of eligible Baloo indexing and Syncthing jobs. It can also defer supported scheduled backups until your session ends.

**Switch to a 60 Hz screen and ×2 follows automatically.** With frame generation enabled, GFG targets 30 real FPS and fills the midpoint between frames for 60 Hz output. The same policy works on the Deck LCD, an OLED set to 60 Hz, or a docked TV running at 59.94 or 60 Hz. Camera Boost respects that target, and Benchmark tests against it.

Bundled **GSF Kedavra 1.7.0** can show a ready real frame one refresh earlier when it would otherwise show a second intermediate and the following frame is ready too.

wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.name: GFG Extreme 3.3.0
wavessevaw/gfg-extreme.body:
# GFG Extreme 3.3.0

**GFG Extreme 3.3.0 combines the stable GFG Extreme 3.2.2 with GSF Kedavra 1.5.0.**

## What improved

- **Clearer detail during fast, reliably reconstructed motion.** Kedavra now reduces its existing motion blur only where source samples and neighbouring motion vectors agree.
- **Conservative reconstruction elsewhere.** Uncertain motion and conflicting image regions retain the previous handling.
- **No extra GPU passes or image buffers.** The change reuses existing texture samples in the reconstruction shader.
- **The familiar 3.2.2 application remains.** This release preserves its interface, settings, generation modes, per-game profiles, Autopilot/Governor controls, graphics filters, HUD, diagnostics and engine recovery mechanisms.

There is no new collection of quality sliders to configure. The earlier experimental colour-range clamp is not included.

cedricdelpoux/steam-deck-colorful.name: Colorful 1.0.0
cedricdelpoux/steam-deck-colorful.body:
This is the first release of Colorful, a Decky plugin that gives each of your TabMaster console tabs a colored panel with the console's artwork, in the style of the COLORFUL theme by Viking.

When a game is selected, the panel shows its playtime, when you last played it, your latest save, and your RetroAchievements progress for emulated games or your Steam achievements for native ones. With nothing selected, it shows the tab's total playtime and your three most played games.

To install it, open the Decky settings, turn on Developer mode, then use **Install Plugin from URL** with this address:

```
https://github.com/cedricdelpoux/steam-deck-colorful/releases/latest/download/Colorful.zip
```

You need EmuDeck and TabMaster set up first. The README explains every step.

n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.name: Sharp Filter Selector 1.2.0
n3ruk/sharp-filter-selector.body:
# Sharp Filter Selector 1.2.0

[Español](#español) · [English](#english)

## Español

### Novedades

- **SGSR en SteamOS:** Nitidez del QAM pasa de FSR `2` a SGSR `5` cuando el Gamescope activo es compatible. El puente comprueba cada ~750 ms más la respuesta X11; no modifica Gamescope de forma atómica.
- **Detección corregida:** se resuelve el bloqueo de `/proc/PID/exe` mediante la ruta absoluta observada y validada del proceso, sin elegir otro ejecutable del PATH ni conceder root al plugin.
- **QAM y controles:** conserva el modo de escalado elegido en SteamOS moderno; los overrides NIS/FSR son excluyentes y la interfaz muestra el estado SGSR.
- **Compatibilidad conservada:** los 12 métodos Ubuntu/UGM, la ruta SteamOS antigua, la lógica HDR y la nitidez 0–5 siguen intactos.

Para usar SGSR, deja **Use NIS** y **Use FSR** apagados y selecciona **Nitidez** en el QAM de Steam. Con entrada HDR, Gamescope conserva su fallback FSR; una salida HDR con juego SDR no oculta por sí sola FSR.

### Instalación

Descarga el ZIP y su archivo `.sha256` en la misma carpeta:

```bash
sha256sum -c sharp-filter-selector-v1.2.0.zip.sha256
unzip sharp-filter-selector-v1.2.0.zip
cd sharp-filter-selector
./install.sh
```

Recarga el plugin desde Decky o reinicia Steam/Gaming para cargarlo. Se conservan tus selecciones. El ZIP es para instalar; las fuentes completas y las pruebas están en el repositorio.

### Validación y organización

- **48 pruebas aprobadas:** 41 Python y 7 frontend, incluida una matriz de 90 casos de filtro/escalado/override. Tipos, build e instalador también comprobados.
- El mantenedor confirmó funcionamiento en SteamOS 3.9.5 / Gamescope 3.16.30.1 el 24-10-2026. No se atribuye una captura GPU independiente ni una matriz física HDR completa.
- Repositorio reorganizado: README breves en ambos idiomas, dos guías técnicas y documentación centrada en el plugin. ZIP simplificado, sin expedientes de tienda ni documentos administrativos.
- **Misma versión y runtime:** esta limpieza cambia documentación y empaquetado, no el plugin validado. El tag original `v1.2.0` permanece intacto; el paquete documental se genera desde el [commit de limpieza](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/tree/f20d02fe91bcd1abbda1042b26df67110ef2209c).

[Guía en español](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/README_ES.md) · [Compatibilidad y comparación con 1.1.0](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md#español) · [Desarrollo](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#español)

## English

### Changes

- **SGSR on SteamOS:** QAM Sharp is promoted from FSR `2` to SGSR `5` when the active Gamescope supports it. Checks run every ~750 ms plus X11 response time; this is not an atomic Gamescope modification.
- **Detection fixed:** restricted `/proc/PID/exe` access is handled using the process's validated observed absolute executable, without substituting PATH or granting root to the plugin.
- **QAM and controls:** preserve the selected scaler on modern SteamOS; NIS/FSR overrides are exclusive and the UI shows SGSR status.
- **Compatibility preserved:** twelve Ubuntu/UGM methods, legacy SteamOS, application-HDR policy and 0–5 sharpening remain unchanged.

To use SGSR, leave **Use NIS** and **Use FSR** off and choose **Sharp** in Steam's QAM. HDR input retains Gamescope's FSR fallback; HDR output with an SDR game does not itself hide FSR.

### Installation

Download the ZIP and `.sha256` file into the same directory:

```bash
sha256sum -c sharp-filter-selector-v1.2.0.zip.sha256
unzip sharp-filter-selector-v1.2.0.zip
cd sharp-filter-selector
./install.sh
```

Reload the plugin through Decky or restart Steam/Gaming Mode to load it. Existing selections are retained. The ZIP is for installation; complete sources and tests remain in the repository.

### Validation and organization

- **48 tests passed:** 41 Python and 7 frontend tests, including 90 filter/scaler/override cases. Types, build and installer checks also pass.
- The maintainer confirmed operation on SteamOS 3.9.5 / Gamescope 3.16.30.1 on 2026-10-24. This is not an independent GPU trace or a complete physical HDR matrix.
- Repository reorganized: concise English/Spanish READMEs, two technical guides and plugin-focused documentation. The ZIP is simplified, without store-submission or administrative documents.
- **Same version and runtime:** this cleanup changes documentation/packaging, not the validated plugin. The original `v1.2.0` tag remains unchanged; the documentation package is generated from the [cleanup commit](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/tree/f20d02fe91bcd1abbda1042b26df67110ef2209c).

[English guide](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/README.md) · [Compatibility and 1.1.0 comparison](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md) · [Development](https://github.com/N3ruk/Sharp-Filter-Selector/blob/main/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md)

**Wake your Steam Deck from sleep by pressing the home button on any Bluetooth controller** — Xbox, DualSense, Switch Pro, 8BitDo, and more. Just like an Xbox or PlayStation console.

koua29/savewaypoint.name: v0.2.0 — Sync your non-Steam saves to your own GitHub
koua29/savewaypoint.body:
First stable release. SaveWaypoint finds the game saves nothing else is backing up — emulators, GOG/itch titles, anything you added to Steam as a non-Steam shortcut — and syncs them to a **private repo on your own GitHub account**. No server of ours, no subscription, and because every backup is a commit, your version history comes free.

### What it does

- **Finds saves on its own.** Known emulator locations, plus a scan of Proton prefixes. Each entry is rated by what is actually in the folder: 🟢 detected (a `SaveGames` folder or `.sav` files are there), 🟡 probable, 🔴 nothing saved yet.
- **Leaves Steam games alone.** Steam Cloud already syncs them and a second writer racing it helps nobody, so they are filtered out — switchable, for the games Cloud does not cover.
- **Signs in from your phone.** GitHub device flow: the Deck shows a short code, you approve it on your phone. No keyboard, no browser on the handheld.
- **Test before you trust it.** Checks a save can be archived *and* written back, without uploading anything.
- **Restore any earlier backup** from the commit history.
- **Updates itself**, on a stable or beta channel.

### Getting started

1. Create a GitHub OAuth App and tick **Enable Device Flow** (see the README).
2. Paste its Client ID, press **Connect GitHub**, approve on your phone.
3. **Manage saves…**, switch on what you want, then **Back up now**.

### Known limitation

Backing up is proven on a Steam Deck and the archives were verified to hold real save data. **Restoring has not yet been exercised on a device.** The code path is tested, but before you rely on it, do a dry run: back up a save, then restore the copy you just made.

### Install

Download `SaveWaypoint.zip` below, then on the Deck in Desktop mode:

```bash
unzip -o SaveWaypoint.zip -d ~/homebrew/plugins/
sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader
```

## DeckyPiP v1.0.0 (MVP)

DeckyPiP `v1.0.0` is the first stable MVP release of a Picture-in-Picture video overlay plugin for Steam Deck Gaming Mode (Decky Loader + gamescope).

### Highlights
- PiP and Expand overlay modes for web video over running games.
- Quick Link provider dropdown:
  - Google
  - YouTube
  - Plex
  - Twitch
  - Netflix
- Position presets + custom drag placement.
- Per-site profile system with:
  - Site profile selection
  - Add new profile
  - Save site profile
  - Fit-to-window toggle
- DRM-safe flow:
  - No DRM circumvention
  - DRM mode launches Widevine-capable browser (Chrome/Chromium)
  - Clear fallback to Desktop Mode when overlay composition is unavailable
- Per-game and global persistence for settings.
- Optional local playback through `mpv` (non-DRM).

### Stability / UX Improvements Included
- Removed incomplete zoom feature entirely for a cleaner, predictable MVP.
- Removed display-profile sizing complexity and simplified PiP sizing behavior.
- Strengthened overlay audio-volume handling with browser-level and in-page enforcement fallbacks.
- Cleaned and aligned UI controls for current supported feature set.

### Technical Notes
- Frontend: TypeScript + React (`dist/index.js`)
- Backend: Python (`main.py`) for persistence and launcher helpers
- Decky Store-compatible layout: `plugin.json`, `main.py`, `dist/index.js`
- Semantic versioning promoted to stable release: `1.0.0`

### Download Artifact
- ZIP: `DeckyPiP-1.0.0.zip`
- SHA256: `bcadc7019a76c7356193e8180cd0d30c81039ae1f36090a5f6adc087af57a929`

### Known Limitations
- Some sites/players (especially DRM/proprietary playback paths) may still limit direct control of in-overlay volume.
- True external-overlay behavior for DRM browser windows remains dependent on SteamOS/gamescope build behavior.

drewboardman/decky-wifi-guard.name: Wi-Fi Guard v0.1.0
drewboardman/decky-wifi-guard.body:
Wi-Fi Guard pauses Steam downloads while connected to a chosen Wi-Fi network and restores downloads when leaving, while preserving pre-existing pauses.

- Event-driven Steam network and download subscriptions: no periodic polling, pings, or active Wi-Fi scans.
- Native Decky panel with current-network selection, an editable SSID, and a master switch.
- Pure decision algebra, small effect interfaces, and separate Steam/Decky/storage/NetworkManager adapters.
- Fault containment for callbacks, async operations, React rendering, startup, and cleanup. Bounded event processing and operation deadlines stop automatic protection on unexpected faults; recovery requires an explicit retry.
- Atomic settings and pause-ownership persistence for reload recovery.

Validation: 53 automated tests, TypeScript checking, production build, and archive validation. Live Steam Deck acceptance (including sleep/wake and native API compatibility) still requires on-device testing. The frontend shares Steam's…

danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.name: v1.4.0 — the builder on the AYN Thor's bottom screen, under Armada OS
danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.body:
### Added

- **The builder on the AYN Thor's bottom screen, under Armada OS.** A new *Bottom screen* section in the Quick Access panel puts the builder on the Thor's second screen, by touch, while you play on the top one. It shows the team, the selected line, and the details of whichever Digimon you tap, with the same edits as the builder: *I'm here*, change branch, evolve, devolve, remove, lock, reorder, and start a new line from a stage-by-stage grid.
- **Both screens stay in step.** An edit on either one shows up on the other at once: the bottom screen waits on the plugin for changes rather than polling, and the plugin tells the Steam UI when the bottom screen saves.
- **Kind to the OLED.** With no touch for two minutes the bottom screen dims, and after ten it goes black. The touch that wakes it doesn't press anything.

### Notes

- The bottom screen is drawn natively: the plugin borrows the panel from gamescope as a DRM lease and draws it with the system's Python and cairo, the way Panel de Control's bottom screen does. Armada's own bottom-screen desktop is paused while it's on, and comes back when it's switched off.
- The section only appears under Armada on a device with a second screen. Elsewhere the plugin behaves exactly as before.
- Only one app can have the bottom screen. If another one has it, the section says so and keeps retrying.

danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.name: v1.3.0 — show the personality an evolution arrives with
danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.body:
### Added

- **The *Next up* view names the base personality you're evolving into.** Each row's next evolution now reads `stage · attribute · personality`, so you can see that the Mega you're working towards arrives *Zealous* before you commit the Agent Rank to it. It sits on the line that was already there, so the rows don't get taller and six lines still fit in the panel.
- **Base personality in the details modal too.** Pressing **A** on a Digimon in the builder now shows its base personality in the header, beside its stage, attribute and type — so the personality you saw in *Next up* is there when you open the evolution to check it.
- **And on the branch picker.** Each option in *Change* / *Evolve* lists the personality it arrives with next to its requirements, which is the moment you're actually choosing between branches.

### Notes

- The personality shown is the Digimon's *base* personality, the one it evolves in with — not whatever the Digimon currently has. It was already in the shipped dataset, so this needs no data regeneration and doesn't change the bundle or `digimon.json`.

### Install

Download the zip below and install it from **Decky → gear icon → Developer → Install Plugin from File**, or unzip it into `~/homebrew/plugins/` and restart `plugin_loader`.

danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.name: v1.2.0 — track where each line is, and what's next
danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.body:
### Added

- **Mark where you are in a line.** Each evolution line can now carry the stage you've actually reached: press **Y** on a Digimon in the builder (or use *I'm here* in its details modal) and it's badged **NOW**. Pressing Y on the marked stage again clears it, as does *Clear the current-stage mark* in the line's ⋮ menu. The mark works on locked lines too — the lock protects a line's members, and where you've got to isn't one of them.
- **A *Next up* view in the Quick Access panel.** The panel now switches between two views: *Lines*, the team overview it has always shown, and *Next up*, which gives each line the evolution it's working towards and the Agent Rank, stat, item or Jogress requirements to get there — the thing you actually want mid-battle. Pressing **Y** on a line there marks that evolution as reached without opening the builder.

### Notes

- Lines with no mark are read as sitting on their first stage, and say so, so *Next up* is useful before anything has been…

### Changed

- **Opening a line from the overview lands on the line.** Pressing A on a line in the panel still jumps to the builder, but focus now starts on that line's first Digimon in the detail panel on the right instead of on the team list, so the d-pad carries on from where you were pointing. danielcamilo1/decky-digimon-sts-team-bui.body:
Fixes for d-pad navigation, so focus moves the way things are actually laid out on screen.

### Fixed
- **Sidebar buttons move by position** — left from *Clear* now lands on *Share* beside it, instead of jumping to *Add line* at the top of the other column.
- **Moving between the two panels** — d-pad right off a line's ⋮ enters the evolution line, and left off the first Digimon goes back to the team list.

infernokun/syncdeck.name: SyncDeck 1.2.1
infernokun/syncdeck.body:
Security fixes. Recommended for anyone using the PC auto-add option.

- The PC's Syncthing API key was being written to the plugin log in plain text. It no longer is. If you set up the PC option on an earlier version, clear ~/homebrew/logs/SyncDeck/ and consider regenerating the key in your PC's Syncthing.
- Folders that hold credentials (~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg, and Decky's own directory, which contains this plugin's settings file) can no longer be picked as a save folder.
- Hardened the systemd unit the plugin writes for Syncthing autostart against unusual directory names.
- A corrupt appinfo.vdf no longer empties the game list.

The README now has a Security section describing how API keys are handled, what the plugin will not touch, and the fact that the connection to your PC's Syncthing does not verify TLS because its certificate is self-signed.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/infernokun/SyncDeck/compare/v1.2.0...v1.2.1
