bradleysharp/amethyst-deploy-decky.name: v0.1.0
bradleysharp/amethyst-deploy-decky.body:
First release of **Amethyst Deploy**, a Decky Loader plugin for running [Amethyst Mod Manager](https://github.com/ChrisDKN/Amethyst-Mod-Manager) from Gaming Mode on the Steam Deck, using only the controller. No Desktop Mode needed.

This is an early release: it works on a Deck, but some flows have only been tested on a development machine (see below).

## What it does

- **Quick Access menu:** pick a game and profile, then **Deploy & Play**, **Deploy only** or **Restore vanilla**. It can also install or update Amethyst itself.
- **Mods tab:** turn mods on and off (A), move them (X, then the D-pad, then A), and uninstall them (Y).
- **Load order tab** (games with plugin files): plugin order, missing-master warnings, and **Sort with LOOT**.
- **Get mods tab:**
  - **Nexus Mods:** browse and search. Premium accounts install in one press. Free accounts open the file's page in Steam's browser and press Slow download once; the mod installs when the download finishes.
  - **Thunderstore:** browse, search and install, including dependencies.
  - **Other sites:** any mod archive saved to Downloads can be installed.
- **Downloads tab:** install any archive in `~/Downloads`.
- **Installer options:** FOMOD and BAIN installers show their options as controller pages.
- **Setup tab:** finds installed games from Steam, Heroic, Unifideck, Lutris, Faugus, Bottles and non-Steam shortcuts. It checks each game's folder, and has a controller folder picker for anything it can't find. Profiles can be created here too.

## Requirements

- Steam Deck (SteamOS) with [Decky Loader](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader).
- Amethyst Mod Manager's Flatpak. If it's missing, the plugin offers to install it from the developer's own Flatpak remote.
- For Nexus Mods: a Nexus account. Log in once from the plugin; it opens Nexus's page in Steam's browser.

## Install

1. In Decky: **Settings → General → Developer mode** on.
2. **Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP**, and pick `amethyst-deploy-v0.1.0.zip`.

## Known limitations

- **Logging in to Nexus,** and pressing **Slow download** on a free account, are done on Nexus's own page in Steam's browser with the trackpad. Everything else works with the gamepad alone.
- **mod.io and Steam Workshop** aren't supported yet. Mods from those sites can still be installed from the Downloads tab.
- **Not yet tried on a Deck:** Nexus Premium downloads, BAIN installers, and some focus details (after "Load more" and returning from mod details). Reports welcome.
- Amethyst changes often; this release was built against its source as of October 2026.

Licensed GPL-3.0-or-later, like Amethyst Mod Manager.

1m93/deckyeclipse.name: v0.2.0
1m93/deckyeclipse.body:
More of Sunshine and Moonlight from Gaming Mode: stream profiles, Steam games for other devices, automatic discovery, Tailscale, a network test and backups.

**Install or update:** Decky settings → Developer → *Install plugin from URL*, with the link of `Eclipse-0.2.0.zip` below. Settings are kept.

### Play: stream games from a PC (Moonlight)
- **Stream profiles**: save the current settings under a name (TV, Hotel Wi-Fi...), switch in one step here or in the Quick Access menu, give a host its own profile. Saved profiles can be renamed and deleted.
- *Hosts* and *Stream quality* are one **Streaming** settings page.
- **Network test** (host settings, Y on a host, or the Playing card): delay and stability to the host, this device's Wi-Fi or VPN link, a suggested bitrate and a button to use it.
- **Tailscale**: *Add a host* lists PCs in your tailnet; for a PC added at home, its Tailscale address is saved so the same host streams away from home.

### Share: let other devices stream from this one (Sunshine)
- **Games for other devices**: pick installed Steam games (with their covers) that Moonlight on the other device starts directly. Closing the app also ends the game here.
- **Automatic discovery**: when SteamOS does not let Sunshine announce itself (`avahi::entry_group_new() failed: Not permitted`), Eclipse announces the device, so Moonlight lists it on its own.
- **Sunshine's options** in Settings → Sharing (name, bitrate cap, encoder, codecs, audio, controllers, input, encryption, network) and the common ones in the Share tab, with *Restart now* to apply.
- **Notification when a device wants to pair**; pressing it opens the PIN entry.
- Pairing requests no longer show Moonlight's placeholder name "roth": the device's network name or address is shown, and the name you enter is saved.
- The Sharing card says which device is streaming, as far as the network shows.
- **Turn off on low battery** (10/20/30 %, off by default).
- This device's Tailscale address is shown for streaming from outside.

### General
- **Backup and restore**: profiles, stream and host settings, Sunshine's options and games, to this device or a microSD card / USB drive (survives a SteamOS reinstall). Restore is also offered on the welcome screen.
- New plugin and tab icons; the author is shown in About.

Devices paired before this version may be listed as "Unnamed device": unpair and pair again to name them.

venatrix-ritz/ratatoskr.name: Ratatoskr 0.2.0
venatrix-ritz/ratatoskr.body:
Second pre-release of Ratatoskr: the AYN Thor's bottom AMOLED as a trackpad, keyboard and quick-settings surface, on Armada OS with Decky Loader.

**Tested on one Thor only.** Ratatoskr was developed on Armada `20261006.9c7dd3e` (kernel 7.2.6); which Armada build that Thor ran for the 0.2.0 tests was not rechecked, and other builds have not been tried. Read `README.md` for the honest status and `docs/` for details.

**New in 0.2.0**
- **PS mode for Chiaki-NG:** while Chiaki-NG streams a PS5, the bottom screen is the PS5 touchpad (one finger: swipe, tap to click, press and hold to hold the click) with Create, PS, Options and Mic buttons. It goes back to the previous mode when Chiaki-NG loses focus.
- **Haptic feedback:** a 15 ms buzz from the Thor's motor for tap clicks, keys and on-screen buttons (not for pointer moves, scrolls or key repeat), with an on/off switch in the Decky panel.
- **Key preview:** a bubble above the held key shows the character it types.
- **Hide button:** blanks the bottom screen except for an Open button; while hidden the whole screen is a trackpad.
- **AMOLED black theme and burn-in protection:** a pure black background, a slow 1.5 px orbit of the whole UI, and an idle dim of lit pixels 30 s after the last touch.
- **Keyboard:** settings for repeat delay, repeat interval and the Caps Lock double-tap window, larger key labels, and a taller header with bigger buttons.
- **Gleipnir view (optional):** battery and charge-cap status in the ribbon and Quick Controls when Gleipnir is installed.
- **Removed:** the bottom-screen debug HUD. The `DBG-nnn` codes, the log and **Run Diagnostics** stay.
- **13 fixes**, among them Shift and Caps Lock, modifiers left pressed after leaving the keyboard, Split-mode drags across the split line, fingers lost after `SYN_DROPPED`, and `config.json` losing keys other tools wrote. Full list in `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Not yet tested on hardware**
- PS mode has run in one short live PS5 stream, but its swipes, tap clicks and buttons have not each been confirmed on the PS5.
- The haptic buzz's strength and length are first guesses. Say so in an issue if it is too weak, too strong or too long.
- The key preview and the Hide button pass their tests and render correctly on the Thor, but have not been checked on the glass.
- Installing the 0.2.0 zip has not been run on a Thor; the zip route was last tested with 0.1.0.
- The optional narrow sudo rule is untested, and what the bottom screen does across sleep is unconfirmed.

**Known issues**
- While a game runs, Ratatoskr costs about 9 to 12 % of one CPU core (measured on 2026-11-20). A reduction is in testing and is not in this release.
- PS mode is one finger only (gamescope turns a touch into a pointer move with the button held), and the outer 6 % of the PS5 touchpad cannot be reached.

**What it changes on your Thor**
- A systemd user service, `touch-master.service`, replaces Armada's stock bottom-screen session while it runs (`Conflicts=armada-bottom-screen.service`). Stopping Ratatoskr from its Decky panel brings the stock session back.
- It grabs the bottom touchscreen (`EVIOCGRAB`) and creates virtual mouse, keyboard and touch devices through `/dev/uinput`.
- Settings live in `~/.config/thor-input/config.json`. Bottom-screen brightness is written with `sudo -n`; the optional rule in `systemd/touch-master-backlight.sudoers` narrows that.
- **Pen +** writes `~/.config/environment.d/50-ratatoskr-cursor.conf` while it is on and deletes it when it is turned off.

**Install**
- Not in the Armada Store yet.
- From the zip by hand: `Ratatoskr.zip` holds one top-level `thor-input/` folder. Unpack it into `~/homebrew/plugins/` with `sudo` (that folder is root-owned), then run `sudo systemctl restart plugin_loader.service` so Decky loads it. On first load the plugin copies the driver, the user service and the launcher entries into your home folder and starts the service. This is what the Armada Store's installer does; the by-hand steps themselves have not been tried.
- From a PC: `scripts/deploy.sh` (see `docs/installation.md`). Do not mix the two routes on one Thor: after a zip install, run `deploy.sh` once, which removes the leftover `driver/` folder.
- Uninstall: see `docs/installation.md`.

`Ratatoskr.zip` SHA-256: `7d17f25d9f98348d748277348a734c9fe02c1dfa24171760a8e3c7ca1024b24c`

Not affiliated with AYN or Armada.

zensenshi/jarngrip.name: JarnGrip 0.10.0
zensenshi/jarngrip.body:
**Spell names and pictures on the number pad, a WoW addon, and a status card.**

- **Your WoW action bars on the number keys.** The new **JarnGrip addon** (in `wow-addon/`, copied into WoW's `Interface/AddOns` by hand) saves what each action bar key holds. By default each number key then shows the name of the spell, item or macro it casts, and a swipe's fan names what that swipe casts. When the pad's copy of your bars is out of date, the addon offers a one-tap **Reload** at login. See the guide to set it up.
- **Number pad icons.** Pick **Icons** under **Number keys show** in Decky, and the numbers become square keys with your own pictures, one for the tap and one for each swipe. With the addon, keys without a picture show the spell's icon or name. **Edit icons…** opens a full-screen page to pick them, with search and **Fill from file names**.
- **A status card.** Tap the clock and battery for the network (Wi-Fi, signal, the Thor's IP address, internet), the battery (time left, watts, health) and the temperatures. A touch anywhere closes it, and it closes by itself after 20 seconds.
- **Icons on WoW's buttons** on the Interface, Target and Utility pages, drawn in the theme's colors.
- **Swipes now go toward their squares:** up for Shift (FFXI: Ctrl) as before, **left** for Ctrl (FFXI: Alt), **down** to cancel. Pictures saved for the old swipe down move to the swipe left.
- **Japanese keyboard bindings for WoW:** `/jarngrip jis` makes the pad's `=` key do what `^` does. Your saved bindings are never changed.
- **A tidier Decky panel**, in sections that open with a tap, and WoW's chat radial in the game's chat colors.
- **Fixes:** swipes keep up with your thumb in game, and Remap a control keeps what you pick again.

**Install or update:** download `JarnGrip-0.10.0.zip`, unzip it, and from the `JarnGrip` folder run `./scripts/install-from-pc.sh armada@THOR_IP`. To show your bars, copy `wow-addon/JarnGrip` into WoW's `Interface/AddOns` folder.

Note: Steam client builds from mid-October 2026 need Decky Loader 3.3.0 or newer; earlier versions crash when the Decky menu opens (Decky issue #988). Decky 3.3.0 is also the first with an official ARM build.

zensenshi/jarngrip.name: JarnGrip 0.9.0
zensenshi/jarngrip.body:
**A Desktop profile, and a Chat radial for WoW and FFXI.**

- **Desktop profile**, for the desktop, the web and anything else that is not a game. Pick **Desktop** under Game in Decky.

k1tsune12/decky-steamgriddb-kitsune.body:
# 🦊 SteamGridDB Kitsune Edition 1.9.4

## 🎞️ Optimize Animated Artwork
- Animated capsules and logos are shrunk to the size Steam shows them when you apply them, keeping every frame and its exact timing. Only the part of each frame that changes is stored, so they stay light to play back.
- Full size animations can make the home screen flicker on some devices (seen on Bazzite while the background zooms), and they cost GPU and battery everywhere. A 600x900 capsule with 410 frames went from 4.6 MB to 1.5 MB.
- On by default. Turn it off in the plugin settings if you want the original files.

## 📦 How to install
1. Download **SteamGridDB.zip** below
2. In Decky, open **Settings** and turn on **Developer mode**
3. Open the **Developer** tab and choose **Install Plugin from ZIP File**

It replaces the regular SteamGridDB plugin and keeps your settings. ✅

keys, full configurations or raw logs.

forlarin/deck-doctor.name: Deck Doctor v0.5.0
forlarin/deck-doctor.body:
New: controller layout check.

If a game's saved controller layout has a main button mixed up (for example A sends RB, so nothing on the Deck sends A), the checkup now says so and shows which button is wrong. **Open controller settings** takes you straight to that game's layout, and the guide explains how to switch to a standard template. Steam's own templates and community layouts are left alone.

Found on Assassin's Creed Mirage, where an old saved layout made the game feel like it ignored the A button.

forlarin/deck-doctor.name: Deck Doctor v0.4.1
forlarin/deck-doctor.body: Fix: games using a CheatDeck trainer whose file name has an apostrophe (for example "Assassin's Creed Mirage Trainer - FLiNG.exe") closed after 2 seconds with no log, because Proton can't read the path. Deck Doctor now spots this and offers **Fix the launch options**, which escapes the apostrophe. The trainer file isn't changed. Found and verified on Assassin's Creed Mirage.

forlarin/deck-doctor.name: Deck Doctor v0.4.0
forlarin/deck-doctor.body:
New: freeze detection, suggested by JawessOme.

- **The graphics chip froze**: the checkup reads the Deck's kernel log around the launch and tells you when the GPU hung and reset.
- **The Deck ran out of memory**: shows which program Linux had to close.
- **The game didn't close normally**: Steam saw the game start but never end, which usually means a freeze followed by holding the power button.
- **Force close the game**: while a game is running, close it and everything it started (launcher, Proton, a trainer) from the Quick Access menu. Press twice to confirm.

Each one has a How to fix guide.

forlarin/deck-doctor.name: Deck Doctor v0.3.1
forlarin/deck-doctor.body: Fix: games Steam's library doesn't know (uninstalled games, demos) now show their real name instead of "App 12345". Thanks to Koonga for reporting it.

forlarin/deck-doctor.name: Deck Doctor v0.3.0
forlarin/deck-doctor.body:
## EmuDeck support

Suggested on Reddit: "tell you what emulator isn't working". For games added by EmuDeck, Deck Doctor now names the emulator and console, and checks the usual reasons it fails:

- **Emulator not installed**, e.g. after a SteamOS reset, or a Switch emulator EmuDeck no longer ships
- **Game file missing**: moved, renamed, or the SD card isn't in
- **Wii U disc images (.wux/.wud) with no key** in Cemu's keys.txt
- **Missing PS1 / PS2 BIOS**, recognised by file size, so a PS1 BIOS isn't mistaken for a PS2 one
- **Missing Switch prod.keys**

If none of those turn anything up, it still tells you which emulator to open to see the error. Each problem has a step-by-step guide in the plugin.

## Install / update
1. Download `deck-doctor.zip` below.
2. Decky → ⚙ → Developer → **Install plugin from ZIP**.

BIOS files, keys and games have to come from your own consoles. Deck Doctor only checks whether they're there.

This release adds a Nintendo Switch Online icon maker: build your user icon the way the console does, from a character, a frame and a background.

## What's new in 1.4.0

- **Nintendo Switch Online icons.** Open **My Page → User Settings → Nintendo Switch Online Icons** (or the new button in **Change Icon**):
  - Pick a **character**, a **frame** and a **background** from **66 game collections** and **over 7,500 parts**: Mario Kart World, Super Mario Bros. Wonder, Zelda, Splatoon, Kirby, Pokémon, Animal Crossing, Metroid, Miis and more. Frames and backgrounds can also be set to **None**.
  - A live preview shows the stacked icon as you go. **Surprise Me** (or **X**) picks a random one, and **Check for new icons** refreshes the list when the collection grows.
  - Your icon appears in the status bar, on My Page and in the Quick Settings menu.

- My Page now shows a new icon as soon as you save it, and the icon editors take over the page so the controller's focus goes straight into them.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/kromossomom-debug/decky-switch2-dashboard/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for earlier versions.

1. Download **`switch2-dashboard.zip`** below.
2. In Game Mode: **Quick Access (`…`) → Decky → ⚙ Settings → General**, turn on **Developer mode**.
3. **Developer → Install plugin from ZIP**, pick `switch2-dashboard.zip`.

Updating? Install the new ZIP the same way; your settings are kept. The plugin panel should then show v1.4.0 at the bottom. If it still shows an older version, restart Steam.

zacharyqin/decky-sideloader.body:
## [0.4.0] - 2026-10-27

### English

- Show package warnings in a native confirmation dialog as soon as preparation completes. Continuing opens Decky's installation confirmation; cancellation keeps the prepared task available for an explicit retry. Preserve uninstall-and-reinstall confirmation and do not replay a pending dialog after reload.
- Bundle a maintained, independently versioned `plugin.json.name` to GitHub repository map for offline first-use recognition. Preserve explicit bindings, completed-install links, takeover repositories, stopped tracking and identity/ownership guards; fall back to package metadata when an entry is absent.
- Add a six-language Repository map section in Settings with revision/count/date and a separate update action using the selected network mode. Validate and atomically replace complete snapshots, retain the last good version on failure, prevent downgrades and changes during installation/release checks, and drain updates on reload. Validate maintained data and revision changes in CI and include the source-commit snapshot in runtime ZIPs.

- 安装包准备完成后，以原生确认弹窗展示安装警告；继续后进入 Decky 安装确认，取消则保留已准备任务供用户主动重试。保留卸载并安装的独立确认，重载后不自动重弹。

- 设置新增六语“仓库映射表”区段，展示修订号、条目数、日期并单独更新，复用所选网络模式；完整校验后原子替换整表，失败保留旧版、防止降级，安装／版本检查期间不切换，重载时排空更新任务。CI 校验数据与修订号变更，运行 ZIP 附带源提交中的映射快照。

burghr/decky-xodus-chat.body:
First release of XBOX Chat, a Decky plugin for Xbox friends and text chat through Xodus Nexus.

Unofficial side project, provided as is. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft or Xbox, or by the Xodus Nexus project.

## Features
- Friends list in the Quick Access menu, sorted by the newest message, with a preview of the last message.
- Chat with the newest message at the bottom. Enter or the arrow button sends.
- B goes back from a chat to the friends list. The gamepad focus goes to the text box when a chat opens.
- Count of new messages for each friend, and an optional background check every 2 minutes with a notification.
- The last friends and messages show at once after a restart.

## Requirements
- Decky Loader.
- Xodus Nexus 0.4.0 or later with backend 0.2.12 or later, signed in. Nexus does not need to run.

Tested on a Steam Deck (SteamOS 3.9). Not yet tested on ARM devices.

## Install
1. Download `decky-xodus-chat-0.1.0.zip`.
2. In Decky, open Settings > Developer.
3. Select "Install Plugin from ZIP" and select the ZIP.

If you installed a test build named "Xodus Chat", uninstall it first.

## Privacy
The plugin keeps friends and recent messages in a base64 file (mode 0600) so that they show at once after a restart. Base64 is not encryption. See the README for details.

## Fix: overlay rendered into the wrong Steam window
A two-window regression test reproduced the v0.7.1 failure: the component was rendered into a 1280×800 game UI window, but its overlay was attached to the module's 320×240 loader window. The game UI had no labels while recognition and speech continued.

The same test now shows two labels in the game window and none in the loader. It also verifies correct capture coordinates, game-window resizing/letterboxing, no movement when the loader window resizes, and correct cleanup.

- Light 12% screen…

Live Steam layouts checked at 1280×800 and 1920×1080, native spatial focus/details/zoom/marking exercised, and existing dropdown, search, rule scroll, generation and persistent clipboard checks repeated in the preview. wx40217/decky-brightness.name: v0.1.5 — 中英文界面与默认下限说明
wx40217/decky-brightness.body:
新增简体中文与英文界面，覆盖按钮、状态和异常提示。加载时优先使用 Steam 界面语言，接口不可用时回退到浏览器首选语言；其他语言使用英文。插件内部名称保持不变，已有自定义下限和亮度控制逻辑保留。

中英文 README 已显著注明：默认 44% 仅来自作者在自己的 Steam Deck OLED 上的个人测试，不是通用的“不频闪阈值”，不保证适合其他机器或 SDR/HDR、刷新率组合；请在自己的设备上确认并保存下限。

48 项自动测试、类型检查、构建及中英文安装包界面验证通过。v0.1.5 已安装到测试 Deck，核实 Steam 中文语言识别正常，原有 44.08136% 精确下限和亮度保留。英文界面由安装包模拟验证覆盖，英文真机显示尚未验证。

仍为手动调光版本：系统自适应需关闭，下限仅限制插件内操作。此前环境光测试确认系统自适应绕过前端亮度拦截，原生最小/最大值写入未生效；本版没有开放系统自适应下限。

Adds Simplified Chinese and English UI, including status and error messages, with Steam-language detection and browser-language fallback. Existing custom floors are preserved. Both READMEs emphasize that the default 44% is based solely on personal testing on the author's own unit and is not a universal flicker-free threshold. Manual plugin controls only; system adaptive brightness must remain off.

48 automated tests, type checking, build and compiled UI validation in both languages passed. Installed on the test Deck with the original exact floor preserved; English layout on real hardware remains unverified.

wx40217/decky-brightness.name: v0.1.4 — 统一中文字体，精简调光面板
wx40217/decky-brightness.body:
统一使用 Steam Deck 系统已有的简体中文 Noto 字体，增大微调按钮和状态文字。精简面板，删除重复说明、兼容性占位内容和日常无须使用的检查按钮；已有精确下限完整保留。

42 项自动测试、类型检查、构建及安装包界面验证通过。已在 Steam Deck OLED / SteamOS 3.8.28 / Decky 3.2.9 上核实字体和按钮布局，并在《赛博朋克 2077》SDR、HDR10 PQ 动态 3D 基准场景的实际 60、90 Hz 下验证：关闭插件面板后调亮、返回精确下限均成功，实际背光读数随之变化。HDR 游戏内容反馈及元数据已确认。

45 的目标帧率请求被映射成 90 Hz，实际 45 Hz 尚未验证。同一控制百分比在 SDR、HDR 下的背光读数不同，调光验证不代表物理频闪已消除。本次临时绕过 MAKO 隐藏 HDR 的启动包装器，测试后恢复原设置；开启 MAKO 时的 HDR 组合尚未验证。系统自适应下限仍未开放。

安装包保持 v0.1.4，不包含任何临时探查接口；本次仅更新真机验证说明。

wx40217/decky-brightness.name: v0.1.3 — 默认下限 44%，自动读取系统自适应
wx40217/decky-brightness.body: 没有自定义配置时，亮度下限默认使用 44%；已有自定义下限保留原始精度。直接读取并监听 Steam 系统自适应状态，移除手动确认开关；自适应开启或读取失败时暂停插件调光，关闭后自动恢复。每次调光前重新读取系统状态，并处理 Steam 浮点舍入，避免回报越过下限。28 项 TypeScript 和 14 项 Python 测试、类型检查、构建及安装包界面验证通过，已在 Steam Deck OLED / SteamOS 3.8.28 / Decky 3.2.9 上安装验证真实状态读取、微调、下限限制及配置保留。此版仍仅限制插件内调光，尚未实现系统自适应亮度下限；44% 是作者个人校准值，SDR、HDR 和刷新率兼容性需分别验证。

wx40217/decky-brightness.name: v0.1.2：校准调光与精细微调
wx40217/decky-brightness.body: 未设置下限时，确认系统自适应已关闭即可在 0–100% 范围内校准。滑块步长为 0.01 个百分点，新增 ±0.01、±0.1 个百分点微调按钮，连续点击按待处理目标累加。保存后，滑块和微调统一受原始精度下限限制。收紧系统亮度确认误差，避免旧回报误判成功。30 项自动测试、类型检查、构建与编译后插件验证通过。系统自适应下限仍未开放。

wx40217/decky-brightness.name: v0.1.1：修复游戏模式检测
wx40217/decky-brightness.body: 修复 Gamescope 主线程更名为 gamescope-wl 后被误判为桌面模式、持续清空当前亮度的问题。新增可执行文件识别，并在当前亮度旁显示停用原因。26 项自动测试、类型检查、构建和编译后插件验证通过。本版仍为插件内手动调光，系统自适应下限尚未开放。

vivoxti/deckyroundcorners.name: Round Corners 1.1.0
vivoxti/deckyroundcorners.body:
- 16:9 game toggle, saved per game. While a 16:9-only game is on screen, the
  corners move to its picture's edges, 40 pixels from the top and bottom on the
  Deck. They return to the screen corners in the frame Steam's menus, Quick
  Access or the library open, following Steam's composition state and focus
  without polling.
- Steam behaves as it does without the plugin. Steam's own interface already
  shows the corners, so Notification composition is requested only while a
  game is on screen with nothing over it, and only 0.4 s after Steam's
  interface has hidden. Holding it all the time, as before, caused two
  differences from stock Steam:
  - closing Quick Access flashed a black screen with an "Abort game" footer
    for up to a second;
  - side menus slid away instead of vanishing.
- Corners slide in diagonally from beyond the screen corners over 0.6 s,
  slowing gently into place, and slide out the same way: when turned on or
  off, and when they return over a game after a menu closes. In a 16:9 game
  they slide out of the black bars. The slide is a CSS transform transition
  that runs only during those changes.
- The top-left corner steps aside while Steam's volume popin is shown, so the
  popin is no longer cut off under it. It leaves in 0.11 s, half the time the
  popin takes to slide in, or at once on the Steam beta, whose popin covers
  most of its way in the first frames. A MutationObserver watches the class
  of the popin's single element.
- Works on the Steam beta from November 2026 with Decky Loader 4. That Steam
  is built from ES modules instead of webpack: it no longer exports its
  composition hook, and the volume popin's class names are inlined into its
  component. Both are also looked up inside Steam's modules there; stable
  Steam and Decky Loader 3 use the webpack lookups.
- The composition request is named "Round Corners" in Steam's composition log.
- After a reload or update, Decky can keep showing the old instance's panel
  while it stays open in Quick Access. That panel now asks you to reopen
  Round Corners instead of changing settings the new instance doesn't see.

## Installing

1. Copy `RoundCorners-1.1.0.zip` to the Deck.
2. In Decky, turn on Developer mode (Settings → General).
3. Open Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP File and choose the archive.
4. Open Round Corners and turn on Enable rounded corners.

If Round Corners was open in Quick Access while updating, go back to the plugin list and open it again.

See the [README](https://github.com/Vivoxti/DeckyRoundCorners#readme) for limitations and details.

- Per-game settings show in Steam's in-game green, including the slider while the running game controls the volume. Saved profiles form a compact list with a delete button.

**Game profiles restore your everyday settings**

bnm12/decky-avr-control.name: v0.5.0
bnm12/decky-avr-control.body:
**New**
- Live updates while the panel is open: changes from the remote or the receiver's app appear immediately on eISCP, Denon/Marantz, legacy Pioneer and HEOS (from protocol docs; not yet measured on hardware). Other receivers keep polling every 2 s.
- Late-night schedule: turn late night mode on and off at set times, optionally with a listening mode. A manual toggle wins until the next boundary.
- Opt-in: power the receiver on when the Steam device wakes, and off when it sleeps.
- Home Assistant: a "Find media players" picker and setup help.

**Under the hood**
Shared TCP connection handling, one control application behind a snapshot/intent interface, a settings repository (schema v4, migrates automatically), listening modes that distinguish the current mode from selectable ones, and CI on pnpm 12 like the Decky store.

eISCP is verified on a Pioneer VSX-935; all other drivers remain experimental.

bnm12/decky-avr-control.body:
New drivers, all **experimental** (built from vendor or community specs and tested against simulated receivers, not yet on real hardware):

- Sony receivers and soundbars (Audio Control API)
- Sonos and other UPnP/DLNA renderers (volume and mute only)
- Denon HEOS speakers and soundbars (volume and mute)
- Yamaha pre-MusicCast receivers (2010-2016, XML API)
- Denon/Marantz now fall back to the HTTP interface when telnet is busy

eISCP (verified on a Pioneer VSX-935) gains per-model volume scales with optional overrides in manual setup. Receivers that only report a volume step number now show it as a plain number instead of a percentage.

Own one of these? A short recording from `tools/avr_probe.py` makes the driver verified; see CONTRIBUTING.md.

cconroy11/frostdeck.name: FrostDeck 1.0.0
cconroy11/frostdeck.body:
## FrostDeck 1.0.0

Battle.net and World of Warcraft addons on the Steam Deck, from Gaming Mode. A Decky Loader plugin.

### What it does
- **Battle.net in one tap.** Downloads the official installer, runs it under Proton, and files it in a "Blizzard" collection in your Steam library.
- **Games launch from Steam.** Installed Battle.net games are detected and added as their own shortcuts that boot straight into the game, with library artwork.
- **WoW addons without a desktop.** Detects each installed flavour (Retail, Classic, Forever…), installs and updates addons from GitHub, WoWInterface and Tukui, and puts ConsolePort controller support one tap away.
- **Tidy removal.** Uninstall a game, remove just its shortcut, or reset everything; uninstalling the plugin itself leaves your games and shortcuts intact.

mrfunkill/decky-dualsense-wired.name: DualSense Wired v0.5.5
mrfunkill/decky-dualsense-wired.body:
## Русский

- **Геймпад больше не отключается при включённом микрофоне на системах без виртуального USB** (например, на ПК с Bazzite, где в ядре нет `dummy_hcd`). В этом режиме микрофон недоступен. Раньше плагин всё равно включал его, драйвер `hid-playstation` принимал голосовые пакеты за нажатия кнопки mute, и поток ответных команд обрывал Bluetooth. Теперь микрофон включается только с виртуальным USB-контроллером.
- **Панель плагина сообщает, если виртуальный USB недоступен**: «Нет аудиоустройства для игр и микрофона», с причиной. В этом случае на геймпад идёт только «Весь звук Deck на контроллер».
- **В отчёте об ошибке скрыто имя учётной записи** в путях (`/home/<user>/…`).

Обновление: панель плагина → «Проверить обновления». Установка с нуля: Decky → Разработчик → Установить плагин по URL →
`https://github.com/mrFunkill/decky-dualsense-wired/releases/download/v0.5.5/decky-dualsense-wired-v0.5.5.zip`

## English

- **The controller no longer disconnects with the microphone on, on systems without virtual USB** (e.g. a PC with Bazzite whose kernel has no `dummy_hcd`). The microphone is not available in that mode. Before, the plugin still turned it on; `hid-playstation` mistook the voice packets for mute button presses, and the flood of commands it sent back broke the Bluetooth link. Now the microphone is only turned on with the virtual USB controller.
- **The plugin panel says when virtual USB is unavailable**: "No game audio device and no microphone", with the reason. In that case only "All Deck audio" goes to the controller.
- **The bug report masks the account name** in paths (`/home/<user>/…`).

Update: plugin panel → "Check for updates". Fresh install: Decky → Developer → Install Plugin from URL →
`https://github.com/mrFunkill/decky-dualsense-wired/releases/download/v0.5.5/decky-dualsense-wired-v0.5.5.zip`

mrfunkill/decky-dualsense-wired.name: DualSense Wired v0.5.4
mrfunkill/decky-dualsense-wired.body:
## Русский

- **Отчёт об ошибке**: раздел «Отчёт об ошибке» в панели плагина, кнопка «Собрать логи». Она сохраняет в папку `~/Downloads` zip-архив с логами плагина, настройками, версиями системы, сведениями о геймпадах, драйверах, звуковых устройствах и Bluetooth. MAC-адреса скрыты, архив никуда не отправляется. Если что-то не работает, приложите этот файл к [issue](https://github.com/mrFunkill/decky-dualsense-wired/issues). Из Game Mode файл удобнее всего забрать через Desktop Mode или KDE Connect.
- **Тест геймпада с несколькими геймпадами**: если подключено больше одного, вверху страницы можно выбрать, какой проверять. Раньше страница всегда работала с первым, и, например, эффекты триггеров уходили на него.
- На странице теста объяснено, что микрофон по умолчанию выключен и где его включить.

mrfunkill/decky-dualsense-wired.name: DualSense Wired v0.5.3
mrfunkill/decky-dualsense-wired.body:
## Русский

- **Микрофон геймпада** (переключатель «Микрофон геймпада» в панели, по умолчанию выключен): микрофон геймпада или гарнитуры в нём работает в Steam, Discord и играх. Кнопка mute на геймпаде выключает микрофон, её индикатор горит. Пока микрофон включён, Bluetooth-геймпад работает с драйвером `hid-generic` вместо `hid-playstation`: тот принимает голосовые пакеты за нажатия mute. При включении и выключении микрофона геймпад один раз переподключается.
- **Наушники в разъёме геймпада**: когда они подключены, звук идёт в них, а не в динамик.
- **Быстрые триггеры** (включено по умолчанию): эффекты триггеров и подсветка отправляются сразу, отдельными отчётами, а не вместе со звуком. Если геймпад начнёт отключаться, выключите.
- **Нет хрипа при наложении звуков**: звук захватывается без обрезки и проходит через лимитер. Раньше, например, звук панели Steam поверх громкой музыки хрипел.

mrfunkill/decky-dualsense-wired.name: DualSense Wired v0.5.2
mrfunkill/decky-dualsense-wired.body:
## Русский

- **Меньше задержка звука и HD-вибрации — примерно на 20–25 мс.** Контроллер держит в буфере столько звука, сколько ему указано в заголовке аудиопотока; раньше плагин всегда указывал 48 мс (как DSX). Теперь по умолчанию 32 мс.
- **Ползунок «Буфер звука в контроллере»** (16–64 мс): меньше — меньше задержка, больше — меньше прерываний при загруженном Bluetooth. Меняется на лету.
- **Нет щелчка в начале звука**: кодировщик Opus работает непрерывно во время потока и начинает заново с каждым новым потоком.
- **Проверка обновлений**: раздел «Обновления» в панели плагина — показывает версию, проверяет релизы на GitHub и ставит новую версию одной кнопкой. Начиная с этой версии плагин можно обновлять прямо из панели.

Назначение полей заголовка аудиопотока подсмотрено в открытом проекте [DS5Dongle](https://github.com/awalol/DS5Dongle) (MIT); код не заимствовался.

Установка: Decky → Разработчик → Установить плагин по URL →…

mops1k/decky-gameartwork.name: GameArtwork v2.7.1
mops1k/decky-gameartwork.body:
GameArtwork v2.7.1 — a bug-fix release for the cross-source artwork plugin.

## Fixes

- **Settings were silently lost.** All settings shared one debounced writer, so
  a second change within the delay cancelled the first one: picking a game in
  the picker saved `external_name_` but dropped `nonsteam_`, and the old match
  came back after a restart. Writes are now queued per key and flushed when the
  menu closes.
- **Source status reported SteamGridDB as down.** The API sits behind
  Cloudflare, which answers `401` to the plain backend user agent even for a
  valid key, so the health panel always showed a failure. The check now uses the
  loader-like user agent and reports the real state.
- **The sources were queried one by one.** Every HTTP call blocked the plugin
  loop, so "parallel" source searches were serial (measured 4.7 s for five
  sources, now 2.35 s) and `Source Status` could freeze the plugin for the sum
  of all timeouts (3.2 s in the good case). All network work now…

## Artwork sources

- **GOG** is queried through its public catalog API instead of page scraping: portrait and wide capsules, a transparent logo and the store background.
- **Steam** artwork now includes the transparent logo PNG next to the capsules, hero and icon.
- **VNDB** screenshots fill the wide-capsule and hero slots, so visual novels have more than a cover.
- **Epic Games Store** tiles use the store logo, carousel key art and gameplay shots, with fallbacks for wide and tall artwork.
- **IGDB** shows every key art and screenshot as its own tile, and **works without a Twitch key**: when the Client ID/Secret are empty the plugin reads the public igdb.com pages (covers and screenshots; key art is API-only). With credentials it keeps using the official API.

white-goblin/deckyremotecontrol.name: Remote Control v1.0.0
white-goblin/deckyremotecontrol.body:
First release. A Decky Loader plugin that turns your phone or tablet into a touchpad and keyboard for your SteamOS device: scan a QR code, nothing to install on the phone.

**Highlights**
- Touchpad with tap, right-click, scrolling and flicks
- Arrow wheel with Enter, hold to repeat, spin to scroll
- Steam menu, Quick Access, Esc, volume and quit-app buttons
- Your phone's own keyboard (swipe typing, dictation, emoji)
- Portrait and landscape layouts; stays on after reboots and updates

**Install**
Download `Remote-Control-v1.0.0.zip` below, then in Decky (developer mode on): Settings → Developer → *Install plugin from ZIP*, or *Install plugin from URL* with this file's link. Then open Quick Access → Remote Control, turn it on and scan the code.

**Good to know**
- A fixed IP address (DHCP reservation) for the device is recommended. The optional mDNS name may be slow or not work on some phones, especially iPhones.
- The page is not encrypted and anyone with the link can control the device: use it on a trusted network.
- Written with AI assistance and not on the official Decky store, so it is installed manually. See the README for details.

doctordefector/lyrenne-decky.name: Lyrenne for Decky v0.1.0
doctordefector/lyrenne-decky.body:
First release. YouTube Music in Steam Deck Game Mode, powered by a Deck-only build of Lyrenne running in the background (93 MB download, no measurable battery cost).

- Quick Access panel: album art, the current lyric line, seek, play/pause, skip, shuffle, repeat, like, download, radio, and a music volume that's separate from the game's
- Full-screen Home, Search, Library, Queue and Lyrics pages that open over your game
- Select mode in Liked songs and Downloads, for playing, queueing, unliking or deleting downloads in bulk
- Sleep timer, and song change pop-ups (with sound, silent or off)
- Sign in from Game Mode: Steam opens the browser, so the STEAM + X keyboard works

**Install**
1. Turn on Decky's Developer mode.
2. Under Developer, use **Install plugin from URL** and paste the link to **`Lyrenne.zip`** below.

**Which file do I need?** Only `Lyrenne.zip`. Once it's installed, Decky downloads `lyrenne-deck-2.20.0.tar.gz` (the Lyrenne app itself) on its own, so you never touch it. The "Source code" files are something GitHub adds to every release.

murdii34/decky-oled-tint.name: OLED Tint 0.2.0 (beta)
murdii34/decky-oled-tint.body:
A Decky Loader plugin for the **AYN Odin 2 Portal** on Armada OS. It fixes the
screen at low brightness: across the lower part of Steam's brightness slider
(roughly 6-38%, worst around 20%) the panel's dark greys turn green and glow
instead of going dark.

## New in 0.2.0

- **Simple view.** The top of the panel is now Correction, brightness with its
  96 / 177 / 310 presets, **Test pattern** and **Info overlay**, then a
  **Simple view** switch that hides everything else. A fresh install opens in
  Simple view (after an update from 0.1.0, switch it on once).
- **Brightness in percent:** the sidebar shows the slider position next to the
  panel level (e.g. "Brightness 440 · 35%").
- **The test pattern shows the version** in large white text, so a photo of the
  screen says which build it is.
- **No flash when floor dimming switches on or off.** Turning the correction or
  "Off for this game" on goes dimmed first, then the backlight rises; turning it
  off drops the backlight before the dimming goes. Before, the screen could
  briefly show about twice the light asked for, or stay uncorrected until the
  next slider move. Compare now shows the uncorrected panel at your brightness.
- **A settings file that doesn't read is left alone** (and the status line
  says so) instead of being replaced by the defaults on the next save, which
  lost profiles and calibration tables.
- Steam's colour vibrance is no longer held at 100% after the menus' correction
  was switched off.

## What it does

- **Floor dimming** (on by default). The backlight stays just above the panel's
  bad range (543 of 4096), and a ReShade shader darkens the picture to the light
  the brightness you picked would give. Steam's slider works as usual; below the
  bad range the panel's own backlight takes over again.
  Camera-measured across the dimmed range on two days: median colour error
  1.4-3.3%, light 3.2-4.1%.
- **Colour calibration per brightness step**, measured with a camera on one
  Portal and shipped as a profile.
- **Dither correction** (Advanced, experimental): keeps the real backlight and
  rebuilds the darkest greys from the levels the panel can really show.
- **Compare** (5 s uncorrected), a test pattern page, off per game, and
  import/export of calibrations.
- Pauses itself, and says why, on external displays, when another colour filter
  is on, and on any device other than the Odin 2 Portal.

## Known issues

- **The darkest greys (4-12 of 255) shift with temperature.** A cool Portal shows
  them greener and darker than a warm one (grey 4 up to ~25% darker); from grey 16
  up it's within 1.5%. A correction that follows temperature is the next step.
- A higher floor (600 instead of 543) didn't help in a first test, but that test
  isn't conclusive. You can set it by hand (`floor_backlight` in the settings).
- At the very bottom of the slider (between 4% and 5%), where the panel's own
  backlight takes over, the screen briefly dips darker for a few frames.
- Floor dimming needs the ReShade engine (the default).
- The calibration comes from one Portal; other panels may differ a little. A
  second Portal confirmed the fix (no more green). Reports from other units are
  very welcome.
- Performance isn't measured or optimised yet. A first check showed no big hit:
  Blasphemous 2 runs at 117 FPS with floor dimming on.

## Install

1. Download `oled-tint-lite.zip` below and copy it onto the Portal.
2. Quick Access → Decky → gear icon → enable **Developer mode**.
3. Decky settings → **Developer** → **Install plugin from ZIP** → pick the zip.

Updating from 0.1.0: install the new zip the same way; your settings stay.

Step by step, with how to compare before/after: [LITE-GUIDE.md](https://github.com/murdii34/decky-oled-tint/blob/main/docs/LITE-GUIDE.md).

## How it was measured

The panel's behaviour and the calibration come from a camera rig (Sony A7 IV,
raw, in a light hood). The method, data and findings are in
[odin2-portal-oled-measure](https://github.com/murdii34/odin2-portal-oled-measure).

## A note on how this was made

Most of the code was written with AI assistance (Claude), then reviewed and
measured on the device. That's why it isn't submitted to the Decky Store.

lexdrev/origami.name: ORIGAMI 3.0.0
lexdrev/origami.body:
ORIGAMI has a sixth tile, **Service**: sharper games with one switch, and a cleanup of what Steam leaves on the disk. The fans can now hold a temperature you choose, the Power screen shows how long the battery lasts, and the interface speaks four more languages.

## What's new ### Service: sharpness - **Sharpness.** One switch on the new **Service** screen makes the picture in games sharper. It is the same sharpening that Radeon Image Sharpening does on Windows: it brings back the fine detail that anti-aliasing and rendering below the screen's resolution blur. - **Strength.** Soft, Medium, Strong or your own, from 0 to 100%. Medium suits most games; too strong, and edges get halos. In a test game, fine detail measured about one and a half times as strong at 40%, and almost twice as strong at 80%. - **Nothing to set up.** There is nothing to install and nothing to add to a game's launch options. Switch it on, start a game, and the game is sharpened. - **Takes effect as a game starts.** A game that is already running keeps what it started with, and the screen says so: "Comes on when the game starts next", "New strength when the game starts next". - **Per-game sharpness.** Start a game and switch on **Per-game sharpness** at the top of the Service screen. The game gets its own strength, or no sharpening at all, every time it runs. **Sharpness profiles** lists the games that have one. - **The Service tile** on the main screen shows the strength and the free space on the disk. ### Service: cleanup - **Cleanup.** A new screen, opened from the Service screen. It shows how much of the disk is free and two lists you can unfold: **Shader caches** and **Leftovers of removed games**, each with its size. Nothing is picked until you pick it. - **Shader caches.** For every game, Steam keeps shaders compiled in advance, the graphics driver's caches and transcoded videos. A game does not need them to run: without them it builds everything again. Removing a game's cache helps in three cases: - **Disk space.** The cache grows by itself and never shrinks; a big game can take several gigabytes. - **A game you have not played for a long time but want to keep.** Its cache is dead weight, and after a system or Proton update part of it is out of date anyway. - **A game that misbehaves after an update** of the driver, of Proton or of the game itself: stutter it did not have, broken graphics, a crash at start, an endless "Processing Vulkan shaders". Clearing the cache is the usual first step, and until now it meant finding the folder by the game's number. - **What it costs.** The next time the game starts, Steam downloads or builds the shaders again, which takes from seconds to a few minutes, and the first minutes may stutter. Saves and settings are not touched. If the disk has room and the game runs well, leave its cache alone. - **Leftovers of removed games.** A game you uninstalled can leave its shader cache, its prefix and sometimes its folder behind. ORIGAMI lists them by the game's name, and for a prefix it says whether the saves are in Steam Cloud too. Where they are not, the line is red. **Pick what is safe** marks the leftovers that cost nothing: caches, and prefixes whose saves the cloud keeps. - **Careful by design.** Nothing is listed or removed while a game runs. A game that Steam is downloading or processing shaders for cannot be picked. Games on a memory card that is not in the slot are not taken for removed. Before removing, ORIGAMI asks once more and says how many of the picked items hold saves that exist nowhere else. Afterwards it shows how much space came back. ### Fans: hold a temperature - **Temperature mode.** The Fans screen has a **Mode** strip: **Curve**, as before, or **Temperature**. Choose a temperature from 45 to 75 °C, and ORIGAMI finds the fan speed at which the chip rests there. The fans run as slowly as your target allows, instead of following a curve drawn for the worst case. - **Safe without ORIGAMI.** Above the target, the firmware gets steps of its own, up to full speed 10 °C over it. They answer a sudden load at once and keep working even if the plugin stops. - **The screen says what the fans do:** quiet while the chip is no warmer, at the slowest while it is cooler, at full speed while it is warmer. When the fans are at full speed and the chip is still over the target, it reminds you that a lower TDP cools it, by about 1 °C a watt. - **Where it is available:** the ROG Xbox Ally X, the ROG Xbox Ally X20 and the ROG Ally. The firmware of the ROG Ally runs the fans at about half speed by itself from 60 °C; ORIGAMI knows this, holds the chip below that point while it can, and says so on the screen. - **The curve is drawn as the fans follow it.** The firmware does not draw a line between the points of a curve: the fans run at the speed of the last point the temperature has passed. The chart now shows these steps, and "Now" under it shows the step the fans are really on. ### Power: the battery's time - **How long the battery lasts.** On battery, the Power screen has a second line: the time left to 10%, and what the whole console draws, not only the processor. Below 10% it counts to zero. - **Measured, not guessed.** The time comes from the energy the battery really lost over the last five minutes, not from the power of a single moment. ORIGAMI also remembers what each game draws at each TDP, so the next time the forecast is right from the first minute. ### Languages - **Four more languages:** German, Spanish, French and Simplified Chinese, beside English and Russian. The names of Steam's own things are Steam's, as its client has them in each language. - **A Language screen** in Settings: **Like Steam**, which is how ORIGAMI starts, or one of the six languages under its own name. ## Fixes - **The TDP could stop being held after Steam's session started.** If the session started right after the charger was plugged in, Steam wrote its own limit several times within seconds, and ORIGAMI answered only the first. It now answers every one of them. - **The end of a screen was cut off.** Text under a screen's last switch or button, such as the battery lines of the Power screen, could stay below the edge of the panel. The panel now scrolls to its very end. - **The fan gauges** now go up to 8000 rpm, which the fans reach at full speed. ## Good to know - **The sharpness works in games that draw through Vulkan.** That is nearly every game: DirectX games under Proton, and native Vulkan ones. It does not reach games that draw with OpenGL. - **It sharpens the game's own picture,** including the game's interface. Steam's menus and overlays are not touched. - **It works together with frame generation** that another plugin adds to a game; this was tried in a game. - **If a game's launch options, or another plugin's launcher in them, set the sharpening themselves,** ORIGAMI leaves that game alone and says on the Service screen who controls it. - **Three files in your home folder, and only while a game runs.** With the sharpness on, ORIGAMI writes two files into `~/.local/share/vulkan/implicit_layer.d/` and `~/.config/vkBasalt/vkBasalt.conf` as a game starts, and removes them as it ends. If you have a `vkBasalt.conf` of your own, it is put back. - **What the cleanup removes is gone for good.** **Restore everything** brings back settings, not files. - **The freed space can be less than the sizes add up to.** On a btrfs disk, files can share blocks with other files; the line "Freed" shows what the disk really gained. - **`ORIGAMI.zip` is bigger now**, about 4.5 MB: the layer that does the sharpening is included, for 64-bit and 32-bit games, so the sharpness does not depend on what the system has. - **Decky Loader 3.3.0 or newer** is still required. ## Updating - **From 2.0.0:** open ORIGAMI's **Settings**, find the **Updates** card and choose **Check**, then **Update**. Decky asks for confirmation and installs the release; your settings are kept. - **From an older version**, or if you prefer: on Decky's **Developer** page, use **Install Plugin from URL** with `github.com/lexdrev/origami/releases/latest/download/ORIGAMI.zip`, or download `ORIGAMI.zip` below and choose **Install Plugin from ZIP File**. - Don't update while a game is running: ORIGAMI stops for a moment while Decky swaps the versions, and the system briefly falls back to its own settings. - New to ORIGAMI? See [Install](https://github.com/lexdrev/origami#install) in the README. ## Tested on - **ROG Xbox Ally X** (board RC73XA) with Bazzite 45.20261117.1, kernel 7.3.4-ogc8.1, InputPlumber 0.84.0 and Decky Loader 3.3.1. There the sharpness was compared frame by frame in games, the cleanup removed real caches and leftovers, the fans held a temperature in games, through sleep and on the charger, and the battery's forecast was checked against the charge the battery really lost. - All six languages were checked on that console screen by screen for text that does not fit. The German, Spanish, French and Chinese texts have not been read by native speakers yet: if something reads wrong, please tell. - The Temperature mode on the ROG Ally (RC71L) is built from recordings its owner made; it has not been tried on that console yet. On the ROG Xbox Ally X20 it uses the numbers of the ROG Xbox Ally X. - The sharpness has been tried on Bazzite only. On SteamOS it should work the same, since ORIGAMI brings the layer with it, but nobody has tried it there yet. - ORIGAMI also supports the ROG Ally X (RC72LA) and the ROG Xbox Ally (RC73YA), but it has not been tested on them yet. Their fans follow a curve; the Temperature mode is not there. ## Feedback Found a bug or missing a feature? Open an [issue](https://github.com/lexdrev/origami/issues/new/choose): the form asks for your console, the versions and the log. English and Russian are both fine. --- В ORIGAMI появилась шестая плитка — **Сервис**: резкость в играх одним переключателем и очистка того, что Steam оставляет на диске. Вентиляторы теперь умеют держать выбранную температуру, экран «Питание» показывает, на сколько хватит батареи, а интерфейс заговорил ещё на четырёх языках.

## Что нового ### Сервис: резкость - **Резкость.** Один переключатель на новом экране **Сервис** делает картинку в играх резче. Это то же повышение резкости, что Radeon Image Sharpening в Windows: оно возвращает мелкие детали, которые смазывают сглаживание и рендер ниже разрешения экрана. - **Сила.** «Мягко», «Средне», «Сильно» или своя, от 0 до 100%. «Средне» подходит большинству игр; слишком сильная даёт ореолы на краях. В игре мелкие детали по замеру стали примерно в полтора раза контрастнее на 40% и почти вдвое — на 80%. - **Ничего настраивать не нужно.** Не надо ничего устанавливать и дописывать в параметры запуска игры. Включили, запустили игру — картинка стала резче. - **Действует с запуска игры.** Уже запущенная игра остаётся с тем, с чем стартовала, и экран об этом говорит: «Включится после перезапуска игры», «Новая сила — после перезапуска игры». - **Своя резкость для игры.** Запустите игру и включите **Своя резкость для игры** вверху экрана «Сервис»: у игры будет своя сила резкости или не будет резкости вовсе — каждый раз, когда она запущена. Такие игры собраны в **Профилях резкости**. - **Плитка «Сервис»** на главном экране показывает силу резкости и свободное место на диске. ### Сервис: очистка - **Очистка.** Новый экран, открывается с экрана «Сервис». Показывает, сколько места на диске свободно, и два раскрывающихся списка — **Кэш шейдеров** и **Остатки удалённых игр**, у каждой строки свой размер. Пока вы сами что-то не отметите, ничего не выбрано. - **Кэш шейдеров.** Для каждой игры Steam хранит заранее собранные шейдеры, кэши графического драйвера и перекодированные видеоролики. Игре они не обязательны: без них она соберёт всё заново. Удалять кэш игры полезно в трёх случаях: - **Место на диске.** Кэш растёт сам и никогда не уменьшается; у больших игр набегает по несколько гигабайт. - **Игра, в которую давно не играете, но удалять не хотите.** Её кэш лежит мёртвым грузом, а после обновления системы или Proton часть его всё равно устаревает. - **Игра стала вести себя странно после обновления** драйвера, Proton или самой игры: фризы, которых раньше не было, артефакты картинки, вылет при запуске, бесконечная «Обработка шейдеров Vulkan». Сброс кэша — обычный первый шаг в таких случаях, и раньше для него нужно было искать папку по номеру игры. - **Цена.** При следующем запуске игры Steam заново скачает или соберёт шейдеры — от секунд до нескольких минут, — и первые минуты возможны подтормаживания. Сохранения и настройки не затрагиваются. Если места хватает и игра работает нормально, её кэш лучше не трогать. - **Остатки удалённых игр.** Удалённая игра может оставить на диске свой кэш шейдеров, префикс и иногда папку. ORIGAMI показывает их по названию игры, а у префикса пишет, есть ли сохранения ещё и в Steam Cloud. Где их там нет — строка красная. **Выбрать безопасное** отмечает остатки, удаление которых ничего не стоит: кэши и префиксы, чьи сохранения хранит облако. - **Осторожность заложена.** Пока идёт игра, ничего не показывается и не удаляется. Игру, которую Steam сейчас качает или для которой собирает шейдеры, выбрать нельзя. Игры с карты памяти, которой нет в слоте, удалёнными не считаются. Перед удалением ORIGAMI спрашивает ещё раз и говорит, сколько среди выбранного пунктов с сохранениями, которых больше нигде нет. После — показывает, сколько места вернулось. ### Вентиляторы: держать температуру - **Режим «Температура».** На экране «Вентиляторы» появилась полоса **Режим**: **Кривая**, как раньше, или **Температура**. Выберите температуру от 45 до 75 °C, и ORIGAMI сам найдёт обороты, при которых чип на ней держится. Вентиляторы крутятся так тихо, как позволяет ваша цель, а не по кривой, нарисованной на худший случай. - **Безопасно и без ORIGAMI.** Выше цели прошивка получает свои ступени, вплоть до полных оборотов на 10 °C выше неё. Они отвечают на резкую нагрузку сразу и работают, даже если плагин остановится. - **Экран говорит, что делают вентиляторы:** тихо, пока чип не теплее цели; на минимуме, пока он холоднее; на полных оборотах, пока теплее. Когда вентиляторы уже на полных оборотах, а чип всё ещё выше цели, экран напоминает, что остудить его можно меньшим TDP — примерно на 1 °C за ватт. - **Где есть:** ROG Xbox Ally X, ROG Xbox Ally X20 и ROG Ally. У ROG Ally прошивка с 60 °C сама держит обороты примерно на половине; ORIGAMI это знает, держит чип ниже этой точки, пока может, и пишет об этом на экране. - **Кривая нарисована так, как её читают вентиляторы.** Прошивка не проводит линию между точками кривой: вентиляторы идут на оборотах последней точки, которую прошла температура. График теперь показывает эти ступени, а «Сейчас» под ним — ступень, на которой вентиляторы на самом деле. ### Питание: время батареи - **На сколько хватит батареи.** От батареи на экране «Питание» появляется вторая строка: время до 10% заряда и расход всей консоли, а не только процессора. Ниже 10% время считается до нуля. - **Замер, а не догадка.** Время считается по энергии, которую батарея на самом деле потеряла за последние пять минут, а не по мощности одного мгновения. ORIGAMI ещё и запоминает, сколько расходует каждая игра на каждом TDP, поэтому в следующий раз прогноз верен с первой минуты. ### Языки - **Ещё четыре языка:** немецкий, испанский, французский и упрощённый китайский — вдобавок к русскому и английскому. Названия вещей Steam взяты из самого Steam на каждом языке. - **Экран «Язык»** в Настройках: **Как в Steam** — так ORIGAMI стоит сразу после установки — или один из шести языков под своим названием. ## Исправления - **ORIGAMI мог перестать держать TDP после старта сессии Steam.** Если сессия стартовала сразу после подключения зарядки, Steam за несколько секунд записывал свой предел несколько раз, а ORIGAMI отвечал только на первую запись. Теперь он отвечает на каждую. - **Низ экрана обрезался.** Текст под последним переключателем или кнопкой экрана — например, строки батареи на «Питании» — мог остаться за краем панели. Теперь панель докручивается до самого конца. - **Циферблаты вентиляторов** теперь идут до 8000 об/мин — столько вентиляторы дают на полных оборотах. ## Полезно знать - **Резкость работает в играх, которые рисуют через Vulkan.** Это почти все игры: игры на DirectX под Proton и родные на Vulkan. До игр на OpenGL она не доходит. - **Резче становится сама картинка игры,** вместе с интерфейсом игры. Меню и оверлеи Steam не затрагиваются. - **Работает вместе с генерацией кадров,** которую добавляет игре другой плагин; проверено в игре. - **Если резкость задана в параметрах запуска игры или её задаёт стоящая там обёртка другого плагина,** ORIGAMI эту игру не трогает и пишет на экране «Сервис», кто управляет резкостью. - **Три файла в домашней папке, и только пока идёт игра.** С включённой резкостью ORIGAMI при запуске игры пишет два файла в `~/.local/share/vulkan/implicit_layer.d/` и `~/.config/vkBasalt/vkBasalt.conf`, а когда игра закрывается, удаляет их. Если у вас есть свой `vkBasalt.conf`, он возвращается на место. - **Удалённое очисткой не вернуть.** **Вернуть всё как было** возвращает настройки, а не файлы. - **Освободиться может меньше, чем сумма размеров.** На диске с btrfs файлы могут делить блоки с другими файлами; строка «Освобождено» показывает, сколько места диск получил на самом деле. - **`ORIGAMI.zip` стал больше**, около 4,5 МБ: слой, который повышает резкость, лежит внутри, для 64-битных и 32-битных игр, поэтому резкость не зависит от состава системы. - **Нужен Decky Loader 3.3.0 или новее**, как и раньше. ## Обновление - **С 2.0.0:** откройте **Настройки** ORIGAMI и в карточке **Обновления** нажмите **Проверить**, затем **Обновить**. Decky спросит подтверждение и поставит выпуск; настройки сохранятся. - **Со старой версии** или если так привычнее: на странице **Разработчик** в Decky — **Установить плагин из URL** со ссылкой `github.com/lexdrev/origami/releases/latest/download/ORIGAMI.zip`, или скачайте `ORIGAMI.zip` ниже и выберите **Установить плагин из ZIP файла**. - Обновляйте не во время игры: пока Decky меняет версии, ORIGAMI на мгновение останавливается и система возвращается к своим настройкам. - Ставите ORIGAMI впервые? Смотрите [Установку](https://github.com/lexdrev/origami/blob/main/README.ru.md#установка) в README. ## На чём проверено - **ROG Xbox Ally X** (плата RC73XA), Bazzite 45.20261117.1, ядро 7.3.4-ogc8.1, InputPlumber 0.84.0, Decky Loader 3.3.1. Там резкость сравнивали по кадрам в играх, очистка удаляла настоящий кэш и остатки, вентиляторы держали температуру в играх, во сне и на зарядке, а прогноз батареи сверяли с тем, сколько заряда батарея потеряла на самом деле. - Все шесть языков проверены на этой консоли экран за экраном: текст нигде не обрезан. Немецкий, испанский, французский и китайский тексты носители языка ещё не вычитывали: если что-то звучит неправильно, напишите. - Режим «Температура» на ROG Ally (RC71L) сделан по записям её владельца; на самой консоли он ещё не проверен. На ROG Xbox Ally X20 он работает на числах ROG Xbox Ally X. - Резкость проверена только на Bazzite. На SteamOS она должна работать так же, потому что слой ORIGAMI приносит с собой, но там её ещё никто не пробовал. - ORIGAMI знает и ROG Ally X (RC72LA), и ROG Xbox Ally (RC73YA), но на них его ещё не проверяли. Их вентиляторы идут по кривой, режима «Температура» там нет. ## Обратная связь Нашли баг или чего-то не хватает? Создайте [issue](https://github.com/lexdrev/origami/issues/new/choose): форма спросит консоль, версии и журнал. Можно на русском.

lexdrev/origami.name: ORIGAMI 1.2.0
lexdrev/origami.body:
ORIGAMI can now update itself: the **Updates** card in **Settings** finds a newer release on GitHub and hands it to Decky. And if ORIGAMI cannot start, it says why instead of showing empty screens.

## What's new

- **Updates in Settings.** **Check** asks GitHub for the latest release. If there is a newer one, the button turns into **Update**: Decky asks you to confirm, downloads `ORIGAMI.zip`, checks it against the SHA-256 GitHub gives for it and puts it in place of the old one. Your settings stay. **What's new** opens the releases on GitHub, with the ones you skipped below the newest.
- **Check for updates · auto.** Switched on, ORIGAMI checks once a day as you open it. A newer release shows on the main screen: an amber dot on the gear and **Update … available** under the system.
- **Updates from ORIGAMI work from this version on**, so this one time update the old way, as below.

## Fixes

- **Empty screens on an older Decky Loader.** Decky Loader up to 3.2.10 runs plugins on Python…

lexdrev/origami.name: ORIGAMI 1.1.0
lexdrev/origami.body:
ORIGAMI now runs on the first ROG Ally with SteamOS too, and on the ROG Xbox Ally X it is tested on Bazzite 45. Paste on Steam's on-screen keyboard works again.

## What's new

- **ROG Ally on SteamOS.** ORIGAMI shows only what this console can do: power, fans, saturation, stick lighting and handle vibration. The system keeps both buttons, so there are no button settings, and the vibration test runs through InputPlumber.
- **TDP up to the firmware's limit.** The scale ends where the console's firmware does: on the ROG Ally at 25 W on battery and 30 W on the charger, on the Ally X at 35 W as before. **Up to 35 W on battery** is hidden where the battery gives no more anyway.
- **Saturation on SteamOS.** 100% is what the system shows: SteamOS already gives the richest colours, so the scale goes from 0 to 100% with Accurate, Soft and System. On Bazzite the scale stays 0 to 200%, and its 100% is called System now too.
- **Every Ally model by name.** The header shows ROG ALLY, ROG ALLY X,…

lexdrev/origami.name: ORIGAMI 1.0.0
lexdrev/origami.body:
The first release of ORIGAMI: power, fans, display, stick lighting and gamepad settings for the ROG Xbox Ally X on Bazzite in one place, right in Steam's quick access menu, with fixes for what is broken on the console today.

## Fixes for Bazzite 44

- **TDP holds.** The limit you set comes back after sleep, the charger, a profile change and every game start, and Steam's slider no longer leaves the console at 40–47 W.
- **CPU frequency cap holds.** After the charger or a profile change, the cores no longer run up to 3.5 GHz and take power from the graphics.
- **CPU boost after sleep.** Switched on after sleep, the boost raises the core clocks again.
- **Handle vibration.** Strength from 0 to 100% that survives sleep, and games rumble about twice as strong: Steam passes only about a third of their vibration on.
- **Trigger motors.** They rumble along with games: right or both, steady or in taps.
- **Gyro.** The horizontal axis turns the right way, without Steam's Invert X box in every…

silvertonguered/decky-demo-finder.name: v1.3.6
silvertonguered/decky-demo-finder.body:
Improves opening the API key page on Windows. Includes the v1.3.5 Steam Deck certificate fix. One zip for Steam Deck (Decky Loader) and Windows.

## Fixed
- **Windows:** the plugin now asks its backend which operating system it runs on instead of guessing from the browser user agent, so **Get Your Free API Key** uses the default-browser opener on Windows. The backend also gains extra fallbacks for opening links on Windows (`webbrowser`, then `cmd start`).
- **Steam Deck:** includes the v1.3.5 fix for `unable to get local issuer certificate` (certificate verification now uses the system CA bundle).

## Install
Download `decky-demo-finder-v1.3.6.zip`, extract it into your Decky `plugins` folder (so you have `plugins/decky-demo-finder/`), then reload Decky / restart Decky Loader. The same zip works on Steam Deck and Windows.

silvertonguered/decky-demo-finder.name: v1.3.5
silvertonguered/decky-demo-finder.body:
Fixes "Failed to load wishlist (ClientConnectorCertificateError ... unable to get local issuer certificate)" on Steam Deck. One zip for Steam Deck (Decky Loader) and Windows.

## Fixed
- **Steam Deck:** Decky's bundled Python could not find any trusted certificates, so every HTTPS request to Steam failed certificate verification, including the wishlist, app details and the new key check. The plugin now loads the system CA bundle (for example `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`) itself. Certificate verification stays on.
- The plugin log (`~/homebrew/logs/`) now says which CA bundle was used ("Using CA bundle: ...").

## Install
Download `decky-demo-finder-v1.3.5.zip`, extract it into your Decky `plugins` folder (so you have `plugins/decky-demo-finder/`), then reload Decky / restart Decky Loader. The same zip works on Steam Deck and Windows.

silvertonguered/decky-demo-finder.name: v1.3.4
silvertonguered/decky-demo-finder.body:
Shows exactly why a Steam API key or wishlist load fails, instead of a generic message. One zip for Steam Deck (Decky Loader) and Windows.

## New
- **Key check on save.** After Grab Key from Steam Page, Paste Key from Clipboard or Save API Key, the plugin asks Steam whether it accepts the key. The toast shows the last 4 characters of the saved key and says "Steam accepted the key." or why not (for example "Steam rejected the key (HTTP 403)" or a network error).
- **Real reason on wishlist failure.** "Failed to load wishlist" now includes Steam's actual reply in brackets, such as the HTTP status, a network or certificate error, or "0 wishlist items returned".

Download `decky-demo-finder-v1.3.4.zip`, extract it into your Decky `plugins` folder (so you have `plugins/decky-demo-finder/`), then reload Decky / restart Decky Loader. The same zip works on Steam Deck and Windows.

silvertonguered/decky-demo-finder.name: v1.3.3

Get your Steam API key into Demo Finder without copying or pasting anything. Built for controller use on Steam Deck, docked or handheld. One zip for Steam Deck (Decky Loader) and Windows.

Press **Get Your Free API Key**, register or view your key so it is on screen, come back to Demo Finder and press **Grab Key from Steam Page**. - Works on Steam Deck, where the key page opens inside Steam. On Windows the key page opens in your normal browser, so use Paste Key from Clipboard…

silvertonguered/decky-volumemixer-window.body:
## Decky Volume Mixer v0.3.0 — one zip for Windows and Steam Deck

### New
- **Single package for both platforms.** The same zip installs on Decky Loader for Windows and on Steam Deck / SteamOS. The audio backend is picked automatically: Windows Core Audio on Windows, PipeWire (`pw-dump` + `wpctl`) on SteamOS.
- Rewrote the install instructions and README for both platforms.

### Notes
- No plugin code changes; the SteamOS path was checked against simulated PipeWire output (list, set volume, hide, settings, reset). Real-hardware reports from Steam Deck users are welcome.

### Install
Download `decky-volume-mixer-v0.3.0.zip`.
- **Steam Deck:** Decky Settings -> Developer -> Install Plugin from ZIP.
- **Windows:** extract into `homebrew\plugins\`, restart Decky Loader.

silvertonguered/decky-volumemixer-window.name: v0.2.0 – Real app names
silvertonguered/decky-volumemixer-window.body:
## Decky Volume Mixer (Windows) v0.2.0

### New
- **Real app names.** Games are now listed by their actual title. Steam games resolve via their appmanifest (e.g. `Discovery.exe` → **THE FINALS**), including games whose anti-cheat hides the process path.
- Falls back to the exe's ProductName/FileDescription, then the exe/session name.
- The underlying exe name is shown as a subtitle when it differs from the friendly name.

### Notes
- Apps hidden under an old exe-based name stay hidden.

### Install
Download `decky-volume-mixer-v0.2.0.zip`, extract into `homebrew\plugins\`, restart Decky Loader.

indyjamesb/decky-plex-audiobooks.name: Plex Audiobooks 0.5.4
indyjamesb/decky-plex-audiobooks.body:
**What's new in 0.5.4**
- **Speed controls fit the Quick Access menu.** The −0.05 and +0.05 buttons now share one row with the speed readout, so nothing gets cut off. Chapter buttons use the same compact size. Speed still moves in 0.05 steps from 0.50x to 3.00x.

indyjamesb/decky-plex-audiobooks.name: Plex Audiobooks 0.5.3
indyjamesb/decky-plex-audiobooks.body:
Download **plex-audiobooks-v0.5.3.zip** below and install it in Decky Loader with Developer mode → Install Plugin from ZIP File. Full steps are in the README.

white-goblin/piston.name: v0.9.0
white-goblin/piston.body:
**Update the plugin on the device and the integration in Home Assistant together; a plugin on 0.4.1 or newer updates itself to this one (you approve the install on the device).** This release keeps protocol version 3 and adds one command and one input event, so an older plugin keeps working for everything else, but seeking from the card needs this plugin (an older one answers that it does not know the command).

### Added
- **Playback buttons on the remote card.** A row of five buttons under the controls: previous track, seek back, play/pause, seek forward and next track. The row can be hidden with the new **Show the play, pause, next and previous buttons** option, and is off while the device is off.
- **Seeking.** The seek buttons move 10 seconds on each tap and keep going while you hold them. The media player now supports `media_player.media_seek` whenever the player reports how long the video is (not for a live stream or a game). The device moves the player with MPRIS `SetPosition` and falls back to a relative seek, because some players mishandle a relative one.
- **Seek amount on the device's cursor.** While you seek, the cursor circle on the device's screen flows to the side (left for back, right for forward), turns into a label such as `+30` or `-1:30` that adds up over a run of presses, and flows back.
- **The playing app shows its progress bar.** A seek is not input for a video app, so the device also nudges the pointer a few pixels and back (the drawn cursor stays still).
- **Two switches in the Piston panel** under **Remote input**, both on by default: **Show seek amount on the cursor** and **Nudge the pointer on seek**.

### Notes
- Seeking depends on the app: players that report their length and accept MPRIS seeks work (tested with Jellyfin and YouTube); a player without a length leaves the seek buttons dimmed.
- The remote card needs the card file of this version: after updating, reload the dashboard (the card address changes with the file, so the Companion app does not keep an old copy).
- The README's media player row and the [reference](https://github.com/White-Goblin/piston/blob/main/docs/reference.md#remote-card) describe the behavior.


## What's Changed
* Codify the project rules and add guards for them by @White-Goblin in https://github.com/White-Goblin/piston/pull/1
* Document decisions, module map and testing; guard three more conventions by @White-Goblin in https://github.com/White-Goblin/piston/pull/2
* Run the real Home Assistant suite on the minimum and the newest relea… by @White-Goblin in https://github.com/White-Goblin/piston/pull/3
* Seek from the remote card: transport row, seek buttons and a cursor label by @White-Goblin in https://github.com/White-Goblin/piston/pull/4
* README: new tagline, drop the seek switches sentence by @White-Goblin in https://github.com/White-Goblin/piston/pull/5
* Release 0.9.0: seeking from the remote card by @White-Goblin in https://github.com/White-Goblin/piston/pull/6

## New Contributors
* @White-Goblin made their first contribution in https://github.com/White-Goblin/piston/pull/1

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/White-Goblin/piston/compare/v0.8.0...v0.9.0

white-goblin/piston.body:

### Added

- **HLX FSR 4 Full**, an upscaler of its own: AMD's full FSR 4.1.2 network
  with HelixSR's runtime, sharper than Lite and slower (about twice HLX FSR
  4's time on a BC-250; no Steam Deck figures yet). It ships built in
  HelixSR Scaler's folder of the release from 3.3.0 and is taken from there:
  a drop-in in a game with FSR 3.1, as cyboman's builds are (no AMD file
  behind it), and otherwise OptiScaler's FidelityFX upscaler, or a custom
  one beside the picked build. From HelixSR Desktop's set-up when its version
  has it; the release is downloaded for it only when it is the one picked.
- **HLX FSR 4 runs natively in Vulkan games.** Its Vulkan build, in the
  same folder of the release, goes into its custom folder (ffx_vk) with every
  OptiScaler install, and a game with HLX FSR 4 picked has VulkanUpscaler
  name it, instead of running it through ffx_12's interop. Where an install
  or a release has no Vulkan build, nothing changes.
