cediqqu/decky-neca.name: N.E.C.A v3.0.0: Eden + Cemu
cediqqu/decky-neca.body:
N.E.C.A 3.0.0 deja **Eden (Switch)** y **Cemu (Wii U)** como emuladores
soportados. **Dolphin (GameCube/Wii) se retira temporalmente.**

> **Si usabas Dolphin**, quédate en N.E.C.A 2.0.0 o configura sus mandos a mano.
> Los datos de `~/eden-autoconfig` (plantillas, backups y configuraciones) no se
> borran; simplemente dejan de aplicarse. Eden y Cemu siguen funcionando.

## Qué cambia

- **Un solo Aplicar.** El botón escribe Eden y Cemu de una vez; ya no hay un
  botón suelto para Eden.
- **Restaurar Eden y Cemu.** Eden vuelve a su `qt-config.ini` original y Cemu
  deshace su último aplicar desde el backup más reciente.
- **Integrado a ancho completo.** La tarjeta del mando integrado ocupa toda la
  fila, muestra estrella, flecha o prohibido según el modo y deja los mandos
  extra debajo.
- **Cupos más claros.** El botón **Mandos** muestra `activos/cupo` y colorea
  hasta el último jugador activo, integrado incluido.
- **Log con filtros.** **Ver log** permite ver Todo, Eden o Cemu, con scroll por
  D-pad, stick o dedo. El ruido de `--who` se oculta.
- **Reglas del integrado.** Con 0 DualSense es P1; con DualSense pasa a Último o
  Desactivado según el cupo. Si lo fijas como Jugador 1 con mandos extra, los
  DualSense corren un puesto y los que sobran se desactivan.
- **Cemu más fiable.** Se corrige el bus del GUID para que Cemu reconozca los
  mandos con Steam Input desactivado y se evita el integrado fantasma cuando SDL
  no lo expone.
- **MAC completa.** Las tarjetas muestran la MAC entera, con salto de línea si no
  cabe.
- **Iconos y avisos.** La ROG Xbox Ally X usa ASUS + Xbox; el panel avisa cuando
  los scripts se acaban de instalar y hay que reiniciar el juego o pulsar
  **Aplicar**.

## Requisitos

- Decky Loader con `api_version: 1`.
- SteamOS en un PC de mano. Probado en ROG Xbox Ally X.
- EmuDeck con Eden (perfil `emudeck`) y/o Cemu (`controllerProfiles/controller0.xml`).
  Si Cemu está en otra carpeta, define `CEMU_DIR` en el `.conf`.
- ES-DE con *Custom Event Scripts* activado.
- Eden y Cemu cerrados antes de aplicar.

## Instalación

1. Descarga `neca-decky.zip` de esta Release.
2. En la consola: **Decky → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP**.
3. Abre el panel y pulsa **Instalar scripts** la primera vez.
4. En ES-DE: **Other settings → Enable custom event scripts**.

Si vienes de N.E.C.A 2.0.0, instala encima. Si vienes de E.C.A, desinstala antes
el plugin antiguo.

## Límites conocidos

- **Dolphin no está soportado en 3.0.0.**
- **Cemu se restaura con `--restore latest` o `--restore N`.** No hay un `stock/`
  fijo para Cemu: `1` es la copia más reciente, `2` la anterior, etc.
- Solo se puede fijar un DualSense como Player 1 por MAC.
- Con Steam Input activado en ES-DE, la asignación exacta de varios DualSense
  necesita desactivarlo para ES-DE.
- Cemu no crea bindings: solo cambia el dispositivo. Si EmuDeck no dejó el
  mapeo, no hay nada que asignar.

## Documentación

- [README en español](https://github.com/CeDiqqu/decky-neca/blob/main/README.md)
- [README en inglés](https://github.com/CeDiqqu/decky-neca/blob/main/README.en.md)
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/CeDiqqu/decky-neca/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

El zip incluye el README en español y el bundle de scripts 3.0.0.

---

## English summary

N.E.C.A 3.0.0 keeps **Eden (Switch)** and **Cemu (Wii U)** as the supported
emulators. **Dolphin (GameCube/Wii) is temporarily retired.**

> **If you used Dolphin**, stay on N.E.C.A 2.0.0 or configure its controllers by
> hand. Data in `~/eden-autoconfig` (templates, backups and configs) is not
> deleted; it simply stops being applied. Eden and Cemu keep working.

Highlights:

- One **Apply** button writes Eden and Cemu; the separate Eden button is gone.
- **Restore** puts Eden back to its original `qt-config.ini` and undoes Cemu's
  latest apply from the most recent backup.
- The built-in controller card is full width and shows star, arrow or disabled
  state; extra controllers sit below it.
- The **Mandos** button shows `active/slots` and includes the built-in
  controller.
- The log has Todo/Eden/Cemu filters and controller-friendly scrolling.
- Cemu GUID bus fix for Steam Input off, plus no ghost built-in controller when
  SDL does not expose it.
- Full MAC on the cards, ASUS + Xbox icon for the ROG Xbox Ally X, and a notice
  after installing new scripts.

Known limits: **Dolphin is not supported in 3.0.0**. Cemu restores with
`--restore latest` or `--restore N`; there is no fixed Cemu `stock/`. Only one
DualSense can be pinned as Player 1 by MAC. The exact Player N = DualSense N
mapping needs Steam Input disabled for ES-DE. Cemu does not create bindings.

Full details: [README in English](https://github.com/CeDiqqu/decky-neca/blob/main/README.en.md).

rayekkk/deckyreshade.body:
### ✨ Added

**Plugin**
- Initial release, tested on Lenovo Legion Go 2 with SteamOS 3.9.5.

**Setup**
- A guided first setup: ReShade build (add-on build by default), version and AutoHDR, then one download.

**Games**
- Set up per game from the Quick Access Menu, starting with the game that is running: ReShade on or off.
- The executable and graphics API are read from the game itself (32/64-bit, DirectX 8-12, OpenGL,
  dinput8 as a fallback) and can all be changed.
- A game moved to another library is followed there, and one that was uninstalled leaves the list by
  itself; a game on an SD card that is out stays set up.
- A game that ships a shader compiler too old for DirectX 12 effects (Windows 8.1's) gets a newer one;
  the game's own is kept beside it and put back when ReShade is turned off.

**Non-Steam games**
- Windows shortcuts and emulators work like Steam games.

**AutoHDR**
- Per game, the AutoHDR add-on (switched on for the game) and Pumbo's AdvancedAutoHDR, with a first
  preset; a start that stayed in SDR is shown on the game's page and said once.
- The HDR part of a game's page says when HDR is off in Steam, with a button to the setting.

**RenoDX**
- Per game, the mod list from the RenoDX wiki with each mod's status and note, matched to the library;
  a mod is installed only from a known author's GitHub release that matches GitHub's checksum.
- The engine-wide Unreal Engine and Unity mods for the games their own lists name; ones that need steps
  the plugin cannot take (a build from Discord, DLSS) are links.
- An Unreal Engine game whose list asks for Engine.ini gets its HDR lines (read-only) and Upgrade Path
  Off; turning the mod off puts its Engine.ini back.

**ReShade**
- The newest version DeckyReshade has checksums for, with automatic updates, or a fixed known version
  (6.3.3 to 6.8.0); a newer ReShade on reshade.me is announced and comes with a plugin update.

**Launch options**
- None needed: ReShade starts by itself, and OpenGL games (and Direct3D 10 when picked by hand) get a
  Wine setting for their executable, removed again with ReShade.
- **Use launch options** in Settings leaves Wine alone instead: turning a game on copies its launch options
  line, and the game's page has a Copy button.

**Shaders**
- Packages from ReShade's own list, shared by all games, with updates.

**Logs**
- When ReShade last started in a game and its errors, ReShade's and the plugin's log in the panel, and a
  report saved to Downloads.
- A warning when ReShade did not start in a game twice in a row.

**Downloads**
- Downloaded files can be removed from the panel.

**About**
- **Use Rayek's store** makes Rayek's store Decky's store channel after you confirm, so Decky's Store tab
  lists Rayek's plugins and offers their updates.

armadaos-freedom/decky-uu-accelerator.name: UU加速器 0.3
armadaos-freedom/decky-uu-accelerator.body:

- 自动补齐缺少的 cgroup 与 DNS 转发组件，优先使用系统已有能力。
- 改进兼容性检查：根据所需内核接口判断，不再因无关的内核配置差异而拒绝启动。
- 保留规则检查和模块加载的具体错误信息，方便定位安装、启动问题。

dimaman/zapret2-armada.name: SpoofDPI Armada 0.3.0
dimaman/zapret2-armada.body:
# SpoofDPI Armada 0.3.0

Pre-release for ARM64 Armada OS. Local SpoofDPI TUN mode now appears as the
primary compact switch in Decky. It runs DPI bypass on the handheld with a
direct connection, without NFQUEUE or a remote VPN server. The second switch
retains Hysteria2 for the occasions when a full VPN is needed. The two services
cannot run simultaneously from the plugin.

Two TLS strategies are available: SNI split with two fake packets by default,
or a stronger chunk split. UDP fake packets are disabled by default to preserve
game compatibility and direct latency. The upstream SpoofDPI TUN implementation
intercepts IPv4 TCP/UDP; IPv6 traffic is outside this mode.

The package contains pinned upstream SpoofDPI v1.5.5 and Hysteria2 v2.13.0
ARM64 executables with license notices. CI verifies checksums, ARM64 execution,
service syntax and installable ZIP checksums.

## Device test required

No physical Odin 3 / Armada 6.11.0 test is available to the maintainer. The
kernel must provide `/dev/net/tun`; available network routes and permissions
must allow a TUN interface. Check the status, logs, direct public IP, blocked
sites and an actual game after installing. SpoofDPI's upstream TUN mode is
experimental. No single DPI strategy works for every provider or restriction.

dimaman/zapret2-armada.name: Hysteria2 Armada 0.2.0
dimaman/zapret2-armada.body:
# Hysteria2 Armada 0.2.0

Experimental ARM64 pre-release. The Decky Game Mode panel now presents one
compact Hysteria2 VPN switch. Turning it on starts the official Hysteria2
v2.13.0 client in system-wide TUN mode; turning it off stops the service.
It routes TCP and UDP over the user's own Hysteria2 server without NFQUEUE.
ICMP is not tunneled by Hysteria2 TUN mode.

Server, UDP port, authentication, optional Salamander obfuscation and TLS SNI
are set in a separate Decky settings dialog. Secrets are stored in root-only
files and omitted from status results. TLS validation defaults to enabled.
Autostart is opt-in. Upgrade retires only the previous plugin's owned service
and nftables table; its old domain configuration is retained.

The binary is pinned to the upstream release SHA256 and verified by CI.
The ARM64 ZIP and source ZIP include license notices and SHA256SUMS.

**LeGO Suite v0.351**

**Changes**

- Added the OptiScaler Injector module, based on [Decky Framegen](https://github.com/xXJSONDeruloXx/Decky-Framegen), which injects OptiScaler into Steam games, Non-Steam games, and games installed via Unifideck. It detects games built with Unreal Engine to patch them properly.

- Added an option to disable the OptiScaler Injector module in the plugin directly from the desktop app (in real time).
 
- Added system resource monitoring to both the app and the plugin.

**Cambios**

**Importante**

src893/decky-emu-lookup.name: v1.0.0 — Foundations
src893/decky-emu-lookup.body:
# Decky Emu Lookup v1.0.0
 
First public release. The plugin adds an **"Available for emulation"** section to Steam store pages, showing whether a game also exists on emulatable consoles: Nintendo Switch, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, 5 and PlayStation Portable.
 
## Features
 
### On store pages
- A section added to the game's feature list, with one entry per console family.
- Works in **gaming mode** (Steam Deck interface) and **desktop mode**.
- Clicking an entry opens a search for the game on the Nintendo or PlayStation store, based on the language selected in the plugin.

### Data and cache
- Data provided by **IGDB**, through a Twitch application (Client ID and Client Secret entered in the Quick Access Menu).
- Detection of separate IGDB entries with the exact same name (for example, the original PSP version of a game ported to Steam).
- JSON cache refreshed when you visit a store page. Validity is configurable: 7, 15 or 30 days (30 by default).
- Respects IGDB's rate limit (about 4 requests per second).

ihulksmashi/clawdeck.name: ClawDeck 0.2.0 beta 20
ihulksmashi/clawdeck.body:
Autotune fixes from anaveto, and the newest XeSS XMX package.

- **Switching Autotune off now gives the watts back:** switching Autotune off in a game, or changing something under
  Advanced, used to leave Autotune's last (lower) TDP on the chip until the game ended. Your pick now goes back at
  once, and your own change stays.
- **Temperature guard:** after the chip cooled down, the TDP now comes back up in games Autotune stays out of (xemu,
  or with Autotune switched off). It used to stay at the guard's lower step.
- **xemu:** picking a new Autotune target in an xemu game no longer makes Autotune take over the game.
- **"Set PL2 yourself"** now reads the value back from the chip. The toast shows the watts, and it says so when the
  chip didn't take the value.
- **Autotune's log** (`autotune.csv`) now has frame times (median, 95th percentile, slow frames) for games whose frame
  rate comes from Steam's overlay. A limit that's only a bit too low shows up there as slow frames even when the fps
  looks full.
- **XeSS XMX package 20261115:** lower latency with frame generation. HHHHanasak1 measured Cyberpunk 2077 at 3x going
  from 45 to 32 ms, and CONTROL Resonant at 3x from 53 to 48 ms. Setup → **Update XeSS XMX**.

Thanks anaveto for all of these!

**Update:** Setup → **Update to 0.2.0 beta 20** (from beta 3 or later). Otherwise Quick Access → Decky → gear →
Developer → **Install plugin from URL**:
`https://github.com/IHulkSmashI/ClawDeck/releases/download/v0.2.0-beta.20/ClawDeck.zip`.

Earlier notes: [beta 19](https://github.com/IHulkSmashI/ClawDeck/releases/tag/v0.2.0-beta.19) (battery and GPU
watts, emulators, temperature guard, diagnostics log), [beta 18](https://github.com/IHulkSmashI/ClawDeck/releases/tag/v0.2.0-beta.18)
(tabs in Quick Access).

ihulksmashi/clawdeck.name: ClawDeck 0.2.0 beta 19
ihulksmashi/clawdeck.body:
Battery and GPU watts, emulators, the temperature guard and a diagnostics log, all from anaveto.

- **Battery watts:** the Claw 8 EX reports its battery current wrongly (about −64 A), and ClawDeck used to divide it
  by 100, which read about 30 % low. It now takes back the real value, so "Battery now" on the Fixes page is right.
- **GPU watts in the overlay:** "Show watts in the overlay" now also opens the counter for the graphics part of the
  chip. MangoHud versions with flightlessmango/MangoHud#2211 show it as GPU watts instead of 0.0 W.
- **Emulators:** autotune stays out of xemu, which shows 60 fps whatever the game's real speed, so your own limit stays
  on the chip. Games without their own MangoHud log (emulators from ES-DE, for one) now get their frame rate from
  Steam's overlay.
- **Temperature guard:** when a couple of busy cores make the chip hot while it's well under its power limit (xemu
  does this), the guard now lowers the CPU's top clock instead of cutting the watts…

ihulksmashi/clawdeck.name: ClawDeck 0.2.0 beta 17
ihulksmashi/clawdeck.body:
Fans, autotune and ES-DE from anaveto, lower frame generation latency, and a gyro fix.

- **Lower latency with XeSS frame generation:** XeSS XMX package 20261113. HHHHanasak1 reports CONTROL Resonant at 3x
  on the Claw 8 EX's chip going from about 35 ms to about 23 ms. Setup → **Update XeSS XMX** after updating ClawDeck.
- **Fans** (thanks anaveto!): presets now reach the fans exactly (Quiet's 75 % used to land at 74 %, and the panel
  then said the preset didn't apply). A new **Extreme** preset sits between Cooling and Full speed, and the panel shows
  the curve the fans follow right now.
- **Autotune** (thanks anaveto!): MangoHud's frame-time log starts again, so autotune reads the frame rate in games
  without XeSS. It only reads the running game's log, and when it can't get a frame rate it puts your own limit back
  instead of leaving its starting point on the chip.
- **ES-DE** (thanks anaveto!): each game you start from ES-DE gets its own power pick and autotune, instead of one…

ihulksmashi/clawdeck.name: ClawDeck 0.2.0 beta 16
ihulksmashi/clawdeck.body:
Non-Steam games with their own Proton prefix, and the older Capcom games.

- **Non-Steam games with a custom prefix:** when a shortcut's launch options send Proton to its own prefix
  (`STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH=...`), ClawDeck now always uses that one. Steam creates an empty `compatdata` folder for the
  shortcut at its first launch, and ClawDeck looked there instead, so the Game page said the XMX cores were never used
  and the health check looked in the wrong place. XeSS on XMX itself kept working. A path starting with `~` or `$HOME`
  works too (thanks maltyjava for tracking it down!).
- **Capcom games without DLSS:** Resident Evil 2, 3, 4 (2023), 7 and Village, Devil May Cry 5 and Street Fighter 6
  have no DLSS in the game, so ClawDeck's Capcom setup (it swaps the game's DLSS and DLSS frame generation for XeSS
  on the XMX cores) had nothing to work with there: RE4 ran as if nothing was installed. ClawDeck no longer installs
  it in these games and the Game page says why;…

loddi-o/claude-deck.name: Claude Deck 0.1.2
loddi-o/claude-deck.body:
## Claude Deck 0.1.2

Claude Code in the Steam Deck Quick Access Menu: an agent that can troubleshoot, repair, configure and install things on SteamOS / Bazzite, with a controller-first UI, Plan and Auto modes, offline voice dictation and persistent memory.

### What's new
- **Fix:** the voice-model download failed inside Decky with `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED`. It now uses the system CA bundle and falls back to `curl`. After a failed download Settings shows the error and a **Retry** button.
- **Settings are always one tap away:** a button at the top of the QAM panel (with a "N to set up" badge) and a gear in the plugin's title bar.
- **English and Italian.** The UI follows Steam's language (English if unsupported) and can be changed in *Settings → Lingua / Language*; Claude replies in your language.
- **Your sudo password now survives plugin updates.** If you update *from 0.1.0*, enter it once more.
- Detailed README (English + Italian) with screenshots and a demo video, plus third-party license notices.

### Install
1. Have [Decky Loader](https://decky.xyz) and Claude Code (signed in) ready.
2. Download **`claude-deck-v0.1.2.zip`** below.
3. In Game Mode: QAM → Decky → ⚙ Settings → General → enable **Developer mode**, then **Developer → Install plugin from ZIP** and pick the file.
4. Open the QAM → **Claude Deck** → **Settings** and follow the checklist (sudo password, voice model).

Full instructions: [README](https://github.com/loddi-o/claude-deck#installation).

### Verify the download
```
sha256sum claude-deck-v0.1.2.zip
fdbede55998460a8df37f8121f0a46e22564dc9356c3fb597ce60ff49405f81c
```

### Notes
- The ZIP includes a static `whisper-cli` (whisper.cpp v1.9.5, MIT; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). The speech model (~190 MB) is downloaded on first use from Settings.
- Developed and tested on SteamOS on an AMD BC-250 with Decky Loader 3.3.1; not yet tested on a physical Steam Deck or on Bazzite. Details in the README's *Known limitations*.
- This plugin lets an AI agent run commands on your device. Please read *Privacy and security* in the README.

---

**Italiano:** correzione del download del modello vocale dentro Decky, pulsante Impostazioni in evidenza, interfaccia in italiano e inglese (segue la lingua di Steam), password sudo che resta dopo gli aggiornamenti e README dettagliato. Installazione: scarica lo ZIP, attiva la modalità sviluppatore di Decky e usa *Sviluppatore → Installa plugin da ZIP*. Guida completa in [README.it.md](https://github.com/loddi-o/claude-deck/blob/main/README.it.md).

thelinuxgmr/decky-dictation-ptt.name: Decky Dictation PTT v1.0.0
thelinuxgmr/decky-dictation-ptt.body:
First release — offline voice-to-text dictation for Steam Deck Game Mode.

**Install now (before it lands in the Decky store):** download `decky-dictation-ptt-v1.0.0.zip` below, then on your Steam Deck open Decky Loader → Settings (gear) → Plugins → **Install from ZIP** and pick the file. Or unzip it into `~/homebrew/plugins/` so the `decky-dictation-ptt` folder sits there, and restart Decky Loader.

**Use:** click into any text box, hold **L4 + R4** together, **wait at least two seconds**, then speak — your voice becomes text. Made for game chat (World of Warcraft, etc.) and any chat room. A Quick Access Menu toggle is included too. Fully offline (Vosk); first run downloads the speech model (~47 MB) with checksum verification.

Note: developed and tested on a Steam Deck running CachyOS Deckify (Game Mode + Decky Loader). The Decky store submission is in review (decky-plugin-database PR #1181).

denver8989/egpu-buddy.name: EGPU Buddy 0.7.310
denver8989/egpu-buddy.body:
0.7.310 — Fix: SteamOS asked for the driver again after every restart; restart with the eGPU connected.

- Fixed: on SteamOS installs made since 0.7.306 (NVIDIA driver 620), the driver was gone after every restart and EGPU Buddy asked to install it again; the eGPU also only came up after a dock power cycle. The boot self-repair looked for the driver in the old place and never put the 620 driver back; it does now, on the first boot after this update. The same mistake kept EGPU Buddy's Game Mode (gamescope) fix from being built on those installs. (SteamOS only; CachyOS / Arch and Bazzite unchanged.)
- Fixed: restarting with the eGPU connected could reset the machine during boot (CachyOS / Arch): the driver had already taken the card and the NVIDIA persistence daemon was using it when EGPU Buddy pulled it away for the memory-window resize. The card is now left alone while a program uses it; the window stays at the firmware size for that boot.
- Uninstall now removes the driver image of every driver version (620 and 615 were left on /home).

denver8989/egpu-buddy.name: EGPU Buddy 0.7.309
denver8989/egpu-buddy.body:
0.7.309 — The installers tell you when EGPU Buddy is already installed.

- New: the .run installer and the one-line command now check first whether EGPU Buddy is already on the machine (installed by any method: Game Mode plugin, .run or the one-line command; they all install the same files). Same version and complete: they say so and change nothing unless you ask for a repair. An older version: they offer the update. A newer version: they warn before going back. Files missing after a system update: they offer the repair. The one-line command says it before downloading anything. (Every install; the Game Mode plugin already did this, and updates, the boot self-repair and the plugin's install are unchanged.)
- The install instructions now say to pick one of the three methods: one is enough.

denver8989/egpu-buddy.name: EGPU Buddy 0.7.308
denver8989/egpu-buddy.body:
0.7.308 — Fix: garbled TV picture through a DisplayPort-to-HDMI adapter.

- Fixed: a TV or HDMI monitor connected through a DisplayPort-to-HDMI adapter (for example a CEC adapter) no longer shows a scrambled picture in Game Mode. Modes the adapter can only pass compressed (4K above 60 Hz) are no longer picked automatically; a resolution picked in Setup > Screen settings still applies. (NVIDIA eGPU installs; screens on DisplayPort or the eGPU's own HDMI port unchanged.)

denver8989/egpu-buddy.name: EGPU Buddy 0.7.307
denver8989/egpu-buddy.body:
0.7.307 — Fix: Game Mode not starting (0.7.306).

- Fixed: with 0.7.306, Game Mode did not start on CachyOS / Arch NVIDIA installs (black screen after a restart or a switch to the TV). Update and Game Mode starts again.

denver8989/egpu-buddy.name: EGPU Buddy 0.7.306
denver8989/egpu-buddy.body:
0.7.306 — NVIDIA 620.73.04 as a beta driver; one driver build at a time.

- New: **Beta driver** (Setup & updates > NVIDIA driver, NVIDIA installs): when NVIDIA releases a new driver and the Driver Lab carries all of EGPU Buddy's patches over to it, Setup offers "Try beta driver". Same safe switch as a driver change: Safe Detach, build, attach, health check, and your current driver comes back by itself if it fails. "Switch to driver 620" returns to the main driver. First beta: NVIDIA 620.73.04.
  NVIDIA 620.73.04 (18 Nov): NVIDIA lists only "minor bug fixes and improvements". Its open driver source shows fixes for colour / HDR tone-mapping settings being dropped on a display mode change, DisplayPort and suspend / resume fixes, and support for newer kernels. 620 (620.70.06) brought faster Wayland explicit sync, fixes for Assassin's Creed Shadows hangs, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth crashes, Vulkan flicker on multi-GPU Wayland and the frame-rate limit with frame generation.

denver8989/egpu-buddy.name: 0.7.70-beta — non-NVIDIA eGPUs get every feature (testers wanted)
denver8989/egpu-buddy.body:
**Beta for non-NVIDIA eGPUs — now the whole project, not just a bring-up script.**

0.7.69 added an AMD/Intel install that skips the NVIDIA driver. This release gives that path every
feature the NVIDIA path has, and applies what other people's reports say about where AMD and Intel
eGPUs actually fail on Linux.

### The instant-reboot problem is not an NVIDIA problem

The AMD SoC resets the machine the moment it hits an unrecoverable interconnect error — a *data fabric
sync flood*, `0x08000800` — and PCIe tunnelling between an AMD USB4 host and a Thunderbolt peripheral is
a documented trigger. Nothing about that depends on who made the graphics card. The non-NVIDIA path was
applying **none** of the mitigations; it now applies all of them: USB4 root ports kept out of runtime
suspend, AER surprise-down and the tunnel ports' fatal errors masked so a cable pull reports instead of
escalating, and latched DPC containment cleared. They are config-space operations on the bridges and are…

denver8989/egpu-buddy.name: 0.7.69-beta — AMD / Intel eGPU install (testers wanted)
denver8989/egpu-buddy.body:
**Beta — AMD / Intel eGPU support, and testers wanted.**

This is the tested 0.7.68 line (RTX 3080 at a full 16 GiB BAR, desktop cable pulls returning to the
desktop) plus a first-class install path for a **non-NVIDIA eGPU**.

### Why an AMD eGPU install is different

Two of this project's components exist only for NVIDIA:

- the patched `nvidia-open` build — the long part of an install, several minutes of compiling
- the GBM-scanout gamescope — solely a fix for the NVIDIA scan-out corruption; it does nothing on Mesa

Neither is needed on AMD or Intel. **Everything else is vendor-neutral and still applies:**

- hot-plug attach in Game Mode and on the Desktop
- safe detach, and recovery from a surprise cable pull
- the session landing back where it started, with the built-in panel re-enabled as an output
- audio following the eGPU output and returning on detach
- the Decky plugin, the desktop app and the boot policy

### How to install it

From the Decky plugin page: **"Install for an…

denver8989/egpu-buddy.name: SteamOS EGPU Buddy 0.8.0-beta3
denver8989/egpu-buddy.body:
0.8.0-beta3 — PRE-RELEASE. Two more attach fixes found while testing beta2 on the NVIDIA eGPU.

- **Panel stayed on next to the eGPU display after an automatic hot-plug (Desktop).** The attach script's panel-off
  step ran as a background job; the script is a transient systemd service, and when its main process exited systemd
  killed the job. It had only ever completed when the script was run by hand. The script now waits for it.
- **The boot_vga step in the NVIDIA attach never ran.** Its functions were defined after the script's `exit`, so the
  call failed silently every time since August. The NVIDIA-only session works on the compositor device pinning alone,
  so the dead step was removed rather than switched on; README and credits corrected (all-ways-egpu's technique is
  used only by the experimental non-NVIDIA path).
- A version hold is only shown while the held version is the installed one.

下载 `DeckyFontPicker-1.4.28.zip`,解压到 `~/homebrew/plugins/` 后重启 Steam。

m4rz3r0/vistazo-decky.name: Vistazo 0.21.0
m4rz3r0/vistazo-decky.body:
### Added
- **Mouse on a desktop.** On the home, the selection follows the pointer, and a click does what A does.
- **Keyboard shelves.** <kbd>Page Up</kbd> / <kbd>Page Down</kbd> switch shelves (Steam's own <kbd>F6</kbd> / <kbd>F7</kbd> keep working as L1 / R1). While the keyboard is in use, the shelf hints show those keys instead of L1 / R1.

### Changed
- **Fewer switches.** The home screen, the game pages, the menu sounds and the daily check for a new version are always on. Their switches are gone, and the settings start with the home and its look.
- **Obsidiana 1.21.** Steam's controller-conflict dialog follows the theme: no grey boxes, and the chosen option in white with the theme's colour.

### Fixed
- **Empty shelves.** Switching to a shelf with no games left nothing selected, and L1 / R1 could not leave it. The full-library tile now takes the selection.

m4rz3r0/vistazo-decky.name: Vistazo 0.20.1
m4rz3r0/vistazo-decky.body:

- **Achievements on the home for RomM games.** The home asked Tender for a RomM game's count, so once Tender was gone it stayed on an old figure. It now asks the add-on the game belongs to (Vistazo RomM 0.10.1 or later), again once add-ons have loaded, after the game closes, and it keeps whatever the game's page has just read.

m4rz3r0/vistazo-decky.name: Vistazo 0.20.0
m4rz3r0/vistazo-decky.body:
### New
- **Add-on buttons sit beside Play.** What an add-on offers on a Steam game's page (GeForce NOW, for instance) is now part of Steam's play row, right after the Play button, reached with left and right. An add-on can show its own mark instead of words.
- **Your picture in the top bar, round.** It now comes round, with a small dot for your status (green online, mint while playing, amber away, grey offline). In Look and sound → Top bar you can pick rounded corners or leave it as Steam shows it.
- **Games added by an add-on get Vistazo's page** even when they are not retro games (GeForce NOW 0.2.0 uses this).
- A retro game's page can show how its save and its console files stand, when the add-on knows.

### Obsidiana 1.20
- The notes of a pending update in Settings → System, and the full-screen patch notes and game news, follow the theme: charcoal cards, the theme's ring, no blurred screenshot behind the text, no capitals.

havok027/nolag.name: v0.17.4
havok027/nolag.body:
## v0.17.4

- **Fonte da versão e do download:** a lista `mudfish.net/releases/` volta a ser a fonte principal (ela traz todos os instaladores, incluindo o Linux mais recente); a página `mudfish.net/download` fica como reserva. O instalador é baixado primeiro do arquivo da lista de releases e, se falhar, do link da página de download.
- **Lista longa:** o plugin passa a ler até 8 MB da página (antes 2 MB), para não cortar a lista antes das versões novas.
- **Motivo da falha à vista:** se a consulta de versão falhar ("Verificar atualização" ou aviso automático), a tela mostra o que aconteceu em cada página (erro de rede ou "nenhum instalador encontrado") e o motivo também vai para o `mudfish-install.log`.
- Nenhum `.py` novo na raiz; nenhuma mudança no `build.yml`; só `mudfish_mgr.py` mudou no backend.

havok027/nolag.name: v0.17.3
havok027/nolag.body:
## v0.17.3

- **Botão "Verificar atualização"** na aba Mudfish (com o Mudfish instalado): consulta a versão mais recente na hora, sem esperar o cache de 6 horas. Mostra um aviso "já está na versão mais recente (X)" ou o aviso de versão nova com o botão de atualizar (que continua pedindo confirmação). Se a consulta falhar, mostra o motivo.
- Textos novos nos 3 idiomas (`mfCheckBtn`, `mfChecking`, `mfUpToDate`).
- `mudfish_check_update` aceita `force` (a consulta automática continua usando o cache).
- Nenhum `.py` novo na raiz; nenhuma mudança no `build.yml`.

havok027/nolag.name: v0.17.2
havok027/nolag.body:
## v0.17.2

- **Atualização do Mudfish corrigida:** a última versão agora vem da página oficial de download (`mudfish.net/download`), que sempre traz a versão atual. A página `mudfish.net/releases/` é só o arquivo de versões antigas e fica como reserva.
- **Download pelo link oficial:** o instalador é baixado do link da página de download; se falhar, tenta o endereço do arquivo de versões (urllib e depois curl em cada um). O erro mostra o motivo de cada tentativa.
- **Você decide:** o plugin não atualiza mais sozinho ao iniciar; só consulta e avisa. Com versão nova, o Painel e a aba Mudfish mostram o aviso e o botão "Atualizar para X", que pede confirmação antes de baixar e instalar. Se o serviço estiver ligado, ele é religado no final.
- Textos novos nos 3 idiomas (`mfUpdateConfirm`, `mfUpdateConfirmOk`).
- Nenhum `.py` novo na raiz; nenhuma mudança no `build.yml`.

havok027/nolag.name: v0.17.1
havok027/nolag.body:
## v0.17.1

- **Nome do jogo corrigido:** a aba Conf mostrava o nome do processo (ex.: "Main") em vez do jogo. Agora o plugin lê o título real no Steam (ex.: Hunt: Showdown) para o "Jogo aberto" e para os perfis salvos, e corrige sozinho perfis antigos que ficaram com o nome do processo. Se o Steam não informar o título, continua o nome anterior.
- **Limpeza do código do Mudfish por jogo:** removidos o ligar ao abrir jogo, a conexão automática e a opção interna `auto_on_game` (backend, tipos e o aviso "Conectar no painel"), sem uso desde a v0.17.0. O Mudfish continua sendo encerrado ao fechar qualquer jogo, e "Manter ligado ao reiniciar" não mudou.
- Configurações antigas com `auto_on_game` são lidas normalmente: o valor é descartado.
- Nenhum `.py` novo na raiz; nenhuma mudança no `build.yml`.

havok027/nolag.name: v0.17.0
havok027/nolag.body:
## v0.17.0

- **Mudfish removido dos perfis por jogo:** como o painel só termina de iniciar depois de aberto no navegador, ligar o Mudfish sozinho ao abrir um jogo não servia mais. Na aba Conf saíram a chave "Mudfish" de cada jogo e a opção "Ativar ao abrir jogo". Os perfis por jogo agora têm só a chave de Wi-Fi.
- O Mudfish passa a ligar somente à mão (Painel ou aba Mudfish, já abrindo o painel no navegador escolhido). Continua sendo encerrado ao fechar qualquer jogo, para proteger os créditos.
- Perfis salvos antes, com a chave Mudfish ligada, continuam válidos: a chave é ignorada. A opção "Manter ligado ao reiniciar" não mudou.
- Textos de ajuda e READMEs atualizados nos 3 idiomas; nenhum `.py` novo na raiz; nenhuma mudança no `build.yml`.

m4rz3r0/vistazo-romm.name: Vistazo RomM 0.12.2
m4rz3r0/vistazo-romm.body:
### New
- **RomM's games on Punktfunk.** Every RomM game shows up in Punktfunk's library, one entry per game, and can be downloaded from the TV. Downloads can be paused, cancelled or removed from there. A game without a Steam entry gets one first. Needs the Punktfunk host plugin in `punktfunk/`.

### Fixed
- **RomM can sleep again.** The Punktfunk catalog no longer reads RomM every 10 minutes on its own. It now refreshes only while you are using RomM, so a RomM that turns off when idle actually turns off.
- **A game stopped from outside closes the emulator too.** When a stream ends, the emulator is closed and the save is sent.
- **Dolphin no longer stays open after a stream.** An emulator that ignores the first request to stop is asked again.

m4rz3r0/vistazo-romm.name: Vistazo RomM 0.11.4
m4rz3r0/vistazo-romm.body:
### New
- **The save is checked when a game starts.** Right before the emulator opens, the save is compared with RomM's: one played on another device is brought first (the start waits a few seconds for it; the previous save is kept as a copy). Until now this only happened when a game closed or its page was opened.
- **A warning when it cannot be checked.** If RomM is not answering, or the save changed both here and on RomM, the game still starts, with a notice not to save over it.

### Changed
- **A game's page asks RomM again after a minute**, not six hours: the game may have been played elsewhere meanwhile.
- **A save RomM did not take when the game closed is sent again** for about two hours, and when Steam next starts.

m4rz3r0/vistazo-romm.name: Vistazo RomM 0.11.3
m4rz3r0/vistazo-romm.body:
### Fixed
- **SteamGridDB backgrounds.** With a SteamGridDB key, a game whose background was ScreenScraper's fanart kept it: Steam took a moment to notice the old one was gone, so SteamGridDB's was skipped. SteamGridDB's background now replaces the fanart. A background you picked, or any other picture, is left alone.

m4rz3r0/vistazo-romm.name: Vistazo RomM 0.11.2
m4rz3r0/vistazo-romm.body:
### Fixed
- **Settings hidden.** Since 0.11.0 most settings groups (connection, saves and BIOS, pictures) did not show in Vistazo's RomM menu. They are all back.
- **Backgrounds from another game.** ScreenScraper's fanart is often from a different game in the series, so it is no longer the first choice: SteamGridDB's background comes first (with your key), then ScreenScraper's fanart, and otherwise just the cover.

### New
- **Change background.** A button on each game's page shows the backgrounds there are as thumbnails (ScreenScraper and SteamGridDB) plus *Only the cover*. The one you pick stays.
- **SteamGridDB key on every device.** Type the key once: it is kept in your RomM account and your other linked devices pick it up on their own. *Remove* takes it off everywhere.

m4rz3r0/vistazo-romm.name: Vistazo RomM 0.11.1
m4rz3r0/vistazo-romm.body:
### Changed
- **This device in RomM.** Each computer shows up in RomM by what it is: *Steam Deck* on a Deck, otherwise *PC* with the system's name. The computer's name, the user and the address are never sent. The new name shows the next time a device is paired.
- **Texts on a desktop.** Messages and the pairing steps say "this device" instead of assuming a Steam Deck.

foxace/decky-collection-creator.name: Collection Creator 1.2.0
foxace/decky-collection-creator.body:
## Collection Creator 1.2.0

Create and fill **Steam collections** from the Quick Access Menu, live — no Steam restart.

It talks to Steam's own `collectionStore` (the same module ROM Sync uses): `NewUnsavedCollection()` →
`AsDragDropCollection().AddApps()` → `Save()`, so the library updates immediately.

### Features
- list of your collections (Steam's dynamic pseudo-collections such as *Uncategorized* / *Soundtracks* are filtered out),
- create/fill a collection from a **title filter** over your non-Steam shortcuts,
- automatic re-naming of collections Steam saved without a `name` (matched by app-id signature),
- French / English UI (follows the Steam client language),
- works in Gaming and Desktop Mode.

### Install
Decky Loader required. Unzip into `~/homebrew/plugins/` so you get `~/homebrew/plugins/collection-creator/`, then
restart Decky (or Steam).

```bash
cd ~/homebrew/plugins && sudo unzip ~/Downloads/collection-creator-1.2.0.zip
sudo chown -R root:root collection-creator && sudo chmod -R a+rX collection-creator
```

### Notes
- `collectionStore` is an undocumented Steam global; a client update may move it (the panel then shows a message
  instead of crashing).
- Game matching is a title substring on **non-Steam shortcuts** only.
- Repository: https://github.com/foXaCe/decky-collection-creator

---

## Version française

Créer et remplir des **collections Steam** depuis le menu d'accès rapide, à chaud, sans redémarrer Steam.

Le plugin passe par le `collectionStore` de Steam (comme ROM Sync) : création, ajout des jeux, `Save()` — la
bibliothèque se met à jour immédiatement.

- liste des collections (les vues dynamiques *Sans catégorie* / *Bandes-son* sont masquées),
- création/remplissage par **filtre sur le titre** parmi les raccourcis non-Steam,
- renommage automatique des collections enregistrées sans `name` (retrouvées par signature d'appids),
- interface **français / anglais**,
- fonctionne en mode Gaming et Bureau.

Installation : Deky Loader requis, dézipper dans `~/homebrew/plugins/` puis redémarrer Decky.

pochowan/decky-autohdr.name: v1.1.0
pochowan/decky-autohdr.body:
### Added
- **Edit profiles** selector: pick the global profile or any installed game (Steam and non-Steam)
  and set up its profile and launch options without launching it. Games with their own profile
  are marked with ★ and listed first. The running game is selected automatically.
- Per-game switch **Hide the game's native HDR**. Some games (Elden Ring, Nightreign and other
  FromSoftware titles) turn on their own HDR as soon as the display is in HDR. It stacks on top of
  AutoHDR and makes colors look washed out. The switch adds `DXVK_HDR=0` to the game's Steam launch
  options so the game sees an SDR display, and removes it when turned off. Existing launch options
  are kept. Available in all 10 languages.

pochowan/decky-autohdr.name: v1.0.0
pochowan/decky-autohdr.body:
First public release.

### Added
- Native Vulkan layer (`VK_LAYER_AUTOHDR`) that turns a game's SDR swapchain into HDR10
  (PQ / BT.2020). It runs below Wine/Proton, so no Windows DLL is injected into the game.
- Compute-shader port of the ReShade `AutoHDR.fx` math: inverse Reinhard tonemap,
  BT.709 → BT.2020 (optional "Vivid" expanded gamut) and PQ encoding.
- Color controls: paper white, peak brightness, brightness, contrast, saturation,
  color temperature and gamma. All of them apply live.
- Global profile and per-game profiles, applied automatically when a game starts.
- Status that reads the real panel state from the kernel (DRM `Colorspace`), plus a
  diagnostics report.
- UI in 10 languages: Español, English, Français, Deutsch, Italiano, Português, Català,
  中文, 日本語, Русский. Automatic mode follows Steam's language.
- Per-game opt-out with the `DISABLE_AUTOHDR=1 %command%` launch option.

[1.0.0]: https://github.com/Pochowan/decky-autohdr/releases/tag/v1.0.0

sknowledge1/ayaneo3-decky.body:
Fan control, joystick lights and Magic Modules for the AYANEO 3 on Bazzite, in the Decky menu.

## What it does

- **Fan:** Auto, Quiet, Manual and a custom Curve, with the CPU temperature and fan speed always in view. 100% at 95 °C in every mode except Auto; the fan goes back to Auto whenever Decky stops.
- **Joystick lights:** Off, Solid, Breathe and Rainbow, five preset colours, your own colour and brightness. Your choice comes back after refitting the modules or waking the device.
- **Magic Modules:** release the left, right or both modules; they switch back on by themselves once refitted.
- If the plugin's background part stops responding, the panel says so instead of showing old values.

## Install

Download `Ayaneo3-Decky.zip`, then in Decky's settings turn on Developer mode and choose **Install Plugin from ZIP File**. Don't unzip it. See [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/sknowledge1/Ayaneo3-Decky/blob/v1.0.0/docs/INSTALL.md).

Tested on an AYANEO 3 (Ryzen 7 8840U) with Bazzite 45 and Decky Loader 3.3.1; see [VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/sknowledge1/Ayaneo3-Decky/blob/v1.0.0/docs/VALIDATION.md). The HX 370 model has not been tested.

First release, experimental. An add-on for [Vistazo](https://github.com/m4rz3r0/vistazo-decky): install it from Vistazo's settings, under Add-ons.

### What it does
- **Any GeForce NOW game as an entry in Steam.** In the settings, search Nvidia's list by name (games of any shop, not only Steam's) and add the ones you want. Each gets its cover and wide picture, and they show on a GeForce NOW shelf on Vistazo's home (turn the shelf on under Shelves).

rosakodu/zapret-deck.body:
## Steam Deck fixes

- The Desktop Mode tray now connects through a Unix socket restricted to the `deck` user.
- Zapret reports a conflict if NFQUEUE 220 is occupied and only stops the `nfqws` process it started.
- Zapret verifies queue ownership before installing firewall rules and saves its enabled state after a successful start. If a strategy switch fails, it attempts to restore the previous strategy.
- The tray API remains available if a saved service fails to start.

Download `zapret-deck.zip` for manual installation. If the tray was open during the update, restart it to connect to the new socket.

Verified with 77 Python tests, a frontend build, and an isolated NFQUEUE binding check on Steam Deck.

cwallace/decky-touchscreen-toggle.name: Touchscreen Toggle 0.5 Beta
cwallace/decky-touchscreen-toggle.body:
## Touchscreen Toggle 0.5 Beta

- Turn touchscreen input off or on from Decky's Quick Access Menu.
- Use **Games only** to disable touch during games and restore it outside games.
- Choose **Game exceptions** for installed games that should keep touch enabled.
- Bundled helper and Decky-managed root backend; no separate system-wide helper installation is required.

This is an early beta with limited device coverage. Broader Steam Deck/SteamOS and handheld testing is still needed before 1.0.

### Installation

Wait for **Build plugin** to attach `touchscreen-toggle-0.5.0.zip`, then install that ZIP through Decky's manual plugin installer. GitHub's **Source code** ZIP/tar.gz downloads are development source, not installable plugin packages.

Keep a controller, mouse or keyboard available: disabling touch also affects Steam menus and Desktop Mode. Turn off Games only and Disable touchscreen to restore touch, or reboot. This release does not publish the plugin to Decky's marketplace.

wayk-a/xray-vpn-decky.name: Xray VPN Decky v1.0.0
wayk-a/xray-vpn-decky.body:
VPN-клиент для Steam Deck на базе Xray-core с TUN-туннелированием. Работает прямо в Gamemode (Quick Access Menu), совместим с подписками Happ/v2rayTUN и полными JSON-конфигами Xray.

## Установка (6 шагов)

1. Скачайте `xray-vpn-decky.zip` ниже
2. Включите режим разработчика в Decky Loader (Settings → Developer → Developer Mode)
3. Установите из архива: Decky → Developer → Install Plugin from ZIP
4. Перейдите в Desktop Mode
5. Выполните в терминале:

   ```bash
   sudo setcap 'cap_net_admin,cap_net_bind_service,cap_net_raw=+eip' /home/deck/homebrew/plugins/xray-vpn-decky/bin/xray
   ```

6. Вернитесь в Gamemode → Quick Access Menu → Xray VPN Decky → добавьте подписку → Подключить

## Что внутри

- Ядро Xray-core 26.11.9 (linux-amd64) + geoip.dat / geosite.dat — в комплекте, ничего докачивать не нужно
- Поддержка подписок Happ/v2rayTUN (base64 со списком vless://) и полных JSON-конфигов Xray (v2rayN export)
- Несколько подписок, пинг серверов (TCP), сортировка и поиск
- Автоподключение при старте Steam, автопереподключение при обрыве (до 3 попыток)
- Логи диагностики прямо в интерфейсе плагина

## Лицензии

- Код плагина — MIT
- [Xray-core](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core) — MPL-2.0
- geoip.dat / geosite.dat — [Loyalsoldier/v2ray-rules-dat](https://github.com/Loyalsoldier/v2ray-rules-dat)

adrigm/vibrantdeck.name: v2.2.4
adrigm/vibrantdeck.body:
Fix: reliably re-apply color settings after resume from suspend.

Detects suspend via CLOCK_MONOTONIC vs CLOCK_BOOTTIME drift — no subprocess, no dbus, no Steam Client dependency. Works regardless of Decky's plugin sandbox.

## Install
Download `vibrantDeck-2.2.4.zip`, extract, and place the `vibrantDeck` folder in `~/homebrew/plugins/` on your Steam Deck.

adrigm/vibrantdeck.name: v2.2.3
adrigm/vibrantdeck.body:
Fix: resume-from-suspend detection now works again.

Valve removed the Steam Client API that earlier versions relied on to notice when the Deck woke up, so vibrancy/brightness/color-temp were being lost until you re-opened the plugin. The backend now listens to systemd-logind's PrepareForSleep signal via `gdbus monitor` and re-pushes the last applied values (with retries) as soon as the system resumes -- independent of the Steam Client.

## Install
Download `vibrantDeck-2.2.3.zip`, extract, and place the `vibrantDeck` folder in `~/homebrew/plugins/` on your Steam Deck.

chiko751/guided.name: Guided 1.6.0
chiko751/guided.body:
**XMB (PS3 preset)**
- Rebuilt after the original PS3 XMB: categories in one row with the content as a list under the chosen category; submenus (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, settings, media library, party …), My games, Friends and Achievements open as a sub-list to the right; the in-game tab, achievements (as a trophy list) and notifications (a drop-down under the clock) follow the look; the button legend sits in the bottom right corner.
- Checkboxes instead of switches and content as a list – both are settings for every preset.

**New**
- *Status bar* for every preset (*Text & icons › System icons*): profile picture, gear, add game, notifications, battery and clock in one frame at the top right; notifications drop down below it. Optional background: your Steam mini profile or profile background.
- Discord screen sharing through Steamcord: watch a screen share in the Guide, in full screen or as picture-in-picture over the game (LT / RT size, stick position); share your own screen; *Stream quality* while you share (sets Discord's own Go Live quality, up to 1080p 60 fps).
- Calls: participants as a compact list; all buttons in one row (down reaches a wrapped row); *Chat* opens the chat of the call.
- Media Player: search for songs (Spotify and YouTube Music), repeat (all / one song).
- In-game tab: volume of the running game only (Linux; also for games whose audio stream carries no process id).
- One palette of 26 colors for every color choice, sorted the same way everywhere; the text color also tints the content icons; tab icon size; bold text for every font; more text colors.
- Presets remember tab position, switch style and list setting; own themes keep changes to them without saving again.

**Changes**
- *Content as a list* and *Switch style* moved from *Window* to *Text › Content*.
- Guided's settings pages use one text size for every row.
- Help: updated menu names, new topic *Friends and party*.

**Fixes**
- YouTube Music and Spotify playlists load completely (only the first ~100 / 400 songs before).
- B in a chat closes only the chat and goes back to the friend.
- Steam keyboard: the home screen behind the Guide no longer slides up.
- Achievements: Steam's request can hang – after 15 s the Guide says so instead of loading forever.
- The tab color now applies to every tab in the XMB look.
- Much lower CPU use while the Guide is open (no style recalculations every 200 ms).

Install: download **Guided-v1.6.0.zip** and install it in Decky (Developer → Install plugin from ZIP), or update from the Guide (System & Power → Update Guided).

- **Sound in quick settings:** Steam has no audio controls on Windows, so Guided now talks to Windows directly – volume, microphone, and output / input device (picking a device makes it the Windows default). Volume changes made in Windows show up too.

shak18/glance-library.name: Glance Library v1.1.2 - Standalone Repo Migration & Custom Sort Title
shak18/glance-library.body:
# 🚀 Glance Library v1.1.2 — Standalone Repository Transition & Update Migration

Welcome to **Glance Library v1.1.2**! This release marks our official transition to a dedicated standalone repository: [**shak18/glance-library**](https://github.com/shak18/glance-library).

---

## 🌟 What's in v1.1.2

- **Official Standalone Home:**
  - Glance Library is now hosted at its own independent repository: [https://github.com/shak18/glance-library](https://github.com/shak18/glance-library).
  - Future issues, discussions, and releases will be centralized there.
- **In-Menu Auto-Updater Migration:**
  - Updated the in-menu auto-updater to query `shak18/glance-library` directly, while maintaining a smooth fallback to `shak18/game-glance`.
  - Upgrading to v1.1.2 automatically re-points your Decky in-menu updater to future releases on the new repository.
- **Full Custom Sort Title Support:**
  - Retains all sorting enhancements honoring Steam's native Custom Sort Title (`sort_as`) and natural alphanumeric ordering for game series (e.g., *Yakuza* / *Like A Dragon*).

---

## 📦 Download & Installation

### Option 1: In-Menu Auto-Update (Recommended)
If you already have Glance Library installed:
1. Open the **Decky Quick Access Menu** (QAM).
2. Go to the **Glance Library** menu.
3. Check for updates and select **Update** to install v1.1.2 automatically!

### Option 2: Manual Installation
1. Download **`glance-library.zip`** from the Assets below.
2. In Decky Loader settings, enable Developer Mode and choose **"Install plugin from ZIP"** (or extract to `/home/deck/homebrew/plugins/glance-library/`).

embergabor/wavesafe-deck-plugin.body:
Quality-of-life release focused on how it **sounds** and how it **stops**.

## 🎧 Audio quality
- **Full float (32-bit) playback path** — ReplayGain, the music-volume mixer, and resampling now all happen in float, so there's no 16-bit truncation. Highs are smoother and quieter passages are cleaner.
- **High-quality resampler (soxr "very high")** — 44.1 kHz music is now upsampled to the Deck's native 48 kHz with a proper resampler instead of MPD's basic internal one, removing harsh/aliased highs.

## ⏩ Playback
- **Seeking no longer garbles** — dragging the progress bar holds the position and makes one clean jump when you let go, instead of stuttering through the track.

- **Uninstalling or disabling the plugin now stops the music** — previously the background audio daemon could keep playing with no way to stop it. It now shuts down cleanly (and your queue/position still restore on next launch).

andriuspetravicius/deckcord.name: v1.0.9
andriuspetravicius/deckcord.body:
## Changelog
- Restored Deckcord loading on current SteamUI/Decky setups by retrying Discord BrowserView creation and tolerating stale backend/client transports.
- Fixed Steam left sidebar injection so Discord appears again even after SteamUI navigation tree changes.
- Hardened the DOM fallback menu injection so observer/interval retries cannot throw uncaught `insertBefore` errors.
- Added safer Discord client websocket handling for state, media, request/response, and CDP reconnect paths.

## Validation
- Built frontend with `pnpm run build`.
- Type checked with `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck`.
- Checked Python syntax with `python3 -m compileall -q main.py defaults`.
- Verified on a Steam Deck via SSH: Decky loaded Deckcord, the backend stayed running, and the Steam left menu showed one Discord item without the previous `insertBefore` execution error.

andriuspetravicius/deckcord.name: v1.0.8
andriuspetravicius/deckcord.body:
## Changelog
- Status bar (clock / battery / wifi) now stays visible on top of Discord while the Discord tab is open. A CSS override forces the Big Picture status-bar container back into view instead of letting SteamUI hide it on custom plugin routes.
- On-screen keyboard now uses the `m_refKeyboard` API directly (`SetAsCurrentVirtualKeyboardTarget` + `ShowVirtualKeyboard`). Blurs the currently-focused Steam UI input (e.g. library search) before showing the OSK so text reliably routes to the Discord chat box.
- Fixed backend `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'prepare'` being logged on every OSK request — the `/openkb` handler now returns a proper `aiohttp.web.Response`.

## Known tradeoff
- Steam's side menus do not render a blur overlay over custom plugin BrowserViews — they are solid black by design. Sidebar overlays on top without blur.

andriuspetravicius/deckcord.name: v1.0.7
andriuspetravicius/deckcord.body:
## Changelog
- Fix: Steam status bar and side menus now overlay on top of the Discord BrowserView (with native blur) instead of hiding behind it. Discord no longer shifts right when the left menu opens.
- Fix: On-screen keyboard now reliably routes key input to the Discord chat box instead of the Steam library search. Blurs Steam's focused input, raises the BrowserView, fires NotifyUserActivation, and re-asserts focus before showing the OSK.

andriuspetravicius/deckcord.name: v1.0.6
andriuspetravicius/deckcord.body:
## Changelog
- Improved Steam side menu behavior by resizing/repositioning the Discord BrowserView instead of hiding it, so Discord remains visible when menus are open.
- Fixed on-screen keyboard routing by forcing BrowserView focus before opening the keyboard, preventing input from going to Steam's library search.
- Updated editable-tap handling to always trigger backend OSK opening for more reliable text input in Discord fields.

## Fix
- Rebuilt release zip with `dist/index.js` included; previous v1.0.6 asset was missing and caused `TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module` on load.

ccc007ccc/ds5bridge-steamos.name: DS5Bridge for SteamOS v0.2.16
ccc007ccc/ds5bridge-steamos.body:
SteamOS lifecycle recovery release.

- Fixes DS5Bridge modules and builder cache being mistaken for an uninstall and deleted when SteamOS shuts down or Decky reloads the plugin.
- Arms destructive cleanup only for an explicit Decky uninstall; plugin updates use generation handoff and preserve modules, runtime settings, and cached build tools.
- Safely discards the legacy v0.2.15 reboot watcher state instead of resuming destructive cleanup.
- Accepts Decky-owned cleanup locks so an interrupted real uninstall can be recovered without invalid_uninstall_state.
- Treats a missing or old-kernel module as a recoverable local-build state, preserves the enable intent, and automatically resumes the bridge after a successful build.
- Makes the About page derive the SteamOS plugin version from package.json and displays the runtime version and kernel source revision separately.

Validated with TypeScript type checking, 9 frontend tests, 86 backend tests, Rollup/package verification, GitHub Actions CI, Decky update/reload testing, a full Decky uninstall cleanup, reinstall, and a cold 19-stage local build on SteamOS.

ccc007ccc/ds5bridge-steamos.name: DS5Bridge for SteamOS v0.2.15
ccc007ccc/ds5bridge-steamos.body:
SteamOS-focused Decky maintenance release.

- Keeps checking the DS5Bridge PipeWire graph at a low 5-second cadence while a controller is bridged, so audio nodes that fail after the initial connection can recover in the same session.
- Reads the active ALSA card dynamically and defers profile rebuilding while a game still owns the raw playback PCM; recovery runs only after the PCM is closed.
- Rebuilds only the affected DualSense card profile and does not restart global PipeWire, WirePlumber, Bluetooth, or the controller bridge.
- Makes the builder failure-stage regression test independent of the developer machine\047s free disk space.
- Does not change Proton, game audio endpoint enumeration, the kernel modules, USB descriptors, or the shared runtime.

Validated with TypeScript type checking, 9 frontend tests, 79 backend tests, Rollup build, package integrity checking, and GitHub Actions CI.

ccc007ccc/ds5bridge-steamos.name: DS5Bridge for SteamOS v0.2.14
ccc007ccc/ds5bridge-steamos.body:
SteamOS-focused Decky release built around exact-kernel local compilation.

- Bundles the pinned DS5Bridge kernel source and builds modules locally for the running SteamOS kernel.
- Keeps module install, rebuild, load, stop, delete, progress, and persistent task logs in one Decky workflow.
- Preserves the active bridge across ordinary plugin updates while Decky uninstall removes the hook, modules, builder image, and owned caches.
- Adds the bridge switch, controller status, audio and haptic controls, microphone level, looped speaker and haptic tests, and the full-screen settings/about pages.
- Uses the native DualSense USB audio identity, UCM endpoints, interface order, and channel layout.
- Detects a stale PipeWire split graph after USB re-enumeration and rebuilds only the affected DualSense profile; healthy audio graphs are left untouched.
- Bundles `ds5bridge-runtime v0.2.0-alpha.7`, including resilient audio path controls and native 48/64-byte adaptive-trigger report handling.…

ccc007ccc/ds5bridge-steamos.name: DS5Bridge for SteamOS v0.2.8
ccc007ccc/ds5bridge-steamos.body:
SteamOS-first local-build release.

- Removes numeric Stage gates, developer mode, qualification records, and candidate/stable release machinery.
- Bundles the pinned DS5Bridge kernel source directly in the Decky package; every machine compiles modules for its exact running SteamOS kernel.
- Removes the separate source plan and builder descriptor.
- Reuses a cached SteamOS compiler environment containing tools only; it does not contain prebuilt kernel modules.
- Keeps build progress, deterministic double-build verification, exact vermagic validation, module start/stop/delete, and Decky uninstall cleanup.

Verified on SteamOS kernel 6.16.12-drmexec7.valve24.5-1-neptune-616-drm-exec-gf253f5da553e without loading or unloading modules during the release test.

qd313/bonsai.name: bonsAI v0.6.0
qd313/bonsai.body:
bonsAI is an AI chat that lives in the Steam Deck's Quick Access Menu. It talks to Ollama, running on the Deck itself or on a PC on the same network, so you can ask about the game you are playing without leaving it. bonsAI is free and open source. It runs on your own hardware, your privacy stays yours. No paid API, no data centers.

### What it does

- **Ask about the game you're playing.** bonsAI knows which game is running, so you can ask about a boss, a level or a puzzle.
- **Notes from the game's wiki.** Answers can use notes from community wikis, 38 games so far, and it works offline.
- **The knowledge library.** The notes from game wikis are downloaded once, after you say yes, and then used offline.
- **Your own notes.** Tell bonsAI what matters to you and it remembers.
- **Spoilers stay hidden until you ask.** In Strategy mode, anything that looks like a spoiler is covered.
- **"Where are you at?"** Strategy can ask where you are in the game, then gives you a checklist of steps.
- **Ask about a screenshot.** Take a screenshot and ask what is on screen, like a puzzle, a menu or an error message.
- **Search your chats, settings and notes.** A Search tab to the left of Main finds things without any AI.
- **Close the menu, keep playing.** Close the menu while an answer is being written, and a popup tells you when it is ready.
- **Saved chats.** Keep up to ten chats and flip between them with the triggers.
- **Talk instead of typing.** Press the mic button and talk. Your speech becomes text on the Deck itself.
- **See how it answered.** Show details under any answer shows which model wrote it and which notes it used.
- **A first-run popup.** The first time you open bonsAI, it asks where the AI should run: on the Deck or on a PC.

### What is different from 0.4.9

- A new tab bar.
- Saved chats: ten of them, with "Sum up this chat".
- The Search tab.
- Your own notes.
- A thinking fold that shows how the AI worked toward an answer, and a decode effect while the answer is written.
- An Internet downloads permission. It is off on a fresh install, so nothing downloads without a yes from you.
- Gone: reading answers aloud.
- Gone: the Steam ban lookup.
- Gone: the recommended-models list refreshing itself from the internet.

### Known problems

- Rarely, the D-pad may stop moving in the panel. Close and reopen the Quick Access Menu. If that does not help, reload the plugin from Decky's settings. Restarting the Deck always clears it.
- On the Settings tab, after opening several sections and walking with the D-pad, the ring can skip a control (for example Terse mode). Closing and reopening the menu puts it right.
- Rarely, after you touch the screen, a faded second copy of the tab bar shows over the suggestion chips for a moment. The plugin hides it again by itself.
- The kids lock (Steam's parental controls turning bonsAI's high-impact permissions off) has not yet been checked on a child account.
- The first answer after installing the AI on the Deck takes a minute or two while the model loads. The panel says so.
- With a game running, the panel can update more slowly while an answer arrives, and very long answers can dip further. With the AI on a PC it stays smooth in our tests.
- Answers come from a small AI model on your Deck or PC. They can be wrong, can repeat wording from an earlier answer, and questions that aren't about a game can pick up game notes.
- Once, with a game running and the AI on the Deck itself, Steam's screen stopped responding a few minutes after an answer; restarting the Deck cleared it.

### Installing over 0.4.9

0.6.0 was not tested as an upgrade from 0.4.9. If anything looks off after installing over the old version, open Settings, press Clear all data, and set up again. Your settings from 0.4.9 are read and carried over where they still exist, but the Steam key is deleted, because the ban lookup it was for is gone.

### The full list

Every change since 0.4.9, session by session, is in [the detailed list](https://github.com/qd313/bonsAI/blob/main/docs/changelog-0.6.0-full.md).

To see the code changes themselves, open the [compare view from v0.4.9 to v0.6.0](https://github.com/qd313/bonsAI/compare/v0.4.9...v0.6.0).


---

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/qd313/bonsAI/compare/v0.4.9...v0.6.0

qd313/bonsai.name: bonsAI v0.4.9

shikamaru2694/cuivarpulse.name: Cuivar Pulse 1.1.0
shikamaru2694/cuivarpulse.body:
## What's new

- **TV mode.** Switch the player from ♪ to 📺 and the song's music video plays as retro pixel art, in sync with the music, in the panel or fullscreen. Three styles: **Retro** (32-colour game palette), **Arcade** (CRT scanlines) and **Game Boy**. Songs with only a lyric video or a still image keep their artwork. TV mode never runs while a game is open, and does nothing when the panel is closed.
- **Fullscreen.** The new ⛶ button shows the artwork big in Music mode, or the pixel video in TV mode. Any button closes it.
- **Simpler light colours:** Artwork (follows the video in TV mode, like Ambilight), Rainbow (flows faster as the song gets intense) and One colour.
- **Bluetooth headphones:** the lights and rumble wait for the audio delay, so they land on the beat you hear.
- **Build-ups:** the lights swell for two seconds before a big drop.
- **A tidier player:** icon buttons, and a Music / TV switch right under the play button.
- **Settings work properly with the D-pad:** the window opens at the top and scrolls as you move.

## Safer, smaller release

- **Built by GitHub** from the tagged source code, with a signed build provenance attestation and a `SHA256SUMS` file. The ZIP is now **0.5 MB** (was 41 MB): no programs or packed code inside, only source files and the built panel. See *What's in the release* in the README.
- **The music engine is downloaded on first launch** from the official yt-dlp and QuickJS releases and checked against their published SHA-256. yt-dlp is now its readable pure-Python version, run with the system's Python.
- **The engine updates itself:** a quiet check once a day, and straight away when YouTube changes something (the song is retried once). A new version is tried before it's used, and the previous one is kept if anything goes wrong. *Update music engine* in Settings stays as a backup.
- Helper programs get only the environment variables they need, and HTTPS uses your system's own certificate store.

## Fixes

- Voice search no longer searches for sound labels like "[music]" when it hears no speech.

The install link now always gets the newest version:
`https://github.com/shikamaru2694/CuivarPulse/releases/latest/download/CuivarPulse.zip`

berczeller/rat.name: RAT 1.1.0
berczeller/rat.body:
Bug-fix release focused on putting game files back exactly as they were.

### Changed
- Settings that change game files are refused while a background task runs, instead of two writers editing the same files
- Preset actions only work on ReShade presets, so delete and import can't touch `OptiScaler.ini`, `fakenvapi.ini` or the game's own .ini files
- Unknown ReShade proxy names and injector option values are rejected
- The job log says when a release publishes no checksum and the download can't be verified
- Release zips use the full version number (`RAT-1.1.0.zip`)

### Fixed
- Removing ReShade no longer overwrites the injector's `dxgi.dll`, and removing the injector afterwards brings the game's original back
- Uninstall keeps a file a game update shipped in place of one RAT added (`dxgi.dll`, `libxess.dll` and others)
- The game's original is restored even when an earlier install was interrupted
- Removing a HelixSR Scaler that RAT didn't install no longer loses the game's file when a restore fails
- Game DLLs that differ from RAT's only in letter case (`D3DCompiler_47.dll`, `LibXeSS.dll`) are backed up and restored like any other
- Turning d4r off only renames the DLLs d4r installed, not the game's own `dxgi.dll` or `d3d12.dll`
- ReShade backs up a game DLL again after a game update puts it back
- "Close the game first" works for libraries on the SD card or other symlinked folders
- Laptops with an AMD APU and a discrete NVIDIA or AMD GPU now detect the discrete card
- The main executable is found even when its name contains words like "server" (`Observer.exe`)
- A game set to the default Proton reports the global default tool
- Pasted `releases/tag/...` links work for releases older than the 15 newest
- `env -u FOO` after gamescope survives launch option cleanup, and backslash escapes are split correctly
- Checksum files in BSD format or with `./name` entries are understood
- Interrupted downloads retry with curl and leave no `.part` file behind
- Unreal's UTF-16 `Engine.ini` is no longer corrupted when RAT writes to it
- A failed re-import of a fork link keeps the source that was already there
- Profiles imported from a `.rat.json` with wrong types no longer break every later game start
- HelixSR's install result is no longer lost when its last output line arrives late
- Switching games during a call no longer shows the previous game's state, launch plan or Proton tool
- Switching the frame generation method clears the previous method's pending edits
- The progress dialog closes on its own again after chained tasks (wipe, then install)
- Cancelling a text prompt closes it cleanly, and **Remove ReShade** leaves launch options alone when ReShade stays for HDR

### Install
Download `RAT-1.1.0.zip` and install it from **Decky > Settings > Developer > Install plugin from ZIP file**. `SHA256SUMS.txt` has the checksums. The "Source code" archives GitHub adds won't install.

danielcamilo1/decky-clean-steam-temp-fol.name: v1.0.0
danielcamilo1/decky-clean-steam-temp-fol.body:
First public release.

### Added

- Quick Access panel for deleting the contents of `steamapps/temp` in any detected Steam library.
- Automatic Steam library discovery: parses `steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf` and always seeds the internal library at `~/.local/share/Steam`, deduplicating by normalized path. External drives, SD cards and shared dual-boot partitions are picked up automatically.
- Temp folder stats before deletion — item count plus total size, measured with `du -sb` so sparse files and symlinks are accounted for correctly.
- Two-step confirmation on the clean action, with a cancel button.
- The selected library is persisted to `settings.json` and restored on the next launch.
- `_is_valid_temp_path` safety gate on every path-taking backend method: any path whose last two components are not `steamapps/temp` is rejected before a stat or a delete happens.
- Result feedback in-panel and via a Steam toast, reporting how many items were deleted and any per-item errors.
- Warning banner in the panel about closing Steam before cleaning.
- GitHub Actions workflow that builds the plugin and publishes a release whenever the version in `package.json` changes on `main`.

### Notes

- The plugin declares the `root` flag so it can reach libraries on mounted external drives. Because the backend runs as root, `decky.HOME` is `/root`, and library detection uses `decky.DECKY_USER_HOME` to find the real user's Steam data.
- Forked from [decky-plugin-template](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-plugin-template); the template's C backend (`backend/`) and `defaults/` directory have been removed, as this plugin is TypeScript frontend plus Python backend only.

pollito001/chat-splitter.name: Chat Splitter v1.2.1
pollito001/chat-splitter.body:
[Leer en español](https://github.com/Pollito001/chat-splitter/blob/main/README.es.md)

Decky Loader plugin for the Steam Deck that splits **voice chat** audio (**Steam chat**, Discord, Vesktop, etc.) from **game** audio.

> ⚠️ **Disclaimer:** Personal project, built with the help of AI (Claude by Anthropic). Provided as-is, with no warranty. If you decide to try it, **you do so at your own risk**.

### What it does
| Situation | Game | Chat |
|---|---|---|
| Docked to TV, no headphones | TV | Deck speakers |
| Docked to TV, with headphones | TV | Headphones |
| Handheld, with headphones | Deck speakers | Headphones |
| Handheld, no headphones | Everything together | |

- Works with jack, Bluetooth or USB headphones.
- Switches automatically when the TV or headphones are connected or disconnected.
- Separate volume sliders for game and chat.
- Mark any app as chat from the panel.

### Steam voice chat
Steam chat runs inside the Steam client, so it isn't detected automatically. During a call, open the panel and turn on **Steam** under *Apps sonando ahora* (Apps playing now). It's saved, so you only do it once. Steam's interface sounds will also go to the chat output. Discord and similar apps are detected automatically.

### Install
1. Download `chat-splitter.zip` below.
2. In Game Mode: Decky → ⚙️ → **Developer** → turn on *Developer mode*.
3. **Install Plugin from ZIP File** → pick the zip.

### Notes
- Tested on Steam Deck OLED.
- On the Deck LCD, handheld mode only works with Bluetooth or USB headphones (the jack and speakers are the same device there).
- The plugin's panel is in Spanish.

This plugin only changes the CPU frequency governor. It does not modify TDP, GPU clocks, or any other power-management settings.

enotherms/haqgen.name: HaqGen 0.1.3
enotherms/haqgen.body:
A cleaner panel, and HaqEngine installs with one button.

## What's new

- **Install HaqEngine from the panel.** The **Engine (experimental)** row now has an **Install HaqEngine** button. HaqGen downloads a pinned [HaqEngine](https://github.com/Enotherms/HaqEngine) release, checks its checksum and installs it. Desktop Mode is not needed. When a newer pinned version ships with HaqGen, the row offers **Update HaqEngine**. **Remove HaqEngine** is under Troubleshooting › Reset and remove and asks first.
- **Clearer layout.** The panel has three sections in Steam's own style: Frame generation, Launch and Settings. The four drop-downs at the bottom are now two: **Advanced** includes the Flatpak apps list, and **Troubleshooting** ends with the reset and remove actions.
- **Plain descriptions** for the advanced settings (motion quality, Gamescope compatibility, lighter model, debug log).
- **Restart tags.** A small amber tag marks every setting that only takes effect after restarting the game or app. Nothing in HaqGen needs the Deck itself restarted.
- **Footer** with the HaqGen version and a GitHub button that opens the source page.
- The frame generation slider is now labelled **Multiplier**.

Your profiles and settings carry over.

## Install or update

In Decky settings › Developer, use **Install Plugin From URL** with the link to `HaqGen-v0.1.3.zip` below. Or download the zip and use **Install Plugin From ZIP**. Installing over an earlier version keeps your settings. If HaqGen is new to you, see the [quick start](https://github.com/Enotherms/HaqGen#quick-start): Lossless Scaling must be on the `lsfg-vk` beta branch.

## Known limitations

- Switching frame generation between Off and on, changing the engine, or changing the FPS cap needs a game restart. 2x, 3x and 4x apply right away.
- HaqEngine is experimental. HaqGen's setup still requires Lossless Scaling, even for players who only use HaqEngine.
- Steam's performance overlay may not count generated frames.
- Frame generation inside a Flatpak game has not been tested on a Deck yet.

HaqGen is an independent, non-commercial hobby project and is not affiliated with Lossless Scaling, lsfg-vk, Decky Loader or Valve.

**SHA-256** `HaqGen-v0.1.3.zip`: `b879841973298fbc006c4e5885e61987fec6502dac78b75322c83701f9b3c7df`

enotherms/haqgen.name: HaqGen 0.1.0
enotherms/haqgen.body:
First public release of HaqGen, a Decky Loader plugin that sets up and controls Lossless Scaling frame generation (through [lsfg-vk](https://lsfg-vk.dev)) from the Steam Deck's Quick Access menu.

This is an early release: it works on a Steam Deck OLED, but has not been tested widely yet.

## Install

tobipjuk/decky-controller-battery.name: Controller Battery v1.2.3
tobipjuk/decky-controller-battery.body:
Bug-fix release of **Controller Battery** for the Lenovo Legion Go's detachable controllers.

- **Fixes a misread that could show a controller as asleep (or, before v1.2.2, at "0%") for a moment.** The
  controllers send several kinds of report with the same ID, and earlier versions sometimes read the wrong one.
  It happened on about one reading in five to ten with the controllers in a charging grip. Only the real status
  report is read now.
- **New state "Charging":** state `0x03`, seen briefly when a charging grip is plugged into power, is no longer
  shown as "State 0x03".
- **Steadier asleep row:** a controller is only shown as asleep once it has read asleep for about 10 seconds, so
  the row appears 15 to 30 seconds after a controller goes to sleep.

**Install / update:** download `controller-battery-v1.2.3.zip` below. In Decky, go to **Developer → Install Plugin
From ZIP File** (Developer mode needs to be on). This replaces v1.2.2 and keeps your saved drain rates.

Tested on a Legion Go (gen 1) with Bazzite stable-44 and InputPlumber: installing over v1.2.2, and 114 readings
over 4 minutes in a powered charging grip with none misread. Not tested on the device yet with this version: a
real sleep, on-battery use, and the "Charging" label (those were tested with captured and simulated readings).

tobipjuk/decky-controller-battery.body:

  idle), its row now reads "Asleep or not connected · press its Legion button", with an empty bar and no
  percentage. Before, it showed "0%" and "State 0x00".
- **Time left survives a sleep:** a sleep no longer ends the time-left session, and the time spent asleep is left
  out of the drain rate.
- **No repeated alerts after waking:** a sleeping controller no longer re-arms its low-battery notifications.

**Install / update:** download `controller-battery-v1.2.2.zip` below. In Decky, go to **Developer → Install Plugin
From ZIP File** (Developer mode needs to be on). This replaces v1.2.1 and keeps your saved drain rates.

Tested on a Legion Go (gen 1) with Bazzite stable-44 and InputPlumber: installing over v1.2.1, the asleep row with
both controllers asleep, and waking them. Not…

Bug-fix release of **Controller Battery** for the Lenovo Legion Go's detachable controllers.

koua29/decky-wicked-dupe.body:
**Fix: the plugin could not find the game save on the console.**

## Fixes
- The Steam folder is now read from the Decky user's home (`DECKY_USER_HOME`): Decky does not always run the backend with HOME set to the deck user.
- The save is found by looking for realm files anywhere in the game's Proton prefix, without relying on exact folder names.
- New **Refresh** button, and the status refreshes every 5 seconds.
- When nothing is found, the panel shows where it searched.
