**Update:** install `Decky-Smooth-Frames.zip` over the old version (Decky → Developer → Install plugin from ZIP), then restart your games once.

lumen-tools/decky-smooth-frames.name: Version 1.2.0
lumen-tools/decky-smooth-frames.body:
**Fixes frame pacing.** Generated frames could reach the screen right before the real ones instead of halfway between them, so motion was not smoother and latency went up. If Smooth Frames felt like "more input lag, no difference", update.

- Frame pacing works in every game: the layer now handles everything the Vulkan specification lets a game attach to a frame (DXVK games were affected most).
- The live status warns if frames are ever generated but not paced.
- Updating the plugin no longer turns Smooth Frames off for all your games.

**Update:** install `Decky-Smooth-Frames.zip` over the old version (Decky → Developer → Install plugin from ZIP), then restart your games once.

lumen-tools/decky-smooth-frames.name: Version 1.1.0
lumen-tools/decky-smooth-frames.body:
**Switch instantly while you play.** The Smooth Frames toggle and the frame rate limit now apply right away in a running game – compare real frames against frame generation without restarting.

- Turn Smooth Frames off and on in a running game: it switches within a second. The live status shows "Off" while it is off.
- Change the frame rate limit while playing: applies instantly.
- A restart is only needed the first time you turn Smooth Frames on for a game, and after changing the frame generation options.
- The minimum frame rate now follows the limit, so lower limits such as 20 FPS keep generating frames.

**Update:** install `Decky-Smooth-Frames.zip` over the old version (Decky → Developer → Install plugin from ZIP), then restart your games once.

ntrpydev/satur8.name: Satur8 v0.5.1
ntrpydev/satur8.body:
The app in Steam Game Mode: its own layout for the Deck's screen, touch and buttons, opened from the Steam library. Also fixes for the Steam Deck launcher entry and the Bazzite installer, the logo as the app icon, and the last backend verified on real hardware.

- The app works in Steam Game Mode. On a Steam Deck it used to open larger
  than the screen (2375x1458 on the 1280x800 screen), so only its top left
  could be touched: the desktop slider stopped at +5% and the add button
  could not be reached. In a gamescope session it now opens at exactly the
  screen's size and shows a layout of its own, drawn 640 logical pixels wide
  (a scale of 2 on a Deck): "General" first (Steam's own screens and
  every game without a row), then one full-width row per game with a wide
  slider, an on/off switch and a remove button that asks first. A tap on a
  slider's track jumps there, a sideways drag changes the value, and a drag
  up or down scrolls the page. There is no mouse cursor and nothing depends
  on hovering. The desktop layout is unchanged.
- The Deck's buttons drive that layout: D-pad or left stick move a
  highlight, A selects (on a slider, A then left and right change it, faster
  while held), B goes back or undoes, X turns the game on or off, Y opens
  the list, L1/R1 change page, L2/R2 change the row's slider by one. A bar
  along the bottom says what the buttons do right now. Touching the screen
  moves the focus and hides the highlight. Steam shows the Deck's controls to
  such a program as a gamepad, which the app reads from the kernel's input
  devices directly; it acts on them only while it is the app in front. A
  keyboard works the same way (arrows, Enter, Escape).
- A game whose row is turned off now shows its normal colors, instead of
  taking the general saturation. This holds in Steam Game Mode and on a
  desktop, in the background service and in `satur8 run`. A game with no row
  at all still gets the general value, and so do the desktop and Steam's own
  screens. On a setup with a value per output, an off row is normal on the
  outputs it would change when on: all of them, the ones it lists, or the
  focused one with `profile_outputs = "focused"`. The first row in Game Mode
  is now called "General" (it was "Everything else").
- A profile the v0.5.0 app named after its program (`eldenring` for
  `eldenring.exe`) shows under its Steam library name ("ELDEN RING") in the
  app when it carries a Steam AppID. Only what is shown changes; the profile
  keeps its name in the file and in the commands.
- A Decky Loader plugin (`satur8-decky-plugin.zip` on the release) for Decky
  users on a Steam Deck: its Quick Access Menu panel says whether Satur8 is
  installed and which version, installs, updates or reinstalls it without
  leaving Game Mode (the release tarball from GitHub, SHA-256 checked before
  anything runs, installed as your user, never as root), and opens the app.
  Install it in Decky under Developer, Install Plugin from URL; it is not on
  the official Decky store. Checked on a Steam Deck OLED with Decky Loader
  v3.3.1: the panel loads and Open Satur8 starts the app. Installing from
  the plugin needs a published release to download, so it is checked after
  this release is out.
- `satur8 auto on|off|status` turns automatic per-game switching on or off
  with one command, the same way the switch on the app's Status page does:
  the background service now and at login, and on KDE Plasma also the KWin
  focus script, with KWin asked to reload over D-Bus by Satur8 itself. In
  Steam Game Mode it is the service alone. The installer's closing message
  and the README show this command, with the commands it replaces kept as a
  by-hand line.
- `satur8 status` marks a level that is kept for an output that is not
  connected as `(not connected)`, so it no longer reads as something on
  screen.
- "Add game" is one list of your games by name, in both layouts: the
  installed Steam games, with any that is running first and marked. A
  running Steam game is recognized by its Steam AppID and shown under its
  Steam name ("ELDEN RING", not `eldenring.exe`); launchers, runtimes,
  wrappers and shells are never listed. A pick adds a profile matched by the
  Steam AppID. The separate "Add running game" dropdown, which listed
  process names, is gone; a running game that is not from Steam is still
  offered by its executable.
- A profile that knows only a game's Steam AppID now also applies to a
  native Steam game on a desktop (its window class is not `steam_app_<ID>`):
  the service reads the AppID from the focused window's process.
- `satur8 steam-shortcut status|add|artwork`: Satur8's entry in the Steam
  library, which is how the app is opened in Game Mode. The installer runs
  `add` on a system with a Steam gaming session (`--no-steam-entry` skips
  it); it asks the running Steam through SteamOS's own tool, never adds a
  second entry, and reports a broken leftover entry named `satur8.desktop`
  from v0.5.0. The entry gets artwork (cover, wide capsule, banner, logo,
  icon). Uninstall takes the artwork off and says that the entry itself
  stays and how to remove it in Steam.
- The Status page works when the app is started from the Steam library,
  where it runs inside Steam's runtime container without `systemctl`: it
  asks the user's systemd over the session bus instead. In Game Mode it
  reads the applied saturation from gamescope.
- Checked for all of the above: unit tests, and the Game Mode layout on a
  virtual 1280x800 screen with a Steam Deck's Game Mode environment (pointer
  presses and drags for touch, keys for the buttons), also started inside
  the Steam Linux Runtime container. Not yet run on a Steam Deck in this
  form: the gamepad reader has not read a real pad, and the step that asks
  Steam to add the entry was not run.
- Fix the app not opening from the application launcher on the Steam Deck:
  the launcher said "Could not find the program 'satur8-gui'", because
  SteamOS does not search `~/.local/bin`. The installer now writes the
  launcher entry with the app's full path. Steam's "Add to Steam" can read the
  entry now too, so the app can be added to the Steam library.
- Fix the installer on Bazzite and Fedora, which have `qdbus-qt6` and no
  `qdbus6`: the command it prints for turning on per-game switching failed
  there, and its steps that unload the KWin effect were skipped. It now uses
  whichever of the two exists. Found on a real Bazzite install.
- The app's icon is now the rainbow 8 from the Satur8 logo instead of the
  green S8 tile, in the window, the taskbar and the application launcher.
- Checked, with no code change: the DRM/KMS path, the last backend that had
  never been run on real hardware. On a Steam Deck OLED's AMD GPU with its
  session held open and no compositor running, `satur8 doctor` chose
  `drm-ctm`, `satur8 set 0` turned color bars gray, 0.5 and 2.0 landed where
  expected, `satur8 off` put the picture back, `--output` with a CRTC ID
  changed that CRTC and an unknown ID was refused. The background service,
  started by hand on that console, showed the desktop saturation at start,
  followed a change to it and restored it when stopped. The README's backend
  table now lists DRM/KMS as Verified.

  - **Start on Boot** (`steamos-crd.target` enable/disable)
  - **Display Resolution** (`1280×800` native 16:10, `1920×1080`, `1920×1200`, `2560×1440`)
  - **Max Frame Rate** (`15`, `30`, `45`, `60` FPS) across PipeWire and X11 capture
  - **Stream Remote Audio**
  - **Clipboard Sync**

  - **Bridge Log Level** (`info`, `debug`, `warn`, `error`) and **Reset Settings to Defaults**

- `steamos-chromoting-decky.zip` — Decky Loader plugin package
- `steamos-chromoting-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` — Portable rootless server & CLI bundle

mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.name: v3.4.10-rc.3
mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.body:
## Changed

- **Plugins from the Decky store now update from the store.** If your installed version is one the stable Decky store lists, only a newer store version counts as an update. A newer GitHub release is mentioned on the card and in details, but isn't offered by quick Update, Update All or paired browsers. You can still install it from the plugin's releases or Search; DeckyHub says first that it replaces your copy. A GitHub install with a version the store also lists is treated as a store copy.
  - For now this works only with the **Registry Channel** set to **Pre-release**. On Stable, nothing changes until the registry's store versions are published there.
- **Clearer audit warnings.** The explanations now say the audit found it, and say "may" where it's only a possibility. They no longer say whether to install.
- **Review wording.** DeckyHub now says it doesn't review plugins, instead of saying nobody does.

## Fixed

- Text you type in the Experimental layout's search fields stays visible when the controller selects the field.

The new text is machine-translated in other languages.

## Try it on your device

- Experimental layout: select the search field in Search and in Discover's filter with the controller, then type. Check the text is readable.
- With the Registry Channel set to Pre-release, find a plugin you installed from the Decky store. Check its card, its details and the Updates count, including **Update All**.
- If it has a newer GitHub release, start installing it from details and check the replace warning, then cancel.
- Check that **Skip version** is hidden for that plugin, and that paired browsers don't offer its GitHub release as an update.
- Read the longer audit warning explanations and check that they fit on screen.

## Security checks

- **Virus scan:** ClamAV found no threats in `DeckyHub-v3.4.10-rc.3.zip` ([scan report](https://github.com/mazillka/deckyhub-plugin/releases/download/v3.4.10-rc.3/ClamAV-scan-v3.4.10-rc.3.txt)).
- **VirusTotal:** No engine flagged `DeckyHub-v3.4.10-rc.3.zip` (0/64) — [VirusTotal report](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/4b202b651f2a9bc887a2aca0316243b855b3c4d6949da0d3626fbe04f5436257).
- **MetaDefender:** No engine flagged `DeckyHub-v3.4.10-rc.3.zip` (0/21) — [MetaDefender report](https://metadefender.opswat.com/results/file/bzI2MTEyN2k2elVud2tJUUQ0SnRrU1RZWk81_mdaas/regular/overview).
- **Desktop installer (`install-deckyhub.sh` and its `.desktop` launcher):** ClamAV: No threats found ([scan report](https://github.com/mazillka/deckyhub-plugin/releases/download/v3.4.10-rc.3/ClamAV-desktop-v3.4.10-rc.3.txt)). VirusTotal: clean (0/60) — [report](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/6430ac05dfbae85e11a7046e1791d81fe87772734cabb12526128da4197f0a53). MetaDefender: clean (0/21) — [report](https://metadefender.opswat.com/results/file/bzI2MTEyN3kzcGY2dnRqUVdpZGRuek1GTF9wUTk_mdaas/regular/overview).
- **Code analysis:** GitHub [CodeQL](https://github.com/mazillka/deckyhub-plugin/actions/workflows/codeql.yml) checks the Python and TypeScript code on every change.

## New

**Before you choose Pre-release:** at the time of this release it installs Decky Loader `v4.0.0-pre1`, whose [own notes](https://github.com/SteamDeckHomebrew/decky-loader/releases/tag/v4.0.0-pre1) say it supports new Steam betas only. DeckyHub hasn't been tried with Decky Loader 4.0. If there's no newer test version than the stable one, Decky's installer installs the stable one.

**To try the new installer,** download `Install-DeckyHub.desktop` from the files on this page. The download links in the README give the latest stable release, which doesn't have this…

mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.name: v3.4.9
mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.body:
## New

- **Navigation sound:** moving around DeckyHub, including its windows, plays Steam's navigation sound. Turn it off with **Sound when navigating** in Settings.
- **Animations:** sections in Quick Access and Settings rise in one after another, and the button the controller highlights bounces. They're off if your device asks for reduced motion.
- **Search YouTube:** a plugin's Manage window can search YouTube for the plugin. It is a plain search, so results may be unrelated.
- **Two settings** (Settings → General), both off to start with: hide the **Support Development** button, and hide **Remote Control** while remote access is off. To turn remote access on again, switch that hide setting off first.
- **DeckyHub says when the official plugin list isn't fresh.** If it comes from the saved copy, a line says so and shows when it was last updated. It also says when the list isn't available.

## Changed

- **Refresh downloads the plugin list again**, then checks for new releases.
- Updated the libraries Remote Install uses.
- The website, deckyhub.com, now has [its own repository](https://github.com/mazillka/deckyhub-site).

## Fixed

- **Vibration works again.** It didn't run on current Steam, which no longer has the function DeckyHub used to find the controller. Each move gives one pulse on the Steam Deck's built-in controller. The haptics switch turns it off.
- Switching Settings tabs with L1 / R1 no longer moves the tabs sideways.
- The **Support Development** button is no longer pushed against the top of its box.
- **Two downloads with the same file name no longer write to the same file** while both are queued or running, even with overwriting turned on.

## Under the hood

- More release, compatibility and website checks. The release size limit now fits the ZIP's real size.

## Try it on your device

- Move around DeckyHub and its windows one step at a time, then hold the D-pad: do you feel one pulse and hear one sound per move?
- Press L1 / R1 on Settings, and turn each new setting on and off.
- Open **Search YouTube** from a plugin's Manage window and come back.
- Go offline, restart DeckyHub and check that the saved-list line appears. Go online, press **Refresh** and check that it goes away.

## Security checks

mazillka/deckyhub-plugin.body:
3.4.7: smaller safety and support fixes from a full product audit.

## Fixed

- **A download link that tries to climb out of the plugin's releases is refused.** GitHub treats `%2e%2e` in a link as "go up one folder", and DeckyHub's check only looked for a plain `..`. Normal downloads are not affected.
- **A damaged settings file is kept, not thrown away.** If DeckyHub can't read `settings.json`, it now saves it beside the new one as `settings.json.bad` instead of overwriting it with defaults, so your GitHub token, custom registries and pinned versions can be recovered.
- **A refused Remote Install request leaves a line in the log.** Before, every failure just said "Request rejected" with nothing to go on. **Export Logs** now shows what went wrong (never a token or code).
- The Ukrainian guide now lists the **Rust** and **In Decky store** badges and names the **Paired devices** button as the page does.
